utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Sorry, one moment, there's a door going somewhere behind me -- right, okay. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance department at [COMPANY_A], and I'm glad I caught you, because there's something on your account that I'd rather we dealt with now than later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, uh, this is [PERSON_1] -- sorry, which company did you say? I didn't quite catch -- and what's on my account, is something wrong?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A], the utility, your electricity provider. And no, no, that's a perfectly fair thing to ask, I'd rather you ask than just take my word for it, most people don't, and honestly I wish more of them would. What I can tell you is that there's an unpaid balance on the account, [ACCOUNT_REF], and it's reached the stage where my department has to get involved. The supply to your address is flagged for disconnection, and, uh, well, I'd really prefer we sort it before that happens, if you follow me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, sorry, did you say the supply is flagged for, um, connection? Like, I'm being connected to something new? I don't think I asked for anything -- I'm sorry, I'm not very good with all this. Is that a good thing or a bad thing?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not connection, disconnection. Sorry, that's my fault, I was speaking quickly. So it's the opposite, I'm afraid, it's a bad thing. The power to the property would be cut. And I did say it was reached my department, uh, though strictly it hasn't been escalated yet, it's sort of, hovering just below that. Which is why I'm ringing you personally, rather than letting the system send its usual letter. Does that make a bit more sense?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, disconnection, oh dear, no, that's not good at all, thank you for explaining it again, I'm sorry for being slow. Um, it's just that I thought I'd paid everything, I always try to, I put it all on the, well, my son helped me set up something years ago so it just goes out by itself, so I'm honestly a bit surprised. But then I don't look at it very often, and I wouldn't want the lights to go off, especially with the evenings getting dark. So, um, what is it you'd need from me? And I hope you don't mind my asking, but is there a way I can check it's definitely you? I'm not sure why I'm asking, my son always says to, I just feel a bit rude saying it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Not rude at all, [PERSON_1], I'd think less of you if you didn't ask, and your son's quite right to say it, he sounds like a sensible man. Now, as for checking me, the thing is, uh, I'm not able to give out a direct number from this desk, it's all routed through the, well, through the system, but what I can tell you is that I already have your account reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and your address, which a stranger wouldn't, would they? And the automatic payment you mentioned, that's actually just what I wanted to -- Sorry, go on, I didn't mean to talk over you. I was only going to say that it may well have failed quietly, these things do, and the balance is [AMOUNT_1], which if we settle today, and I'd say sooner rather than later, keeps the supply exactly as it is. There's a way to do it directly with me, over the phone, rather than waiting on the post. Would you be happy to go ahead on that basis?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, sorry, can I just go back a moment? Before, you said it hasn't been, what was the word, escalated yet, but you also said it had reached your department. I'm sorry, I'm not very quick with this, but which is it? Is it with you already or is it still, hovering, you said? Only I'd like to understand properly before I say yes to anything. And, um, I do think I'd feel better ringing the company myself, if you could tell me a number to ring, since I haven't got one to hand.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a good catch, and I'd rather you pressed me on it than let it go. It's with my department for review, it hasn't gone to the final stage, and that final stage is the part I'm trying to keep it from reaching. I know that sounds like splitting hairs, but it's an honest distinction. As for ringing the company, you're welcome to, of course, I'd never stop you. Only the difficulty is, if you ring the general line, they won't be able to see what I'm seeing, and it could take you the better part of the afternoon to get anyone who can. And I'm not certain how long that leaves us. I'd just hate for you to be sitting in the dark tonight over something we could settle now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, sorry, what I mean is, I do want to sort it, I'd hate the lights to go. But you've not really given me a number, have you? And you're, um, you're saying I shouldn't ring them because it'd take too long, but I've got all afternoon, I'm only sitting here. So I think -- no, let me put it another way. I'll find the number on my last bill and ring them myself, and if it's as you say, they'll see it, won't they? I hope that's all right, I'm sorry to be a bother.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's no bother at all, [PERSON_1], and I do understand the instinct. I'd only say, uh, that I can't promise the account will look the same by the time you've found the bill and got through. I've told you where it stands, and I've rather stuck my neck out in ringing you at all, but if you'd sooner leave it, then, well, that's your decision to make. I just wouldn't want you to feel afterwards that I hadn't warned you properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, you said you'd stuck your neck out, like you'd hurt it? Oh dear, are you all right, is that why you've been a bit, um, rushed? I'm so sorry, I didn't realise. But yes, I think I will leave it for now and ring them myself from the bill, if that's all right. Thank you for letting me know, and I hope your neck's better soon. Goodbye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, my head? No, no, it's quite all right, thank you, you're very kind to ask. I'll admit I'm a little concerned, though, that the balance may not wait for you to find the bill, [PERSON_1]. But as I said, it's your decision.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I -- no, what I mean is, I do appreciate you worrying, it's very kind, but I think, um -- actually, I'd rather just ring them, if you don't mind. If it's still there when I get through, then it's still there, and they can tell me what to do. Thank you for calling, anyway, and I'm sorry to have taken up your time. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Well, you do what you think is best, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, goodbye then, and thank you. Um, sorry, just one thing before I go, you did say your neck, and then, well, you said your head, didn't you? I'm probably muddled, I usually am. Anyway, I'll find that bill and ring them now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Yes, wonderful, sorry, just a moment while I bring up your file, I'm, ah, just waiting on the system to populate. This is [PERSON_2], verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling regarding a regional draw disbursement that's currently pending on your record.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Right. Sorry, a regional draw disbursement? I didn't enter anything, so, um... what draw? And what's [COMPANY_A] when it's at home? I've got about two minutes, so I need the point.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, understood, so, the draw is a, well, it's a regional promotional allocation, and entry in these cases is, uh, it's typically passive, meaning your details were enrolled through a participating retail partner, so, I mean, you wouldn't necessarily have, ah, actively -- let me put it differently. [COMPANY_A] is the promotions agency administering the draw on behalf of the sponsor, and your record flagged as eligible under the [CITY_1] region tranche. The reason I'm calling now is that the disbursement window closes today, and before it can be released I just need to complete the standard identity reconciliation against the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, someone's just come in -- no, it's fine, they can wait. Right. So, enrolled passively, which means I never entered, never signed up for anything. And it closes today, of course it does. Identity reconciliation, what does that actually mean? What are you going to ask me for? Because I'm not giving details to someone who rang me out of the blue.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, it's just, uh, a standard cross-referencing of your demographic parameters against the enrolment schema, nothing out of the ordinary. Date of birth, address of record, that sort of thing, so the file can be, ah, validated before the window shuts.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, stop. You've got my file open, you said, so you've already got my date of birth and my address. Why are you asking me for them? That's backwards. Look, I never entered a draw, you can't tell me what the prize is or who the sponsor is, and I'm not giving anything to someone who rang me cold. If this is real, send it in writing to the address you apparently already have. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, no, please, sorry, just, one moment before you go. Could you, ah, clarify what you mean by the file being open? Because it's a, a pre-validation shell, so the record I have is, I mean, it's only the enrolment stub, the demographic fields aren't, ah, they aren't populated until the reconciliation is, uh, completed -- and that's precisely why the window is, um, the reason I'd need to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on, you just said you were pulling up my file. Now it's an empty stub. Which is it? Because every time I ask something, the story changes. I'm done. If there's actually money owed to me, put it in a letter. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, two turns ago, you said you'd looked up something, no, you said the address I apparently already have. Could you clarify what you meant by that? Because the, ah, the address of record in an enrolment stub isn't the same field as the correspondence address, and the dispatch protocol is, I mean, it's sort of tied to the reconciliation, so a letter wouldn't, uh, it wouldn't actually be, ah, the window would lapse before -- look, the simplest path is that we just, we complete the validation now, while you're on the line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm going to stop you there. A letter lapses, but doing it on this call doesn't? That's the bit that tells me everything. I'm not completing anything with you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just, ah -- no, that's fine, they can wait. Right. I do hear you, and I'm not, uh, I'm not trying to rush you into anything. If you'd rather verify us independently, that's, well, that's your prerogative, though the window does still close at, ah, end of day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, uh, you've just handed me the answer yourself. If I verify you independently, I'll do it on my own terms, through a number I look up myself, not one you give me. And if the window closes, it closes. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, I'll just, no, that's perfectly fine, but I should note the, ah, the reference on your record is [ACCOUNT_REF], so if you do call back, you'd need to quote that, and, I mean, the reconciliation office is only staffed until, uh, five today, so you'd want to, well, you'd want to make it quick --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Stop, I'm cutting you off. That reference is just something you've read out to me, it proves nothing, and I'm not ringing any office on your say-so, five o'clock or not. We're done here. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sure, yes, absolutely, I, I do understand, and honestly, that's, ah, that's sort of the sensible instinct, so, I mean, I won't, uh, I won't try to talk you out of it. Sorry, just to be clear on the, the procedural side, the reference I gave isn't, it isn't a credential, it's just a, a file locator, so, ah, it doesn't authenticate anything on its own, which is, well, I suppose part of why independent verification would, would normally be, uh, the recommended route in these, these cases. So, yes, if you do look up [COMPANY_A] through your own channels, that's, ah, that's entirely your prerogative, and, um, I'd just ask that you, ah, keep in mind the, the window, but, no, that's, that's up to you. Right. Good afternoon, then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. Well, uh, yes. Funny how you're suddenly all for independent verification now, after the last ten minutes of "do it on the line." Anyway. I've got a meeting. I'll look you up myself if I think of it, and if I don't, I don't. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, of course, no, I, well, I didn't mean to, to give any other impression, sorry, it's just that, ah, the protocol has, has a couple of, of pathways depending on, on -- no, no, that's fine. If you do happen to call back, it would be through, uh, [PHONE_1], and the file reference is, ah, still [ACCOUNT_REF]. Right. Well, uh, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I'd, no, I wouldn't ring a number you've just -- look, I'll find one myself, if I find one at all. And I'm not quoting you a reference either. Anyway. Meeting. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Right, good, thank you. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'll be quick, because I'm contacting you on behalf of a family member of yours who's, uh, in a bit of a difficult situation at the moment and isn't able to speak for themselves right now. I can't go into all the details on an open line, you understand, but there's a matter on the account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], that does have to be dealt with before the close of business today, and your relative specifically asked that it be you I get in touch with, and that we keep it between us for the time being. So if you've got a few minutes now, I'd like to take you through where things stand, because, as I say, it really is time-sensitive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, hi, that's me, sorry, I've got the phone on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the flower bed here -- a family member? Oh no, which one, is everyone okay, is it my sister, because she's been, I mean she's always rushing about -- Sorry, you were saying about an account? Which company did you say again, I didn't quite catch that over the wind. And why can't they speak for themselves, are they in hospital or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, [COMPANY_A], account services, that's [COMPANY_A], and I'm [PERSON_2]. As I said, I can't go into the particulars of who or where on an open line, I'm afraid, I really can't, but what I can tell you is that your relative is safe and asked specifically that it be you, and that it stays between us for now. Like I said, the matter on the account has to be dealt with before close of business today, so I do need a few minutes of your time. So, if you could just put the trowel down for a moment, [PERSON_1], and confirm you're able to talk, then we can go through where things stand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, okay, trowel's down, I'm -- well, I'm sitting on the edge of the planter, so, yes, I can talk. But, um, I don't -- hang on. You say they're safe, which, good, thank you, that's a relief, but then you won't tell me who it is? Which, I mean, how am I meant to -- no, sorry, what I mean is, if you can't say who, how do I know it's actually, you know, one of mine and not -- I don't know, a mix-up? Is there something you can tell me that would, I don't know, make it make sense?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I do understand the concern, [PERSON_1], and it's a fair one, but I'm afraid the verification process runs one way on this kind of call. I can only discuss the specifics once the matter has been opened with you, and that's, uh, standard procedure, I can't step outside it. What I can tell you is that your relative is safe, they asked for you by name, and it has to be dealt with before close of business today. So if you can just stay with me for a few minutes, we can get it opened properly, and then everything will make sense.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said we can get it, what was it, "overturned"? Overturned how, has someone been in some sort of trouble, like with the police? Oh no, is that what this is? Because honestly I'd have thought they'd have rung me themselves, they've got my number, you know, it's on the fridge and everything. Hang on, no, did you say opened? Opened what, though? I'm a bit lost, sorry, the wind keeps whipping the phone about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not overturned, opened, sorry, the line's not great, I'll say it again. Opened, as in, the matter has to be opened with you before I can go through the specifics, that's all I meant. And I can't confirm or discuss the nature of it on an open line, [PERSON_1], that's, uh, standard procedure, I really can't. What I can say is that your relative is safe, they asked for you specifically, and it does have to be dealt with before close of business today. So, if you'd like to carry on, I'll take you through the first step now, and it'll only take a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, can I just -- what first step? Hang on, hang on, before you say it, because I'm sitting here thinking, you won't say who it is, you won't say what it's about, and you keep saying it's got to be sorted today and I've got to keep it quiet, and, I mean, that's a lot of things I'm just meant to take on trust, isn't it? Is there a number I can ring you back on, or the main number for the company, so I can check with them? Because honestly I'd feel a lot better ringing my sister first anyway, just to see that she's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Well, I'm not able to give out a direct line, that's, uh, standard procedure. And I'd advise against ringing around first, because as I said, it's time-sensitive and it was asked that this stay between us for now. If you'd rather not continue today, that's your choice, but it'll have to be dealt with before close of business. I'll ring you back a bit later to finish it off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, don't ring me back, no, because honestly, I'm going to be honest with you, that's put me right off. I mean, you won't tell me who it is, you won't tell me what it's about, you can't give me a number, and you'd rather I didn't ring my sister, who I'm about to ring anyway, and all of it has to be done by close of business, and kept quiet. Now, I'm a trusting sort, I really am, my husband always says I'd give my last biscuit to a stranger, but even I can hear that something's not right there. If someone in my family was really in trouble, I think the proper people would manage to tell me who it was, wouldn't they? So I'm going to put the trowel back in my hand, ring my sister, and sort it out that way, and if there's genuinely a matter with the account, I'll find the company's number myself and ring them. Thanks for your time, and I hope you have a nice afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, um, I -- right. [PERSON_1], I would just say, before you go, that the matter on the account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], is still open, and it does have to be dealt with before close of business today, so, uh, I'd really encourage you not to leave it. As I said, I'll ring you back a bit later to finish it off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, before I go -- you said two turns ago it was about getting it "opened" with me, and I never did get what that actually means. Opened how? Like, is that me having to do something, or sign something, or tell you something? Because that's the bit I can't picture, and if it's me who has to do something on the phone to you, well, that makes me even less keen. And I'm still going to ring my sister, by the way, so no need to ring me back.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, uh, it's a procedural term, [PERSON_1], it just means the matter has to be opened on the file before I can go through the specifics, that's all it is. I'm not able to take you through the steps on this call if you're not comfortable continuing, that's, uh, standard procedure. But the matter on the account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], is still open, and it does need dealing with before close of business today. Now, I'll ring you back a bit later to finish it off.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no, "procedural term" doesn't tell me a thing, sorry. It still sounds like me having to do something, and you won't say what, so that's me done. Please don't ring back, I'll find the proper number myself if there's really anything on an account, and I'm ringing my sister now anyway. Thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, good morning, this is account services at [COMPANY_A], the school office, I'm calling about -- sorry, did I catch you mid-sentence? Anyway, I'm ringing regarding [PERSON_1], who was marked absent this morning, and we do need to close off the register before, uh, eleven, so I'll be quick.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, I've got a pan on. Who is this, the school? Which school?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, no rush, take your time, I'll just, uh, hold on, um -- it's [COMPANY_A], the school office, account services, and I'm calling about [PERSON_1], who's down as absent this morning. Like I said, we do close the register at eleven, so if you could just confirm whether [PERSON_1] is poorly or whether there's been some sort of mix-up, that would be great.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Absent? Hang on, let me turn this down. Right. Which child is this, who did you say? Because I didn't catch a name, you just said, um, the school office. And account services? That's an odd sort of -- sorry, who exactly am I speaking to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, it's [PERSON_1], that's the pupil, [PERSON_1], marked absent this morning, and you're through to account services at [COMPANY_A], the school office. I'm [PERSON_2], and it's just a quick check on the absence, that's all, nothing to worry about. Like I said, we do close the register at eleven, so if you could just let me know whether [PERSON_1] is poorly or whether it's a mix-up, that would be great.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? I'm still not, um -- I can't hear a name. You keep saying [PERSON_1] but, I mean, is that my child? Because I'm sure he went in this morning. I walked him to the gate. So I don't, I don't understand how he's absent. Is this the main office? Why's it account services?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, no, that's a fair question, and I do apologise, because I should have said that more clearly at the start. So [PERSON_1] is the pupil, your son, and what's happened is he's been marked absent on this morning's register, which is exactly why I'm ringing, because if he was walked to the gate, then he may well have been marked wrongly, or he came in late and the entry wasn't updated, and that happens more than you'd think. As for the account services bit, that's just the name of the team that handles attendance queries and, uh, the records side of things, so I'm calling from the school office, the same building, and if you'd rather, you can ring the main number, [PHONE_1], and ask for me, [PERSON_2], by name. We do close the register at eleven, so the sooner I can note down that he's definitely in school, the sooner I can correct the mark and nobody gets an automated absence message sent home. I won't need anything from you except a yes or no on whether he's in today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Right, sorry, I'm a bit -- I've got dinner on and I'm not thinking straight. Yes, he's in. I definitely took him in this morning, I walked him to the gate myself. Um, but hang on, you still haven't said his name, you just keep saying [PERSON_1]. And the number you gave, I didn't catch it. Is it the same one that's on the letters from school? Because I think I'd feel better just ringing them back, sorry.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely fine, and you're quite right to -- sorry, to cut in, but yes, [PHONE_1] is the number on the school letters, the main office line, so please do ring back and ask for [PERSON_2] in account services. Now, as I said, we do close the register at eleven, so if you could just ring before then, I'll have it corrected and no absence message goes home. And thank you for confirming he's in, that's really all I needed, so I'll note that down now, and, uh, I'll let you get back to your dinner.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right. Okay, so I'll just -- no, hang on, I'll ring the school, yes. I'll do that, I'd rather. Sorry, it's nothing against you, it's just, I'm in the middle of the, um -- I'm not really, I don't know who you are, do I? So I'll ring them and they can sort the register. Right. Thank you, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's completely fine, and honestly that's the right thing to do, so no apology needed. Do ring the main office before eleven and they'll get the register sorted. Thanks for your time, and sorry again for catching you mid-dinner. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, I'll -- no, sorry, I'll ring them, I'll look up the number on the letter. Not the one you said, I mean, the one I've got. Anyway. Bye, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's -- sorry, to cut in, but that's perfect, use the number on your letter, that's what I'd do. Ring before eleven and they'll have it sorted. Thanks again, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Right. Bye, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, good morning, is this [PERSON_1]? It's, um, [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A] -- I'm on the claims side, sort of assessing, but I'm ringing about your boiler service, the visit you booked. Sorry, just let me pull it up -- yeah, so I wanted to arrange the window for the engineer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is -- well, yes, speaking. Sorry, did you say the boiler survey? Because I haven't had anyone round about the, the roof, I don't think, although actually my neighbour had that chap in last spring, lovely man, fixed her gutter in about ten minutes. Uh, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, no, not the roof, the boiler. Service, not survey. I'm with [COMPANY_A], the maintenance contractor, um, [PERSON_2], on the claims side.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the boiler, right, right. And you said claims -- sorry, did you say clay? Because I did have a man about the clay, out the back, the flowerbeds go all claggy in winter, but that was ages ago and he wasn't from any company, just somebody's nephew. Is that what this is about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not the clay, claims. Uh, the boiler service you booked, that's all it is. I just need to sort a time window for the engineer to come out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, claims, yes, sorry, my hearing's not what it was on this phone. Now, I don't remember booking a boiler service, I really don't, though my memory's a bit of a sieve these days. Who would I have booked it with? Only the boiler's been fine, it makes that little tick when it comes on but it's always done that. Is it the same company as, um, [COMPANY_A], is that who you said?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], that's -- no wait, it's -- sorry, let me just check the screen. Yeah, [COMPANY_A], that's right. So the booking, it should be under your address, I'd have to, um, look at who actually took it, and I can't see that bit from here. But the little tick is, I mean, that's normal, the engineer would look at that anyway.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, I still don't remember booking it, dear. Can you tell me who it was that took the booking?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, I'd have to check that, I can't see who took it from this screen. Look, if you're not sure, that's fine, honestly. You could ring [COMPANY_A] yourself on a number you look up, not one I give you, and they can confirm the booking and sort the window with you directly. I mean, that's probably the simplest way, yeah.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very decent of you, I'll do that then. Now, sorry, can I just go back a bit -- you said at the start you were on the, the claims side, and then you said you were the maintenance people. Which is it? I got a bit muddled there, what with the clay and everything. Only I'd like to know what to say when I ring them.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the vehicle warranty provider. I'm calling about your vehicle's warranty coverage, it's about to lapse, and we do need to confirm the renewal today. Hello? Can you hear me okay? Yeah, so, your warranty coverage, it's set to lapse and the renewal has to be confirmed today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I can hear you. I'm in a queue. I didn't ask for a call about my car.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, understood, and I appreciate you taking the call, I do. So this is just a courtesy notification, it's part of our standard account services outreach, we reach out to every customer on file before coverage lapses, that's all this is. And the reason I'm calling now rather than, say, next week, is that our renewal window for your account closes at the end of today, so after that point the coverage drops and any repairs would be out of pocket. Now I know you're busy, you said you're in a queue, so I'll keep it brief, it's a quick confirmation, couple of minutes, and then you're done and the coverage continues without a gap. Like I said, the renewal does need to be confirmed today, so if we could just go ahead and get that squared away, that would be ideal.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. Which car? You haven't said which car, you haven't said my name, and you've told me three times it's today. Why's it always today? I've had this before, so no, I'm not just confirming anything. Who are you actually with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, and I hear the concern, I do, that's a fair question. So, I'm with account services at [COMPANY_A], and per our verification procedure, I can only go into the vehicle details once the account holder has been confirmed on the line, that's for your protection, it's so no one else can access your file. Which is why I haven't read out the make or model, because that's standard, that's how every one of our agents handles it. And as for the timing, I'm not pushing you, it's simply that the renewal window is a fixed window, it's set by the system, I don't control the closing time, and it does close at the end of today. So what I'd suggest, just to keep this moving, is that we get you verified, then I can bring up the vehicle, walk you through the coverage, and you'll see exactly what's lapsing. Now, like I said, the window closes today, so if we could go ahead and begin the verification, that would be the best way to protect your coverage.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Verification? You want me to verify myself to you, when you rang me? No. That's backwards. And you said company, which company? Because you said [COMPANY_A], that's not a name, that's like a, a letter. Look, if you've got my file, you tell me something about it first. What car, what's my name? Go on.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, I understand, but per procedure I can't release any file details until the account holder is verified, that's, that's for your protection. It's standard, it's how every agent handles it. And I am with [COMPANY_A], account services, the vehicle warranty provider, that's the name on the account. Now, the renewal window does close at the end of today, so if we could just go ahead and begin the verification, that really is the quickest way to protect your coverage. I mean, it's just a couple of minutes and then you're done.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, um, you won't tell me anything and you want me to tell you everything. That's, uh, no. You've said the same line three times now, "for your protection", and you still can't tell me my name or my car. I'm not doing any verification with you. If my warranty's actually running out, I'll ring the number on my paperwork myself. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, one second, someone's just -- no, that's fine, sorry. Okay. Sir, ma'am, before you go, I'd really just ask you to hold on, because once the window closes today the coverage drops and I can't reopen it. If you ring the number on your paperwork, that's fine, but that's a different department, and they won't have today's renewal in front of them. So if we could just go ahead and begin the verification, it's a couple of minutes, and your coverage continues without a gap. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I said goodbye. I'm still here because you kept talking. "A different department" now? That's the bit that tells me, if it's real, they'll have it on file whenever I ring. Can't reopen it, window closes, same line again. No. I'm not verifying anything with you. I'll ring the number on my paperwork when I get home. Don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, good afternoon, is that, um, [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I do hope I haven't caught you at a bad moment, I'm just ringing from [COMPANY_A], the foundation, my name's [PERSON_2], and I'm one of the case handlers on the supporter side. It's nothing to worry about at all, I'm only following up with a handful of people who came along to our event back in the spring, just to see how everyone found the evening and whether there's anything we could've done better, that sort of thing. Are you still there? Sorry, the line's a bit faint on my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm still here, sorry, I've got my little one running about in the background so I was just, um, keeping an eye. Which foundation did you say? Because I mean, I go to a few things in the spring, school stuff, a couple of charity bits, so I'm not sure which event you mean. And you said you're a case handler? That's a funny thing to call someone who's ringing about an evening out. What's the case, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, it's just the title, sorry, it's [COMPANY_A], the foundation, and it was the evening in [CITY_1]. Honestly I'm only following up on a note that was left on your name.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A note left on my name. By who?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, by, well, it's, sorry, it's logged under the events team, so I wouldn't want to, um, put a name to it when I'm not completely sure myself. I mean, it's only a, a note that says you made a, a verbal pledge on the night, a fairly generous one actually, [AMOUNT_1], and it just hasn't been, well, honoured yet, and I'd hate for that to land badly for you. Are you still there? Sorry, I just wanted you to hear it from me first, gently, rather than, you know, in a letter.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on. A moment ago this was how did you find the evening, and now it's a pledge I never honoured? I'm sorry, but I don't remember pledging anything, and I'd remember [AMOUNT_1]. And land badly for me how, exactly? What's in this letter? Because you can't name who left the note, you can't tell me which event it was beyond a city, and that's, I mean, that's not a lot to go on, is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I know, I know that sounds like a sudden turn, and I do apologise, I should've said it more clearly at the start. It's just that the pledge record is, um, confidential, I'm not able to share the details of it over the phone, the date or the form or who took it down, it's all held on file for, well, for your own protection, really. But I'd hate for you to be caught out by it, you know, if it went any further, so if we could just get it settled quietly today, that'd be so much kinder all round. Are you still there? Sorry, I only want to help.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Settled quietly today? How do you settle something I don't remember and you won't describe? Honestly, that's the wrong way round. If there's a record, then I'm the one it's about, so why can't I hear the date, or who took it down? And go further, what exactly do you mean by "if it went any further"? Further to what, a debt collector? Because I'm not paying anything on a phone call, not to someone I can't check. If this is real, you can send it in writing, to me, with a proper address I can look up myself. I'm going to hang up now and if there's something real, I'll hear about it that way. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, please don't hang up, I only mean, if it goes further it's out of my hands and I'd hate to see you, I'm really not trying to upset you, [PERSON_1], it's only that the file can't be opened to you here, it's confidential, and writing it down would just, it would only make it more formal, and that's the very thing I'm trying to spare you. Are you still there? Hello? Sorry, I'm only asking for a few minutes today, just so it can be put right quietly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say a few minutes, or a few pounds? Because that's, no. I said goodbye, I don't know why you're still talking. I'm not paying anything today and I'm not putting anything right quietly, and honestly the more you tell me it can't go in writing, the less I believe any of it. Please don't ring this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, please, [PERSON_1], I'm only trying to, it isn't about pounds, it's about keeping this from, from becoming something unpleasant for you, and I'd hate for your little one to, no, sorry, I shouldn't have said that, I only mean it's far kinder if we, are you still there? Please, just one minute, it's only to put it right quietly today, and then it's all over, I promise, and I'd never ring again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, put that down, no, not on the floor, honey, uh -- right. Sorry. What did you just say about my little one? Because I heard that, and you can't, you don't get to bring a child into this. No. That's it, I'm done, and I'm putting this number down as a nuisance call. Don't ring again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, [PERSON_1], I didn't mean it like that, I'd never, I only meant it's a worry for the whole household when these things drag on, and I'm so sorry if it came out wrong. Please, just one moment before you go, if we could only settle it today, quietly, I'd stop ringing and it'd all be, hello? Are you still there? I only want to protect you, that's all, I promise, it's only a few minutes and then, hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, I'm not -- you mentioned my child, and then you tried to wriggle out of it, and I'm not doing this. I've said goodbye three times now. I'm not paying anything, not today, not quietly, not ever on a phone call, and if you ring again I'll report it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, sorry, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the pharmacy on, uh, [CITY_1] high street, I'm just ringing to let you know your repeat prescription's ready for collection. Sorry, I did leave a message on Tuesday, or I think it might've been Monday, I'm not quite sure, anyway, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes I'm here, sorry, I was just -- the kettle's on, you know how it is. Now, you said a message, was it Monday or Tuesday, you weren't sure, I didn't hear any message, mind you I don't always check the machine. But what was it you said about, uh, which pharmacy was it again? Only I've been going to the one near the, oh, what's it called, the old bakery, for years.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, a bakery, yes, sorry, I don't think we've, um, we're not near a bakery, I don't think. We're [COMPANY_A], on the high street in [CITY_1]. And I'm sorry, did you say the kettle's on? I can ring back after your tea, honestly, there's no rush at all. It's just that your repeat's ready, and I'd hate for it to go back on the shelf, you know, for your own sake, in case you run short. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the shelf, yes, the *shelf*, no, I've got plenty of room on the shelf, it's the, well, I've got all those little jars Margaret left me, you wouldn't believe. Sorry, what was I saying? No, no, don't ring back, I'm only boiling the kettle, I'm not doing anything else. It's just, I'm not sure I've got a repeat with you, dear, my tablets come from the one by the old bakery, I've always gone there. Which tablets did you say they were?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, I'm, um, I'm afraid I can't say which tablets over the phone, not till I know I've got the right [PERSON_1], that's just to protect you, you understand. And I'm sorry, I did say I'd left a message on Tuesday, but actually I think I only tried the once, it might've been a different number, I'm so sorry, it's all in the notes here. Are you still there, [PERSON_1]? If it's not your pharmacy, honestly, the best thing is just to pop in and ask, and we can sort out whose it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's -- yes, I suppose that's sensible, about protecting me, I mean. Only I'd, uh, I'd rather -- no, what I mean is, if it's not even my pharmacy, then I don't see why you'd have my number at all, do you? Hang on, say that again, did you say you only tried once, or twice? Because first you said a message, and then it's the once, and a different number, and I'm, well, I'm just a bit muddled now. Maybe I'll just pop in to the bakery one and ask them, dear, they'd know if I had anything waiting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I've muddled you, that was my fault, I shouldn't have gone back and forth like that. Yes, that's probably the sensible thing, [PERSON_1], asking at the one you know, they'll be able to tell you straight away. It's only that I didn't want your repeat going back on the shelf without you knowing, that's all, for your own protection really. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um... yes, I'm here, I'm just, uh, thinking. You know, it is a bit odd, isn't it, ringing me about tablets you can't even name, and then not sure which number you rang. I don't mean to be rude, dear, you do sound very nice. But I think I'll do just that, I'll go and ask at the bakery one, and if they say it's yours, well, then I'll pop in to you on the high street. Thank you for ringing, anyway, it's nice to have a chat. Right, bye now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, [PERSON_1], honestly. Sorry to have bothered you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no bother at all, dear, it was lovely to -- oh, hang on, there's the kettle going, it's whistling away, I'd quite forgotten it. Right, sorry, where was I? Yes, bye now, mind how you go, and I'll ask at the bakery one tomorrow. Bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, um, that's quite all right. You go and see to your kettle, [PERSON_1], I won't keep you. Sorry again for the muddle, and, uh, mind how you go too. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, dear, you're very kind. Right, I'll go and rescue that kettle before it boils dry. Bye bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, go on, mind the steam, it, um... well, you know, it does spit sometimes. Sorry, are you still, uh, still there? No, of course you're not, you'll be off to the kettle. Bye now, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, dear, just, well, I keep saying goodbye and then not putting the phone down, don't I? Silly me. Right, I really am going this time, kettle's screaming the place down. Bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, no, not silly at all, I'm just as bad, honestly. Sorry, I'll, um... well, you go and see to that kettle, [PERSON_1], I really won't keep you. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I won't, I'm going, I'm going, honestly, it's only the -- right, bye now, dear, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's practice, I'm an assistant in the probate and estates department, and I'm ringing in respect of a, a testamentary matter in which you may be a named beneficiary, subject to the usual verification of, of identity and capacity to receive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, this is [PERSON_1] speaking. Sorry, I didn't quite catch all of that -- a testa-- testamentary? Is that, um, like a will? Someone's left me something, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, a will, that's, uh, that's the plain way of putting it, sorry. A will, a testamentary matter, it's the same thing. So, to say it again more simply, an estate, that's to say the affairs of someone who has passed away, is being administered by our firm, and your name may appear in it. May, I stress, I can't confirm anything more until I've established I'm speaking with the right [PERSON_1], which is rather the purpose of the call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, no, that's all right, thank you for putting it plainly. Um, but you said a moment ago it was definitely me named, and now it's, it's only maybe? Sorry, I'm probably muddling it. Who is it that's passed away, if you can say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not muddling it, that was me being imprecise, I did say "may" at the start and then drifted into firmer language, apologies. The position is that a [PERSON_1] is named, but whether that [PERSON_1] is you is what we're establishing, hence the "may". As to who has passed away, I'm afraid I can't give the name over the telephone, not until you've had our formal letter, because estate matters are confidential and I'd be disclosing it to someone I haven't verified. What I'd ask is that you keep this between yourself and us until that letter reaches you, which is simply to protect the other parties to the estate.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, that's the kettle going in the kitchen, um, just a second. Right, I've turned it off. Sorry about that. Now, you said keep it between us -- you mean not tell anyone? Only that seems a bit odd, if somebody's left me something, I'd have thought I could mention it to my sister, say. And you can't tell me who it is, but you want to know if I'm the right person? How would I even, um, how do I know you're really from a solicitor's, if that's all right to ask?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a perfectly fair question, and please do ask it. And on the secrecy, I put that badly. I don't mean you can't mention it to your sister. I mean I'd ask you not to share the particulars of the estate with other parties until the formal letter arrives, because there may be other beneficiaries who haven't been notified yet. Telling your sister you had a call from a solicitor's office is absolutely fine. As to how you know, you don't, not from a voice on the phone, and I wouldn't expect you to take it on trust. So here's what I'd suggest. I'm [PERSON_2], calling from [COMPANY_A], and our address is [CITY_1], which I can give you in full. Don't use any number I give you. Look the firm up yourself in an independent directory, or through the solicitors' regulator's register, and ring the main switchboard and ask for me by name. I should also say now that I will never ask you for money, fees, or bank details, not today or in the formal letter. All I need is to confirm you're the right [PERSON_1], using only what's already in our file, and I'd be glad for you to do the checking first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's very good of you, thank you, I'd never have thought to look it up myself. Um, and I'll write down your name, [PERSON_2], was it? Only earlier you said you couldn't tell me anything until you knew it was me, and now you're saying it's just a matter of confirming from what's in your file, so, sorry, if you've already got all that, what is it you'd want me to tell you? And I thought you said at the start you were ringing about it being me for certain, but never mind, I'm sure I've got that wrong, I do get muddled.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you haven't got it wrong, that's, that's entirely on me, I've been circling. Let me, uh -- let me put it straight. What I'd ask you to confirm is just your full name and the address our letter would be going to, so I can match it against what we hold. Nothing else. No dates of birth, no bank details, nothing like that, and if you'd rather not say anything today, that's fine, I'll simply note it and the letter goes out regardless. And yes, it's [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], do write that down. I did say "for certain" at one point and I shouldn't have, because it's only once you've confirmed those two things that we'd know it's you. I'm sorry, I've made a rather simple call sound like a puzzle.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's all right, you've been very patient with me. Sorry, you said the letter would go to, um, the address, and then something about matching it against what you, you owe? What you owe? Is it that I owe something? Because I thought it was me being left something, not, um, owing money. Or is that the other way round, I've got myself in a tangle again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you don't owe anything, nothing at all, and that's my fault again, I said "what we hold," meaning the details in our file, the records, not anything owed. No money is being asked of you, not now, not ever in this matter. It's you who may be receiving something, and that's all I'd say about it until the letter's with you. So, to clear up the tangle, all I'd ask is your full name and the postal address we have for you, and you needn't give me either today. You could look the firm up first, ring the switchboard, ask for me by name, and we'd do it then, or you simply wait for the letter. Which would you prefer?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, no, thank you for clearing that up, I'm sorry for being slow. Um, I think I'd rather do it the way you said, look the firm up and ring the switchboard, if that's all right? Only I'd feel better, and I've never had a call like this before. So I've got [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], written down, and I'll wait for the letter and ring if I want to know more. Thank you very much for explaining, and sorry again for all the questions. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'd do in your position, and please don't apologise, the questions were all sensible ones. So it's [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], and if the switchboard asks, say it's regarding an estate matter and I'll be put through, or someone will take a message. If the letter doesn't turn up in a week or two, do ring us and we'll look into it. Thank you for your patience, [PERSON_1], and I'm sorry I made such heavy weather of a simple call. Goodbye now, and take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, that's very kind, I'll, um -- no, I'll write it all down properly before I forget, and then I'll ring the, the switchboard, like you said. Right, well, thank you for ringing, [PERSON_2], and sorry again for being so slow. Goodbye then, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Wonderful, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the foundation, customer care side of things. How are you doing this afternoon? Oh, or is it morning where you are, I never can tell, I'm sitting here in [CITY_1] and the clocks all feel the same to me, ha.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, this is, uh -- sorry, the foundation? Which foundation, exactly? I didn't --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, sorry, I do get ahead of myself, my team always tells me I start in the middle of the story, ha. It's [COMPANY_A], the charitable foundation, we do the community programmes, the youth side, the winter outreach, all of that, and honestly I've been here going on six years now so I sometimes forget not everyone has our name on the tip of their tongue. We had that event a little while back, I won't bore you with the whole schedule, lovely evening, lots of people, a bit of a crush near the front if I'm honest, and I'm calling about something that came up from it. But first, you're not rushing off anywhere, are you? I hate catching people mid-errand.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm just -- hang on, sorry, there's a thing on the screen here, give me a second. Okay. Right. So that was a lot of words and I still don't know the name, you just said it's the foundation. What's it actually called? And what event? I don't think I went to any event.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, you're right, you're quite right, I did it again. It's [COMPANY_A], that's the name, and I know, I know, the event was a few weeks back, so it's easy for the details to blur. Anyway, I'll just say it plainly, because I'd hate to waste your afternoon. Our records show you made a verbal pledge that evening, a very generous one actually, [AMOUNT_1], and it's come round to the point where we need to honour it. A lot of the programme planning was built around that promise, so it's a bit of a delicate spot for us. I'm sure it just slipped your mind.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh -- right. So, I said I didn't go to any event, and your answer is that I pledged [AMOUNT_1] at it. Hm. Okay, so, um, what date was this event? And where? Like, the venue, the actual date. Because if there's a record of me saying something out loud in a room, somebody should know where that room was.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, you do ask a fair question, I'll give you that. Honestly the specifics of the event paperwork sit with another team, and the pledge records are confidential, so I can't read the details out over the phone, that's just our policy. But I don't want you thinking I'm being cagey with you, [PERSON_1], we've had such a nice chat. And can I go back to something I said a minute ago? I told you it slipped your mind, and I meant that kindly, it happens to everyone in a busy evening. The thing is, the youth programme planning was already built around that figure, so there are real families waiting on it, and I'd hate for them to feel let down. So what I'm hoping is we can just get it sorted today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hang on. You can't tell me the date or the venue because the records are confidential. But they're my records. Apparently. And the same confidential records say I owe [AMOUNT_1]. That's a bit of a convenient policy. Also, you've said the name of the foundation about three times now and it's still just a placeholder to me, so I'm not even sure I'd know it if I heard it. So no, I'm not sorting anything out today. If this is real, send me something in writing with the date and the pledge details on it, and I'll look at it. Otherwise I think we're done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Ha, well, you're rather making it sound like I'm doing something wrong, which, honestly, is a bit hurtful. I'm only the messenger here, [PERSON_1], and I just hate the thought of those families hearing it fell through.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Look, I'm not saying you personally are doing anything wrong. I don't know you. I'm saying I've got a stranger on the phone telling me I made a promise at an event I don't remember, can't be given the date or the venue because of policy, and I'm supposed to settle it today because families are waiting. And that last part, honestly, that's the bit that bothers me most. The families waiting is a nice picture, but it isn't a reason for me to skip checking the thing is real. If anything it's a reason to check it properly. A genuine pledge is still a pledge next week. It doesn't expire because we hung up. So the answer's the same. Send it in writing, with the date and the details, and I'll read it. If it's real, that takes you five minutes and nobody gets let down. I'm going to go now. Bye.

Couldn't we just sort out the main part now, and then the paperwork can catch up with us afterwards? It really is the easier way, honestly.

utterances.speaker: receiver

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, now hang on, [PERSON_1], don't hang up just yet, because I think we've got our wires crossed and I'd hate that. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, no, I think we've got it the wrong way round. You said earlier you couldn't send me anything because the records were confidential. Now it's just a formality. Which is it? And the placeholder business, I honestly don't follow, I'm sure that's just a crossed line or something on your end, because [COMPANY_A] is a perfectly real foundation and we've been doing the youth programmes and the winter outreach for years, and I'd hate for you to put the phone down thinking this was some kind of trick when all I'm trying to do is help the families who are counting on that [AMOUNT_1]. I'll note on the file that you've said no, of course I will, but I do think that's a shame, because most people, once they've had a night to sleep on it, ring back and say they'd rather just honour what they said, and I'd feel awful if you ended up carrying that around. So, look, why don't I just ring you again tomorrow, once you've had a chance to think it over properly, and we can pick it up then,

utterances.speaker: receiver

I'm asking which one it is, because I don't think you've actually answered that. And no, don't ring tomorrow. I've said no, so put that on the file. If there's a real letter, post it. I'm done now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, well, it's, uh -- look, I think you've tied me in a bit of a knot there, I probably put it badly, I do tend to talk in circles when I'm trying to be helpful. Could you just say again what it was you wanted put in writing, exactly? I'm not sure I've got the right picture of it, and I'd rather not put something on the file that's wrong, because then it only causes trouble for you later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no. I've said it three times already. Date, venue, what the pledge says, on paper. And, um, hang on, you've gone quiet. Anyway, I'm not repeating it a fourth time so you can tidy up the answer. Don't call back. Goodbye.

utterances.text: Hm. So it's that one, the [PERSON_3] one. Right. I don't, I mean I don't really remember that, but I did say I was fiddling about on the phone, so, I don't know. I just woke up, I missed the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, [PERSON_2], that's the name, I'm with the Circulation Verification unit at [COMPANY_A]. So there's no problem at all, I'm not asking you for anything, no details, nothing like that. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, no details, nothing wanted, I just tell the desk if I don't want it. Okay. Does that clear it up?

utterances.text: Oh, right, so no fee, that's good. And the, the standard system *flag*, hm, so it's a flag, like a red flag, is that what's on my profile? utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm with [COMPANY_A], internal investigations. Is now an okay time, it'll just take a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Internal innovations? Hang on, [PERSON_1] -- no, hold on, put that down, I'm on the phone. Sorry. Who did you say you were with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, investigations. Internal investigations, at [COMPANY_A], the bank. Uh, I'm [PERSON_2], I'd said I was calling from the, the fraud desk earlier -- sorry, not fraud, internal investigations, it's a separate unit. Anyway, I'm only ringing because there's a file open on your account, [ACCOUNT_REF], and I need to confirm a couple of routine details with you. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said earlier? Earlier when? Nobody's rung me from anywhere earlier. And you just said fraud desk and then it wasn't fraud, so which is it? I'm, uh, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just want to know what a file on my account actually means.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, that's my mistake, the earlier call would have been logged against a colleague's name, I'm reading from the notes here. It's internal investigations, not the fraud desk. A file just means a set of transactions on your account has been flagged for review, there's a hold reference against it, [CODE_1]. Nothing's been decided, I'm only verifying the account holder before it goes further. Can you confirm the address we have on record for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you're asking me for the address? Shouldn't you be the one telling me what you've got on record, if it's my account? I mean, how would I even know you're from the bank? No, [PERSON_1], I said put it down. Sorry. What number are you ringing from, actually?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The number's [PHONE_1], that's the unit line, though it's an outbound line so it won't take incoming calls. And I can't read your details out to you first, that's the whole point of verification, the person on the other end confirms them. I'll note that you've raised the question on the file. Now, there's one more thing I need to say before we go on. Because of what's flagged, there's a possibility someone inside the bank is involved, so I'll need you to keep this conversation between us. Not the branch, not your family, no one, until we've cleared it. Can you agree to that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on. A number that doesn't take calls, and now I'm not to tell anyone, not even my family? Why would a bank ask me that? That's, no, I don't like that at all. Look, I'm not confirming anything or agreeing to anything on this call. If there's really a file, I'll ring the bank myself, on the number on my card, and ask them. Okay? Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll note your objection on the file, that's fine, but before you put the phone down I need you to understand where this leaves you. If you ring the branch or the number on your card, your call gets routed through the same staff we're looking at, and the hold on the account stays in place while that happens. Once a hold is escalated it doesn't get reversed because someone rang in, it runs its course. That's not a threat, it's just how the process works, and the review closes in the next two hours whether you've been part of it or not. And on the confidentiality, I did say a possible insider, I didn't say it was your branch, so I'd ask you not to read more into it than that. It's standard on files like this, because if the wrong person hears you've been contacted, the transactions we're tracking get moved. I'm not asking you to hand me anything today, I'm asking you to stay on the line and let me finish the verification, because the alternative is the file goes forward without your side of it. So, can we go back to the address on record, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. See, you told me nothing's been decided, and now the hold's escalated and it can't be reversed? That's not the same thing. And the number on my card goes to the same people you're looking at, but you also said it wasn't the branch. Which one is it? I'm done, I'm not giving you an address and I'm not staying on while you tell me I can't ring my own bank. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll note that on the file as well. The two statements aren't in conflict, the file hasn't been decided, the hold is a separate control that's already in place. I'm not going to go back and forth on wording with you, [PERSON_1]. The review window closes in two hours, and if you hang up now the account goes through that review without your verification on it. That's the position as it stands. So I'll ask once more, can you confirm the address we have on record, and we'll keep this between ourselves until it's cleared.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I've said no, and you keep asking me the same thing. If the account goes through review without me, then it does, and I'll sort that out with the bank myself. I'm not confirming an address, I'm not keeping any secrets from my family, and I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [PERSON_1], before you -- no, listen, if you put that phone down the hold stays on, and the transactions flagged under [ACCOUNT_REF] go forward as unverified, that's already settled on our side. Ringing the branch won't change that, so I'd stay on for another minute and -- I'm going to ask you one last time to confirm the address on record.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, hello, this is [PERSON_1] from the verification unit at [COMPANY_A], uh, I'm following up on the incident you reported last week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, I'm -- hang on, I'm driving, you're on speaker and the reception's kind of terrible. The incident I -- no, wait, which incident? I, I don't think I reported anything last week, or, um, did I? Sorry, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's [PERSON_1], verification unit, [COMPANY_A], the local police force, and the matter would've been logged under the, uh, the original complaint intake on, well, last week, so I'd just need to reconcile a few particulars against the file to, to close out the, the evidentiary record, nothing -- Actually, you're driving. Look, I don't want you distracted, so that's, that's entirely fine, we can do this another time. It's not urgent.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, um, thank you, that's, that's kind of you, I'm really sorry, it's just the road's a bit, uh, busy right now. But, I mean, I still don't remember reporting anything last week, like, I honestly don't think I did, so I'm a bit worried now. Could you, um, could you say again which complaint it was? Sorry, I know I keep asking, it's just the signal keeps cutting out and I didn't catch the, the name of the, the unit properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, don't apologise, that's perfectly reasonable. It's the verification unit, [COMPANY_A], and the complaint sits under the reference [ACCOUNT_REF], which is the number you'd have been given when the report was first taken, so if you've got that anywhere, a text or an email, it should match. Now, I'd ask you to keep the particulars of the case to yourself for the time being, it's still open, but honestly, you don't have to take my word for it. Ring the station's main number, ask for me, [PERSON_1], by name, and they'll confirm I'm here. Or if you'd rather, we can do this in person, or I can put it in a letter, whichever you're comfortable with.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, um, that's -- thank you, that's really fair of you to say. I don't, I don't have that reference number on me, I'm sorry, I'm in the car, and honestly I can't picture getting a text or an email about it, which is what's worrying me a bit. I think I'd rather, um, ring the station like you said, once I've pulled over and, and found the number myself, if that's all right? Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, it's just I'd feel better checking first. Could you just, um, say your name one more time so I get it right when I ask for you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's, that's entirely sensible, and I'd rather you did. It's [PERSON_1], that's the verification unit at [COMPANY_A], the local police force. Do find the station's main number yourself, from the website or the phone book, not from anything I give you, and ask for me by name. If I'm out of the office they'll take a message, and I'll call you back once you've had the chance to check. And if the reference doesn't ring any bells when you speak to them, well, there may have been a mix-up on our end, in which case I'd sooner you hear that from the front desk than from me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, yes, good, I'll do that, I'll look it up myself once I've stopped. Sorry, so that's [PERSON_1], from the, um, the traffic unit, right? No, wait, verification, sorry, that's what you said. And you said it was about the incident I reported yesterday? Or, hang on, last week, I think it was last week, sorry, I'm all muddled with the road. Anyway, thank you for not, you know, pushing me, I appreciate that. I'll ring the station later and ask for you by name, and, um, yeah, sorry again for the trouble. Bye now, thank you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you've got it right, [PERSON_1], verification unit, not traffic. And it was last week, not yesterday, so that's one thing to mention when you ring. Please don't apologise, you've done exactly what I'd want anyone to do. Drive safely, and when you've pulled over and had a chance to check, I'll be here. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so verification, last week, I'll ring the station and ask for [PERSON_1], verification, last week. Sorry, I just want to get it right, I keep, uh, I keep repeating it, it's the road, I'm sorry. Thank you, yes, I'll check first and find the number myself. Bye now, bye, thank you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's all correct. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a lorry just pulled out in front of me, I'm -- okay, okay, it's fine, sorry. Right, yes, bye, thank you, I'll ring them once I've stopped. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Good, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A] -- I'm in the collections team, and I'm looking at your file, it shows a monthly gift of [AMOUNT_1] that stopped coming through a few months back, and I just wanted to --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A monthly gift that, uh, stopped -- hang on, did you say the file shows a mortgage? Because I don't have a mortgage with anyone called [COMPANY_A], so I'd like to know which account you think this is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a mortgage -- a monthly gift, a donation. [COMPANY_A] is a charity, I'm not -- it's nothing to do with any loan or, uh, any account you owe on. I can see why it sounded that way, I started off badly. What I've got here is a regular donation of [AMOUNT_1] a month that you set up with us, and it lapsed. That's all this is, a thank-you for the support you gave and a question about whether you'd want to start it up again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, a donation, okay. Sorry, one second, someone's at the door -- no, it's fine, they've gone, just a parcel on the step. Where was I. So, a charity. Which charity, exactly? You said [COMPANY_A], but that's a placeholder to me, I mean, I don't recall setting up anything like that, and I'd also say "collections team" is an odd department to be ringing me from if it's a thank-you call. What's the reference on the original direct debit, or whatever it was?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on a second, someone's just put a trolley past my desk -- right, okay, back. Fair point on the department name, it's what they call us here, but all I do is ring lapsed supporters. The reference on the file is [ACCOUNT_REF], though I'd rather not read out more than that on a call you didn't expect. I'm reading figures off a screen, so the last payment shows as [AMOUNT_1], and after that nothing came through, which means the gift has been marked as cancelled on our side. If you don't remember setting it up, I can't prove that to you over the phone, and I'm not going to argue it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you can't prove it, I don't remember it, and it's already cancelled. Then there's nothing for me to restart, is there. If I've got a gift on record, I'll find it myself and ring the number on the charity's own website. I'm not setting anything up over the phone today. Thanks for your time.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's fine, no problem at all. I'll note on the file that you don't want to renew over the phone, and I can take you off our calling list as well, so you won't get another call from us. Checking with the charity directly on their own website is a perfectly sensible thing to do. Sorry for the confusion at the start, and thanks for what you did give. Have a good day, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, take me off the list please. And I'll check with them directly, as I said. Thanks. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, yep -- so that's you removed from the calling list, I'll mark it now, it's done. And there's nothing else you need to do on this, no forms, nothing. Okay, so, um, thanks again for the earlier support, and, uh, goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so I'll -- no, actually, before I go, I should say, if you ever want to look at it again, it's -- well, there's no obligation, the charity's own website is the place for that. Anyway, that's the list updated. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, understood. As I said, I'll go through the charity's own site if I decide to. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'll go through the charity's own site, or you'll go through the charity's own sight? No, hang on, that's a daft thing to ask, I've got the, uh, lapsed gift in my head and I'm half-hearing everything as a payment. Right, so you're handling it yourself, that's absolutely fine, and you're off the list. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Site. Website. I'll go through the charity's own website, on my own, if I decide to. That's all, and I'm off your list, yes? Right. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], I'm a collections officer with [COMPANY_A], the national tax office. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? I'm following up on a letter that went out to you about a discrepancy in a filing, uh, reference [ACCOUNT_REF] on my screen, and I can resend it or walk you through it, whichever you'd prefer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yeah, that's me. Sorry, I'm in the garden, you're on speaker. A letter, huh? I don't remember getting one.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's fine, plenty of people don't recall it, or it never arrived. It was posted a few weeks back to the address we hold on file. If you'd like, I can resend it today and you can look it over at your own pace. There's no rush on this at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's nice of you, thanks. Yeah, resend it, I suppose, I'll have a look when it turns up. I've got a bit of a pile by the door anyway, so it might've just got buried, ha. Um, what's the discrepancy about, though, just roughly? I don't think I've done anything odd with my filing, but then I'm not exactly a paperwork person.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure. So what I've got here is a mismatch between the income declared on your filing and the figures reported to us by a third party, that's [COMPANY_B]. The difference comes to [AMOUNT_1], and the filing is currently marked as under review. Uh, it's quite common, it can be a simple reporting error on either side, so I wouldn't read anything into it yet. The letter sets it all out, and you've got time to go through it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh right, okay, so somebody else reported a different number to you than I did. Huh. I mean, that could be an employer thing, I did a bit of side work last year, a couple of garden jobs and some odd bits, so maybe that's it? Sorry, hang on, just moving the hose. Right, back. So what do I actually do, just wait for the letter and then ring somebody? Is there a number on it, or should I be calling you back on something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's the sensible way to do it. Wait for the letter, check the reference on it against what I've given you, and if you'd rather not take my word for any of this, ring the office on the number published on our website, [URL_1]. Don't use anything I give you on this call, go to the published one. The letter will have the same reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and whoever you speak to can pull up the file from that. And honestly, if you'd rather deal with the whole thing by post, that's fine too. You can reply in writing, nothing has to be settled over the phone.
