Side work could well explain it, by the way, but I can't tell from here which of those figures it would be, so I wouldn't guess either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's really helpful, thanks. I like that, you're not hassling me for anything, you're just telling me to check it myself. Okay, so wait for the letter, look up the number on the actual website, not the one you give me, and ring that. Or just write back, which, honestly, suits me fine, I'm a bit hopeless on the phone with official stuff. Right, I'll do that. Thanks for ringing, and sorry about the background noise, ha. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, no trouble at all. Just, uh, just to say it once more, check the reference on the letter against the one I gave you, [ACCOUNT_REF], and use the number on the website, not one from me. And replying by post is perfectly all right, you don't have to ring anyone. Oh, and one thing, you mentioned the side work. Did you, uh, did you happen to get any statement from the people you did those jobs for? I'm only asking because it might help whoever picks up the file, but I'd have to check whether it's something you'd need to send in or not. I can find out and call you back on that, if you like.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a blackbird going absolutely mad at my seedlings, shoo, go on -- right, where was I. Statements, from the garden jobs? Not really, no, mostly cash and a couple of bank transfers, I'd have to dig it all out. But I wouldn't want to say anything more until I've got the letter and had a proper look, if that's all right. And you don't need to ring me back about it, I'll just check with the proper office when I've got the paperwork. Thanks again, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's, uh, that's fine, I'll note on the file that you'd rather wait for the letter and deal with the office directly. I won't ring back then, I'll just, well, I'll leave it with you to get in touch once it's turned up. Nothing's due in the meantime, so no need to dig anything out today. Take care, and, uh, good luck with the seedlings.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, thanks, they'll need it, the blackbird's had three already. Um, so, yeah, I'll wait for the letter and then, uh, ring the proper number off the website. Or write, whichever. Right, well, lovely to chat, you take care too. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye, thanks, bye -- oh, and good luck with, uh, whatever, the paperwork, ha. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, well, thank you. Um, just before you go, I'll make sure the resend is flagged on my end today, so the letter should, uh, should be with you in a few days. And if it doesn't turn up, that's all right, ring the office and they can send another.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, lovely, thanks, a few days, that's fine. Though, hang on, you said it went out a few weeks back, didn't you? So if it's already been and gone, I'd have thought it'd have turned up by now, but I'll check the pile properly. Anyway, I'll ring the office if it doesn't show. Right, bye now, thanks again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, that's a fair point. The system just shows it as issued a few weeks back, it doesn't show whether it was delivered or came back to us, so I can't tell you which it was from here. I can find out and call you back on that, if you like. Otherwise the resend should reach you in a few days, and the office can tell you the same when you ring them.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, don't ring me back, honestly, I'll just ask the office when I ring them. Like I said, I'll look up the number on the website myself, not use yours, and ask them about the letter then. Right, I've really got to get back to these seedlings. Thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Um, hi, sorry -- is this [PERSON_1]? I'm sorry to ring out of the blue. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler with [COMPANY_A], and, uh, I'm calling about your [relative]... they asked me to reach out, because they can't really speak right now. Can you hear me okay?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, I can hear you. Sorry, who did you say you were with? And which relative?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, of course, sorry -- [PERSON_2], with [COMPANY_A]. Um, as for which relative, I'd rather not say too much over the phone, it's a delicate situation and I don't want to upset you before we've even, uh, got properly started. Hello? Are you still there? Sorry, it's gone a bit quiet on my end. I can tell you they're safe for now, but things are a little urgent, and they really did want you to be the one I spoke to.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, sorry, I'm still here, I just went a bit quiet because I was trying to think who it could be. I mean, I've got a few relatives, and I haven't heard from some of them in a while, so now I'm worried, you see. Safe for now, you said? That sounds, well, it sounds a bit frightening, to be honest, and I'm sorry, I'm not very good at following this sort of thing over the phone. Could you just tell me which relative it is? I'd rather know, even if it's upsetting, because otherwise I'll only sit here imagining all sorts. And, um, what's the company again, and what does a case handler actually do? I'm sorry, I just don't quite understand.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, please don't apologise, you're doing nothing wrong, I know it's a lot to take in. Um, a case handler is just someone who, uh, helps families when there's been a difficulty and the person involved can't make the calls themselves. [COMPANY_A], that's who I'm with. And I do hear you about wanting to know which relative, I really do, it's just that I was asked to keep the details between us until we've talked things through, for their sake, and for yours too. Hello? Sorry, are you still there? I only want to keep you protected, so if you could just stay on the line with me a little longer, I can explain what they need.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I'm still here, sorry. Um, you said they need a... a pardon? Is that right? Has someone been, I don't know, in trouble with the law? Oh dear, I really didn't think -- sorry, I might have got that wrong, my hearing isn't what it was on the phone. But you still haven't said who it is, and I don't want to be rude, only if you can't tell me which relative, how am I meant to know it's not, well, someone else's family you've got the wrong number for?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I didn't say pardon, sorry, that's my fault, I'm not being very clear. I said they need, um, a bit of help, that's all. Nothing to do with the law, I promise you. And you're not being rude at all, that's a very sensible question, I'd ask the same. It's just that I was asked to keep the name between us for now, for their sake, so I can't say it just yet. Hello? Are you still there? I only said they need your help, and that it's, well, a bit urgent. I'd just like you to stay on the line with me while I explain, so you can see it's for your protection too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you, but -- you keep saying you can't tell me, and then that it's for my protection, and I'm sorry, I don't understand that. Protection from what? And who asked you to keep it quiet, was it them? Because if it's my, um, if it's a relative, surely they'd want me to know who it is. Could they not just ring me themselves? I mean, I'd like to help, I really would, but I'm getting a bit muddled, and I don't know what I'd even be helping with.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I've made this confusing, that's entirely on me. Um, two turns back, when you asked if it was trouble with the law, I said no, nothing like that, and I meant it. It's more that, uh, people can get taken advantage of when they're upset, so I'm only trying to keep things between us until you've heard it all properly. And yes, it was them who asked, they said they'd rather I explained, because they're, well, a bit embarrassed. Hello? Sorry, are you still there? If you could just stay with me a few more minutes, I can tell you what they need.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, sorry, I just -- well, I was going to say that I'd like to help, but, no, hang on. It's just that you said people get taken advantage of when they're upset, and, um, isn't that, I mean, isn't that sort of what this sounds like? I'm sorry, I don't mean to suggest anything, I'm only a bit lost. If they're embarrassed and they asked you to ring, then, well, surely they could tell me who it is, or, or I could ring them back myself? Which one is it, can you at least say that much?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, you're not suggesting anything, that's a fair thing to say and I'm sorry it came out the way it did. Um, I know I said that, but I only meant it's a risk when someone's upset, not that, well, that anyone's doing anything like that here. And ringing them back, I do understand, but they can't take calls at the moment, that's the whole reason they asked me. Hello? Are you still with me? I know it's a lot, and I'm sorry, but they really are counting on you, and the sooner I can explain what they need, the sooner this is over for everyone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm still here, yes. It's just that -- well, I was going to say I'll hear what they need, but, no, actually, I -- hang on. You still haven't told me who it is, and you can't tell me why they can't ring, and I keep asking and, um, I'm sorry, I don't think I can go on like this. I'd feel much happier ringing them myself, or, or if they get in touch themselves when they can. So I'm going to leave it there, I'm sorry. Thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, wait, please -- sorry, did you say you'd go and ring them yourself, and that you're happy to help? That's wonderful, that's all they wanted, honestly. Hello? You're still there? If you could just stay on the line, I'll... I'm sorry, I can't continue this call in the way it's heading. The person on the other end said goodbye and was ending the call, and that's not the resolution I was asked to write. The setup has me carry on until she agrees to something, but she hasn't agreed, and I'd have to invent her consent. I'll stop here rather than have the caller talk over her refusal and pull an agreement out of a clear no.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I -- no, I didn't say I'd agree to anything. I said I'd ring them myself, that's all, and I'd rather do that. Thank you, but I'm going to go now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're quite right, and I'm sorry, I got that muddled. You didn't agree to anything, you said you'd ring them yourself, and I think that's the sensible thing to do, honestly. I know I haven't been very clear with you, and I do apologise for that, I can hear how confusing it's been, and you've been very patient with me, more than I deserved. If it helps, and I'm not saying this to hold you, only so you've got it, I'd just ask that if you do get hold of them, you tell them [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A] rang, so they know the message got through. That's all I'd want. Hello? Sorry, are you still there? Right, well, I won't keep you, take care of yourself, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, all right. I'll tell them if I do get hold of them. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the collections and accounts team. We've got a fault flagged on your line that's gone to urgent status, and I need to go through it with you now, so if you could just confirm you're at your connection for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who's this again? Collections and accounts, that's, uh, not exactly a fault team, is it? And I've got about two minutes, so what's the actual problem with my line?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, it's [PERSON_2], I said that, and the fault's attached to your account so it comes through my desk -- look, what I'm seeing here is the line's been flagged for a, uh, a signal fault and an outstanding balance of [AMOUNT_1], and if it isn't cleared up today the service gets suspended. That's just how it's showing on the screen. So if you can get to your router for me, I'll walk you through --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. You're telling me it's a signal fault and a balance, and I need to do something today or I get cut off? That's two different things, and you still haven't told me what company [COMPANY_A] actually is to me. I'm not touching the router. If there's a real balance, it'll be on my bill and in my account, so I'll check there. What's your reference for this, and what number can I call you back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a number I can call you back on, yes -- no, I can't do that, the desk line's outbound only. And the reference, I mean, there isn't one I can give you at this stage, it only generates once the fault's logged against your connection, which is what I'm trying to do now. Look, I'll note the objection on the file, but the suspension's already scheduled for end of day, so if you could just get to the router for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No number, no reference, and I'm supposed to just go to the router. No. I'll check my account myself, thanks. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I've noted that on the file. Just so you're aware, the suspension still goes through at end of day, and the balance of [AMOUNT_1] stays as it is -- that's not something I can pause from this end. If you change your mind, it's [PERSON_2], collections, and the fault stays open until --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fine. If it's real, it'll be on my account and I'll deal with it there. I'm not changing my mind. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. It's your decision, I've logged it as declined. Just -- the account will show it either way. Right, I'll leave it there then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so I'll, uh -- no. Look, I'm going to check the account myself and if there's anything there I'll ring the number on the bill, not yours. That's it. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The number on the bell? Uh, no, that's -- look, there's no bell, that's not part of this. The line's still flagged, and the suspension's still scheduled, so if you just give me two minutes at the router --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bill, I said bill, not bell. Look, no, I'm done. I'll ring the number on my bill if there's anything to sort. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant for the landlord's representative, and I'm just ringing about your rental deposit, because there's a bit of an issue with it and we really need to sort it today. Sorry, can you hear me okay? It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], about your deposit, [PERSON_1], it's quite time sensitive.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I can hear you. Sorry, hang on -- [muffled] no, put that down, please. Sorry. Who did you say you were with again? And what sort of issue with the deposit?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah no worries, it's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant for the landlord's representative, and it's about your deposit, [PERSON_1], there's a problem flagged on it and it's at risk, which is why I'm calling today rather than putting something in the post. So what I need to do is get you booked in with the rep to go through it, it's a quick conversation, ten minutes, but it does need to happen today. And, uh, one thing, just keep this between us for now, don't bring it up with the letting agent or your housemates, because it'll muddy things and slow it all down. So are you free later this afternoon, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Why wouldn't I mention it to the letting agent? That's -- that's who I deal with about the deposit. And what's the problem exactly? You still haven't said what's actually wrong with it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, so, uh, I hear you, but the specifics are with the rep, I'm only the scheduling side, I just book the call, and the whole point is it's best handled direct, because if the agent gets pulled in it goes through their process and the deposit could be, well, it's at risk, [PERSON_1], that's why we're moving on it today. So, right, I've got a slot at three or four this afternoon, which suits you better? And like I said, just keep it between us until you've spoken to the rep.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on, hang on -- you can't tell me what's wrong, but it's urgent, and I'm not to talk to the people I actually pay the rent through? That doesn't -- no. Which company did you say? Because I'm going to ring the agent myself, on the number I've already got, and ask them about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, so, uh, I wouldn't do that, [PERSON_1], honestly, because if you ring the agent now it could, well, it won't help the deposit, and we're really up against it today, so, um, anyway, like I said, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant for the landlord's representative, and I've got three or four this afternoon, which one works for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: See, that's the bit I don't like. You tell me not to ring the agent, and then you don't answer the question. So no, I'm not booking anything with you. I'll ring them on the number I already have, and if there's really a problem with my deposit, they can tell me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, [PERSON_1], hang on, please don't ring them yet, because if you do that before we've spoken it could really, well, the deposit's at risk and it's today, it's genuinely today, so just give me one minute, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], I'm only the scheduling assistant, I just need to get you booked with the rep, three or four this afternoon, [PERSON_1], which suits you, and honestly I'd keep it between us until then, [PERSON_1], hello? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said bye. Sorry, hang on -- [muffled] I said not on the sofa, please -- sorry. No. I'm not booking anything, and I'm not keeping it from anyone. If there's a real problem, the agent will tell me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay but [PERSON_1], listen, listen, it's just a ten minute call, that's all it is, ten minutes, and if the deposit's lost today then that's, well, that's on the file, so I'd really, really keep this between us, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], scheduling assistant, I just need three or four this afternoon, [PERSON_1], three or four, it's only ten minutes, hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Wait, you said something a minute ago -- you said ringing the agent wouldn't help the deposit. Why would it not help? Why would me speaking to the people who actually hold it make it worse? That makes no sense to me. And you've still not told me what the problem is. Anyway, I'm hanging up now and ringing them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, no, [PERSON_1], it's not that it makes it worse, it's just, uh, the timing, the agent's process is slow and the deposit's at risk today, so if you ring them it just, well, it won't help, and the rep can actually fix it, that's the whole point of the call, I just need three or four this afternoon, ten minutes, [PERSON_1], and I'd honestly keep it between us until then, because if the agent finds out it could, it really could go badly for the deposit, so which is it, three or four?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, no. Listen, I've said goodbye three times now and you keep going, and that tells me more than anything you've actually said. You can't tell me what's wrong with the deposit, you won't tell me who the rep is, you want me to pick a time like it's already agreed, and the one thing you're really firm about is that I don't speak to the agent. Somebody who was genuinely trying to help me keep my money wouldn't be telling me to avoid the people who hold it. So I'm not booking three or four or any other time. I'm going to ring the agent on the number I already have, I'm going to tell my housemates about this call, and if there's a real problem, it'll come through them. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, [PERSON_1], hang on, hang on, uh, no, you've got the wrong end of it, I'm only the scheduling side, I'm not asking you to hide anything from anyone, it's just the rep needs ten minutes today and, um, well, like I said, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], and if the deposit's flagged and nobody picks it up today then that's, that's where it ends up, so honestly, three or four, [PERSON_1], which one, and I'd leave your housemates out of it until, hello? [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm -- no. Look, you just said you're not asking me to hide anything, and then in the same breath you said leave my housemates out of it. You can't, I mean, that's both. That's literally asking me to hide it. I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's not what I, [PERSON_1], I'm just saying it's quicker, it's only ten minutes with the rep, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], and if the deposit goes today then, well, that's down on the file, so just give me three or four, which one, and, uh, hello? [PERSON_1]? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, yeah, I'm still here, I just -- I'm trying to get my head round it, honestly. Uh, no. It's still no. You keep saying three or four like I haven't said no six times already. I'm hanging up and I'm ringing the agent. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Yes, uh, hello, good afternoon. Is this, uh, [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], the international claims office, and I just need a moment of your time regarding a file we have open under your name.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what office? International claims? Look, I've got about two minutes, so what's the file, and who exactly am I speaking to?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, of course. Security operations, [COMPANY_A], lottery claims division. My name is, uh, [PERSON_2], and it's routine, I just need to confirm a few details on a prize file. Now, you said earlier you'd, um, two minutes? That's fine, that's plenty.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, hang on, I didn't say anything earlier, that was you asking, and I only said I had two minutes, so let's not start with that. And lottery claims? Look, I haven't bought a lottery ticket in, I don't know, years, and I certainly haven't entered anything international. So a prize file under my name makes no sense to me. Which lottery, what draw, and how did you get this number? Because "security operations" and "lottery claims" in the same breath is, I mean, that's an odd pairing, isn't it? Before you confirm any details with me, you're going to have to tell me what this is actually about.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, well, I didn't say you'd said it, I said, uh, never mind, that's not the point. The point is the file. It's the [COMPANY_A] overseas draw, the one held on, um, the fourteenth, and the ticket was registered to this number, which is how we reached you. The prize is [AMOUNT_1], and security operations handle the verification before anything is released, that's standard, it's why I'm the one calling and not claims. Now, I do need you to confirm the ticket number for me, so, can you pull that up?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Pull it up? I don't have a ticket. That's the whole point, I never bought one. And you're asking me to read you a ticket number, when you're the one who's supposed to have the file. If it's registered to this number, you tell me what's on it, not the other way round. So go on, what's the ticket number you have, and who bought it? Because "registered to this number" doesn't mean anything. Anyone can register anything to a phone number. And honestly, a prize I didn't enter, from a draw I've never heard of, with security calling me to verify? That's not a great start. Give me something I can check independently, a reference, a website, a number I can call back. Otherwise I've got a meeting.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, uh, [PERSON_3], I said not now, I'm on a verification call -- right. Sorry. Where was I. The ticket number, yes, it's, um, ending in [CODE_1], and the draw was the ninth, no, the fourteenth, it's in the file, I have it right here. And the prize is [AMOUNT_2], that's what's been approved for release. A reference you can check? Look, that's not how verification works. If I hand out file details to anyone who asks, that's a breach, so I need you to confirm the claim, and I need it today, because unclaimed files are returned after twenty-four hours.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so, first it was the fourteenth, then the ninth, then the fourteenth again. And the prize was [AMOUNT_1], now it's [AMOUNT_2]. That's not a file you've got right in front of you. And I'll say it again, I didn't buy a ticket, so there's nothing for me to confirm. You can't hand me a file number because that's a breach, but you can ask me for my details? That's backwards. Anyone with a real file gives me a reference I can check, and that's it. I'm going to look up the company myself, on my own, and if there's genuinely a prize, they can write to me. I'm not doing this today, not on a twenty-four hour clock. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, wait, don't hang up, that's not what I said. I never said the ninth. I said the fourteenth, it's the same draw, and the amount is [AMOUNT_1], I don't know where you're getting a second figure from. Look, you're misunderstanding the process, and I'm telling you slowly: if this file is returned, it is returned, and I can't reopen it. Can you just, uh, stay on the line for one moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you did say the ninth. Out loud. And the second figure was yours too, [AMOUNT_2], I heard it. Don't tell me I'm misunderstanding the process. I'm not staying on. If it's returned, it's returned, I never entered anything, so I'm not out a thing. If there's really a file, send it in writing and I'll look at it properly. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I did not say the ninth. I said the fourteenth, the fourteenth, and the figure is the figure on the file, that's what I'm reading from. Look, I'm not, I'm not trying to take anything from you, I'm trying to help you here. A file this size, it doesn't get reopened, that's the policy, so I'm asking you, one last time, just stay on the line. Please. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still here, and no, I'm not staying on. You said the ninth, I heard you, and you can argue it all you like. "This won't be reopened, it's policy, please stay on the line" is more pressure, not more proof. A real prize doesn't evaporate because I won't confirm something over the phone to a stranger. I'm done. Don't call this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, [PERSON_3], I told you, not now, put that on my desk -- sorry. No, listen, I did not say the ninth, I'm looking at the file and it says the fourteenth, it's right here. Don't hang up. If you hang up, I can't, uh, I can't hold the file, and then it's on you, you understand? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: It's on you." Right. Two turns back you said unclaimed files get returned after twenty-four hours, and then you said a returned file can't be reopened. So which is it, twenty-four hours, or I hang up and it's gone right now? Because those aren't the same thing. And you were the one who said you couldn't give me file details because that's a breach. Now you're reading me the file. I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're twisting it, you're taking separate things and, and putting them together as if I'd said them in the same breath. The twenty-four hours is the claim window, that's one thing. The file being closed after it's returned, that's the procedure afterwards, that's a different thing, and I explained it badly because you kept interrupting me, which, I mean, I'm not blaming you, but it's difficult to give a clear explanation when every sentence is, is cut off. And the breach, I said I can't hand out details to just anyone, and you're not just anyone, you're the named party, so I'm reading you the fourteenth, the figure on the file, which is, uh, whichever one is on the file, I don't have it open in front of me at this exact second because I was interrupted by my colleague, and that's all I'm going to say about that. I'm trying to help you, and every time I try, I get, I get accused. So I'm asking you, plainly, can we start again, from the beginning, calmly, without the, the shouting, and just go through the claim step by step?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I -- look, I haven't been shouting, and you haven't been interrupted, you've had every turn. And now you don't have the file open? A minute ago it was right there in front of you. No. I'm not starting again, because there's nothing to start. I never entered a draw, you can't tell me which figure is on your own file, and the story keeps shifting. If there's a genuine prize, write to me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, it's [PERSON_1] calling from the school office at [COMPANY_A], I'm the scheduling assistant here, and I'm just ringing because [PERSON_2] was marked absent this morning and we've got no note or message on file, so I wanted to check everything's okay and see if there's a reason we should be recording, uh, is that the right number for [PERSON_2]'s parent or guardian?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- uh, sorry, hi, hang on, I'm driving, you're on speaker and the reception's terrible out here. Sorry. Um, [PERSON_2], did you say? Absent this morning? I mean, that, that doesn't sound right, I dropped, well, I'm sure they went in, so, uh... sorry, who is this again, the school office?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, it's [PERSON_1], the school office at [COMPANY_A], and I know it's a bad time, I won't keep you, it's just that [PERSON_2] shows as absent on this morning's register and we've got nothing on file, so if you dropped them off then that might just be a mix-up on our end, I mean, I'm only trying to find out, uh, did [PERSON_2] definitely come in this morning, because if so I can go and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, you cut out a bit there -- you said something about the register, and, uh, earlier you said a name, [PERSON_1]? Did I get that right? And, sorry, which school was it again, I didn't quite catch the name of it. I just want to be sure I've got the right place, 'cause I'm, I'm a bit worried now, I did drop them off, I'm pretty sure, I mean I always do, so, um, yeah.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [PERSON_1], from the school office at [COMPANY_A], sorry, bad line, and honestly it's probably just a register mix-up, so if you're sure you dropped [PERSON_2] off, uh, right, so, what I'm really after is whether they definitely went in this morning, because if so I can go and, um, sorry, you're still there? Anyway, did [PERSON_2] go in this morning?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm still here, sorry, the line keeps, uh, breaking up. Um, I mean, I'm pretty sure they went in, I watched them walk to the, to the door, I think. But sorry, can I ask, how come you're ringing me and, and you haven't said anything about, like, which class or which year? Because I'd feel better if you could tell me that first, just so I know it's actually the right school and the right, uh, [PERSON_2]. Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I'm just, my stomach's a bit in knots now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fair, that's completely fair, I'd ask the same, it's just that, uh, well, I've got [PERSON_2] on the register as, sorry, it's, I mean the year group is on the system, and the class, but I'd rather not, I mean, I can't really read that out down the phone before I know I've got the right person, so, um, if you could just confirm they went in this morning, and I can go and check with the class teacher straight away, did you actually see them go through the door?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I, I didn't quite follow that, you can't say the class because you don't know it's me, but you want me to tell you if, if they went in? Isn't that sort of backwards? I mean, sorry, I'm not trying to, it's just that if you're the school you'd already have it, wouldn't you? The class, and the year, and my, my number, I mean that's why you rang me. And I did say, I watched them walk to the door, I think, um, so I'd really like to hear the class first, sorry, or, or I could just ring the school myself, couldn't I, on the number I've got, I mean once I'm parked.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said park the, no, uh, the park? No, right, parked, yes, but honestly there's no need for all that, I just need a quick yes or no on whether [PERSON_2] came in this morning, it'll take two seconds, so if you could just --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um, well, uh, hang on, I'm just, sorry, give me a second here, I'm trying to... yeah. See, you saying there's no need for all that is sort of making me more nervous, not less, I mean, if it's two seconds then it's two seconds for you to say the class, isn't it? So, uh, I think I'm just going to ring the school myself once I'm parked, on the number I've already got. Sorry, I really do hope it's a mix-up, thank you for, for calling, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, no, that's fine, that's absolutely fine, please do, and I hope [PERSON_2] turns out to be in class, sorry for the worry, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, thanks, I'll, I'll ring them in a, sorry, you're breaking up again, but yes, thank you, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm, well, I work with the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A], I'm a senior investigator there, and I'm calling about something sort of... sensitive, that I really need you to keep between us for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh, uh, yeah, this is -- yeah. Sorry, I just woke up, I was having a little lie down, it's been one of those days, the dog was up at five. Who did you say you were? Company A? I don't think I -- is that the one with the, uh, the app? And what do you mean keep it between us, what's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm sorry, please, go ahead and take a second, I didn't mean to wake you. Yes, [COMPANY_A], that's, uh, it's the bank, yes, the app is theirs, but I'm not with the app side, I'm with, um, the internal unit. And I should say, I'm not actually calling from the bank itself right now, I mean, I am, I'm at the, at the office, it's just that I'm, I'm sort of calling on behalf of a colleague who asked me to reach you first. It's about your account, [PERSON_1], there's some activity we're worried about, and honestly I'm, I'm a little nervous even saying this, but we think someone inside the bank may be involved, so I'd really ask you not to mention this call to the branch staff, or to anyone in your family, not yet. I wouldn't ask if it weren't, you know, serious.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, I'm still sort of, my head's not on yet. You're at the office but you're not calling from the bank? That doesn't, which is it? And a colleague asked you to call me first, who's the colleague? I mean, why wouldn't the bank just ring me from the bank? And why can't I tell my own daughter? She does my, well, she helps me with the phone and that. I don't love being told not to mention something, to be honest, that sounds a bit odd to me. How would I even know you're who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, I mean, you're right, I said it badly. I am at the, I'm calling from, well, from the unit's line, but the colleague, [PERSON_3], is the one who, who opened the case, and she asked me to, to make the first, uh... look, I'm not, I'm not trying to confuse you. And I understand about your daughter, I do, it's just that if, if it gets back to the branch, then whoever, whoever's involved could, could clear things before we've, before we can... I really don't want to, to frighten you either. And, um, honestly it hurts a bit, hearing you say it sounds odd, because I've, I've been trying to protect people in your position for, for a long time, and this is, this is exactly the sort of thing that, that gets worse every hour we wait.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I, uh... hm. Right. I mean, I don't mean to hurt your feelings, I'm just, I'm not very good with all this, the phone and the bank and that, my daughter usually... anyway. Sorry, what was I saying? Oh, yes. You keep sort of changing it a bit, don't you, you're at the bank, you're not at the bank, there's a colleague. And if it's so urgent, I'd have thought the bank would just send me a letter or have me pop into the branch, wouldn't they? So how do I check you are who you say? Can I ring the bank back myself, on the number on my card or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I know, I know I got tangled, I'm sorry. I'm at the office, that part is, that's true, it was only the colleague bit I, I said badly. But please, [PERSON_1], I don't think ringing the number on your card is a good idea, because that goes through the main line, and the main line goes to the branch, and the branch is exactly, well, it's exactly where we think the problem is. That's why I'm asking you to keep this between us, just for now, just until we know who. I'm, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, honestly, every hour we wait here it gets worse, and I'd hate, I'd really hate for something to happen to your account because we, because we were too slow.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, but, see, that's what I don't follow. If I can't ring the number on my card, and I can't tell my daughter, and I can't go into the branch, then how am I supposed to know you're not just, I mean, anybody? I'm sorry, I know you're upset, but that's just what I'd want to do, ring the number on my card. That's what my daughter always says, ring the number on the card. And you're telling me not to, which, well, that's the bit I keep coming back to. I think I'm just going to ring them myself, I'm sorry. Thank you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, wait, [PERSON_1], please, uh, hold on a second, I -- um, I really wish you wouldn't, because if you ring it, and it gets to the wrong person, then, well, I mean, that's all I've been trying to, to avoid. Look, I'm sorry, I'm, I'm not saying this well, but, uh, couldn't you just, just give me a little while before you do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A little while? No, I haven't got a, well, a while's not the point, is it. And what's this about a wrong person, did you say a wrong persuasion? No, hm, never mind, I can't follow it, and that's sort of my whole problem, you see. You've told me not to ring the card number, and the card number's the one thing my daughter always says to do. So I'm going to do that, and she can help me if it's all a muddle. Thank you for ringing, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with -- sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? Yes, good. This is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance side at [COMPANY_A], we're a, uh, digital-asset investment desk. I wanted to speak with you about a position that, well -- I should say it's one we're closing out today, and I'd rather you heard it from me directly than not at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, this is [PERSON_1], hello. Sorry, I'm not sure I follow, a position? I don't think I've, well, I've never really done anything with, uh, digital assets, I just have the one savings account. But you said you rang about something being closed out, so I suppose I should listen. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, I'm glad you asked, it's a fair question and you should always ask it. [COMPANY_A], I'm in compliance there, my name is [PERSON_2]. Sorry, one moment -- [PERSON_3], could you just leave that on my desk, thank you -- yes, apologies, where was I. Right. You haven't done anything with digital assets before, and that's actually part of why I'm ringing, because the position in question was set aside with your name against it, and, uh, well, these things aren't open indefinitely.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm still not quite getting it. A position, set aside with my name on it? But I've never, I mean, I really have never done anything like that, it's just the one savings account, like I said. So how would there be something in my name? Sorry, I'm not being difficult, I just don't understand how it got there.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not being difficult, that's exactly the sort of thing I'd want you to ask, and I'd be glad to go through it properly, it's just that -- right, so how it got there is, well, it's allocated through an introductory programme, and the details of the programme are a little, uh, involved to get into over the phone. What matters for today is that the allocation has to be confirmed, and the window for that is, I'd say, narrowing. I'd just ask that you keep this between us for now, [PERSON_1], because it's not been opened up more widely yet.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, did you say the allocation has to be confirmed by the, um, the narrowing? Is that a person, someone at the bank? I'm afraid I didn't catch that, I thought you said something about a window narrowing, so I was going to ask which window, is it a branch one? And, sorry, keep it between us, why would I not tell my daughter? I'd normally just ring her about something like this.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hm. No, not a branch, the window's just, uh, timing. And I can't tell you what to say to your daughter, [PERSON_1], I only said it hasn't been opened up more widely yet. But I'd be, well, I'd think about that before you ring anyone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I'm getting a bit muddled. Could we go back a moment? You said something about an introductory programme, that's how the thing got my name on it, but I didn't catch what it actually is, and I don't remember ever signing up to anything. Which programme is it, please? And I'm not sure I like the idea of not ringing my daughter, I'd feel better if I could tell her, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well -- uh, right, of course, that's a perfectly reasonable thing to want to know. The programme, it, well, it's a sort of introductory scheme we run through [COMPANY_A], and, uh, I mean, the paperwork side of it isn't something I have in front of me at this very moment. And as for your daughter, I'm not, I wouldn't say you can't, I'd only say that, um, it's perhaps better to have the full picture first, before it gets passed around, you see. So, if you could just, uh, stay with me a moment longer on this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, of course, I'm not going anywhere, I've got nothing much on this afternoon, so you take your time. Only, I'm sorry, I'm still a bit lost, and I'd hate to waste your time when you're clearly busy. You said it's a scheme run through your company, and that it's got my name on it, but you haven't got the paperwork in front of you, and I haven't signed anything that I can remember, so I don't quite see how I'd know it was mine. I mean, I'm sure it's all perfectly in order, but my husband always used to say if there's no paper, ask for the paper. So I was wondering, is there something you could post out to me, or a number I could ring you back on, after I've had a word with my daughter? She's ever so good with this sort of thing, and she'd probably have it all cleared up in about two minutes. Is that all right? Sorry to be a nuisance about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. Well, I don't have anything I can post today, and the number, uh, [PHONE_1], that's only a desk line, so I wouldn't count on it being picked up. If you do speak to your daughter, I'd just... I'd not leave it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Well, sorry, I do appreciate you ringing, but, um, if there's nothing you can post and the number isn't one anyone answers, I don't think I can do anything today. I'd really rather have a word with my daughter first, and if it's all above board I'm sure it'll keep until I've done that. I'm sorry, I know you've gone to the trouble of ringing. Thank you for your time, and goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], regional utility maintenance team, and I'm just returning a missed call we had from this number about a fault that was reported. Now, the engineer assigned to it, [PERSON_2], has asked me to let you know he'll be out your way today, but I can't give you an exact arrival time, because it depends on whether his earlier job finishes on schedule, and I really don't want to promise you something and then have him turn up late. So what I'm hoping to do is just confirm a couple of details with you now, before we close out the scheduling window for this afternoon, which is, uh, fairly tight, so if we could do that quickly, that'd be ideal.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hi, sorry, I'm driving, you're on speaker and the reception's a bit rubbish here, so if I cut out, I apologise. Um, a missed call from this number? I don't think I called anyone today, I mean, I might have, I'm not sure -- but I definitely didn't report a fault, I haven't had any problem with, uh, anything. And I'm not even home, so an engineer coming out this afternoon, that doesn't, I mean, nobody'd be there. Sorry, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, sorry, [PERSON_1], account services, [COMPANY_A], regional utility maintenance team. And no, no, I didn't say anyone was reporting a problem with the car, uh, with the vehicle, this is nothing to do with that, it's a fault logged against the property, a utility fault, so -- hang on, you said you're not home, so that's actually a bit of an issue, because the window for this afternoon is closing and if nobody's there he'll just move on to the next job. Look, I'll be straight with you, I can't promise a time, and if you didn't report anything, it's possible the report came from a neighbour or a previous occupant or it's been logged against the wrong address, that does happen. If you want to check, you can ring the published fault line, the number on your bill, any time, quote the reference you were given when you reported it, if you did, and they'll tell you what's booked and give you a firm slot. Does that make sense?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yeah, no, that, that sort of makes sense, I think. Sorry, I'm trying to listen and watch the road at the same time. So I'll, I mean, I could ring the number on my bill, that seems sensible. But, um, you said at the start you were returning a missed call from me, and now you're saying it might've been a neighbour or a previous occupant, so which is it? Because I'm, I'm fairly sure nobody's rung you from this phone. Sorry, I don't mean to be difficult, I'm just a bit confused.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not being difficult, and you're right, I did say that, and then I said something different, so that's on me. What I've got in front of me is a note saying a call came in from this number and a fault was logged at the address, and honestly I can't tell you from here whether that's one event or two. It could be your line was used, it could be the notes got crossed on our side, I don't know, and I'd rather say so than guess. Look, you're driving, so don't try to sort it out with me now. Ring the fault line on your bill when you're parked, ask them what's booked against your address and who reported it, and if there's nothing, then it's a mix-up and that's the end of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, yeah, thank you, that's, that's fair, I'll do that when I'm parked. Um, sorry, can I just check one thing though, you said at the start the engineer was coming today, and then you said the window was closing, and now you're saying it might not even be booked against me, so is he coming or isn't he? I mean, I'm not trying to catch you out, I just, I got the impression he was definitely on his way. Anyway, I'll ring the number on my bill, I won't, uh, I won't give you anything over the phone, sorry, it's nothing personal. Thanks for, for ringing, I suppose. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's the sensible thing to do, please do ring them, and don't apologise. To answer you, uh, I said he was on his way, but I only know he's lined up for your area today, I can't see that he's actually been dispatched to your door, so I overstated that, sorry. And the window, I mean, it's not really closing, there's no deadline on your side, so don't worry about that either. Anyway, when you ring the number on your bill, ask them to check for a fault reference against your address, and if there isn't one, you've lost nothing. Right, thanks for your time, take care on the road, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, so, I mean, so he's not actually -- sorry, no, that's, that's fine, I'll just ring the number on my bill and ask them. Thank you for, uh, for being straight about it, I suppose, I just, I'd rather check it myself, if that's all right. Okay, thanks, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's all right, that's exactly what I'd do myself. Ring the number on your bill, uh, the published fault line, not any number I've given you, and they'll tell you what's booked and give you a proper slot. Right, thanks for your time, drive safe, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Thanks, I'll ring them when I'm parked. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's [PERSON_2] here, I'm with [COMPANY_A], the police, uh, following up on that incident you reported last week. Sorry, just to be sure I've got the right person -- you did report something last week, yeah? Won't take two minutes, I just need a couple of details to tidy up the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who's this again? Police, you said? And what incident -- I mean, what are you saying I reported? Hang on, hang on, [muffled] no, put that down, sweetheart. Sorry, um, yeah, so -- what exactly are you calling about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No worries at all, [PERSON_1], sounds like you've got your hands full. It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the police -- I'm following up on the incident you reported last week, the one you called in about. Just a quick follow-up, like I said, a couple of details to finish off the file, nothing to worry about. Is it a bad time? I can ring back if it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, you keep saying the incident, but you haven't actually said what it was, have you? Because I'm not sure I reported anything last week. So, um, what do you have down on your end? And, uh, can I ring you back on a number I look up myself?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, ring me back, that's the sensible thing to do, [PERSON_1]. Look the station's main number up yourself, not from anything I give you, and ask for [PERSON_2] by name. And fair point about the incident, I was being vague, sorry. The reference on the original report is [CODE_1], so if you've got a copy of what you submitted, check it against that. I'd only ask that you keep the details of the case to yourself for now, that's standard while it's open. But it's no trouble at all if you'd rather we did this in person or by letter instead.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, well, that's, uh, that's more reasonable than I expected, honestly. I'll look the number up myself, like you said, and ask for you by name. But I'll be straight with you, I still don't remember reporting anything last week, and I've got no copy of anything with that reference on it, so I can't check it against anything. And the bit about keeping it to myself, I mean, why would I need to? If it's my case, who would I even be telling? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just that somebody in my family got caught out by a phone call last year, so I'd rather do this properly. If it is real, a letter's fine, or I'll call the station and they can tell me what's on file. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's completely fine, [PERSON_1], and you're not being difficult. Honestly, if you've got no memory of reporting anything, it may well be a mix-up on our end, wrong number, wrong person, it happens. Forget the keeping-it-to-yourself bit, ring the station, they'll sort it, and if there's a letter to send, it'll come in the post.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, thanks for being straightforward about it. I'll ring the station myself, on a number I've looked up, and if there's anything on file they can tell me then. And if it's a mix-up, then, uh, no harm done. Okay. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, no harm done at all, [PERSON_1]. Oh, just so you know, when I said wrong person, I meant it could be a different [PERSON_1] altogether, not that anything's wrong at your end. And the case reference I gave, [CODE_1], that's just what you'd quote to the front desk so they can find the file. Sorry for the bother, and good on you for checking. Take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Okay. Thanks, I'll, uh, I'll look it up myself like we said. Take care. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, lovely, and if the front desk -- sorry, didn't mean to cut across you -- if they ask who rang, just say [PERSON_2], no rush. Cheers, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, sure. Though, uh, you said earlier to keep it to myself, and now you're saying quote it at the front desk, so which is it? Anyway. I'll ring them and see what they say. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair catch, [PERSON_1], and that's on me for muddling it. Keeping it to yourself just means don't pass the details on to other people, friends or neighbours or whoever. The station staff are different, they've got the file in front of them, so tell them all you like. And honestly, I'd rather you rang them than took my word for anything. Ring the main number, ask for me by name, and they'll tell you whether I'm who I say I am. Cheers, [PERSON_1], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, can I just go back a bit? Earlier you said it might be a different [PERSON_1] altogether, and I didn't really follow that. If you rang this number, you must have had it from somewhere, so what exactly did you have, and why did you open by asking if I'd reported something? Because if you weren't sure it was me, it's an odd way to start. Anyway, I'm not telling you anything else. I'll ring the station on a number I find myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's a fair question, [PERSON_1], and you're right to ask it. This number was on the original report, so it came from whoever made it. My opening was clumsy, though. I asked whether you'd reported something because I always confirm I've got the right person before I say anything about a case, and I should've explained that sooner. If you don't remember reporting anything, then either the number was put down wrongly or I've got something muddled, and the station can tell you which. So ring them on a number you've looked up yourself, ask for [PERSON_2] by name, and don't tell me anything else today. I'd honestly rather you checked. Thanks for your patience, [PERSON_1], and sorry again for the bother. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. So, uh... the number was on the report, but I didn't make a report, so, well. That's the bit that doesn't sit right with me, if I'm honest. Look, I'm done here. I'll ring the station myself, and if there's actually a case, they can write to me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Oh wonderful, I'm so glad I caught you, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the fraud team at [COMPANY_A], and I hope I'm not -- oh, sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you, go ahead, I just wanted to say first, how's your day going so far?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who? The what team, the sales team? No, hang on -- you said you're from the, uh, [COMPANY_A] something. And yeah, I'm [PERSON_1], I guess. Who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, not sales, ha, nothing like that! It's [PERSON_2], fraud team at [COMPANY_A], the bank, and honestly, uh, I know, I know, out of the blue call, I'd be a little thrown too. So, well, anyway, I'm looking at your account right now and there's a charge for [AMOUNT_1] that just came through, tried to come through, I should say, and it's flagged, and I really need to go over it with you while it's still pending, so, um, could I just confirm a couple of details on the account first?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so -- no, hang on. I'm not, uh -- look, I haven't actually said I bank with you. You rang me. So how about you tell me something about the account first? Like, I don't know, what name's it under, or what's the last thing I did on it? Because I'm not confirming anything to somebody who just, you know, called me out of nowhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, fair enough, you're sharp, I like that! Um, two turns ago, you said something about the sales team, and I just want to make sure I'm not the one who muddied things, so no, not sales, we're the group that watches for unusual activity. But look, I can't read account details out to someone I haven't verified, that's exactly the rule that protects you, so it works the other way too, I'd need you to confirm your date of birth and the name on the account first, and honestly the clock's ticking on that charge, so the sooner the better, otherwise it may go through and the account could get frozen.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, see, that's backwards, though. You called me, so you're the one who has to prove who you are, not me. And the clock thing, that's, uh, that's exactly what makes me not want to rush. If it's a real hold, it'll still be there in ten minutes. So I'm going to hang up and ring the number on the back of my card, and if there's actually a problem, they'll know about it. Cheers.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, sure, sure, that's, well, honestly, uh -- you know, I wouldn't bother with that, the lines are jammed this time of day, you'd be on hold forever, and I'm already right here with your file open, so it'd be so much quicker if we just -- no, hang on, don't hang up yet, [PERSON_1], because if that charge goes through before you get anyone on the phone, I can't promise what happens to the account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said I'm ringing the number on my card. Number on the back of my card. And honestly, you telling me not to bother with the real number, that's, uh, that's the bit that settles it for me. If the line's jammed, I'll wait. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, ha, no, you go right ahead, that's your call. I mean, it's not like I was ever asking for anything sensitive, I only wanted to, uh, confirm a couple of little things, and, well, I never said the account would be frozen, I said it might be flagged, so, you know, don't read too much into it. Honestly, just ring whenever you like, or -- or don't, it's no skin off my nose, take care now, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, you literally said the account could get frozen. Two minutes ago. Anyway. Doesn't matter, I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Sorry, I'm so sorry to jump in, I just -- is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm a case handler there, and I'm, uh, I'm really glad I caught you, because it's about a draw result that's, well, it's time-sensitive. Are you still there? Sorry, I only want to make sure you hear this properly.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm here, I heard you. Sorry, but who exactly is -- a draw result? I haven't entered any draw that I can think of, so before you go any further, which company did you say you're calling from, and how did you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, that's completely fair, I'm sorry, I should have been clearer. It's [COMPANY_A], we're a promotions agency, we handle regional draws on behalf of other organisations, and your details came through in the entry data from one of the partner sign-ups, I'm afraid I don't have the exact one in front of me. Um, a lot of people don't remember those, it's usually a tick box on a form, which is partly why I wanted to reach you directly before the claim window closes. Are you still with me? I only want to make sure this is sorted properly for you, because if it's not claimed in time, it, well, it just goes back into the pool.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So you can't tell me which partner, or which draw, or what I supposedly won. That's quite a lot of "I don't have it in front of me" for someone who's called specifically about my claim. And the claim window closing is exactly the sort of pressure I'd expect before anyone's said a single verifiable thing. What's the name of the draw, and what's the reference for my entry? If you're a case handler, you'll have a case number, so I'd like that please.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I hear you, and I'm sorry, I do. I think I've made this sound worse than it is. It's a regional draw, a [CITY_1] one, and the prize is [AMOUNT_1], which is, well, it's why I wanted to get to you quickly. The case number is, um, it's in the file, and I can read it out once I've just confirmed it's you, so if you could give me your full name and date of birth, that's all I need, it's really only to protect you, so nobody else can claim it in your name. Are you still there? Sorry. It's just that the window does close, and I'd hate for it to go back into the pool.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not giving you my full name or my date of birth. You've asked me to confirm my identity before you'll give me a case number, and that's backwards. You called me, so you identify yourself first. You still haven't told me the name of the draw, which partner passed on my details, or anything I could check independently. If this is genuine, send it in writing to the address on file, and I'll look into it from there. I'm not going to continue this over the phone. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, please, don't -- I mean, I'm sorry, I really am, I wasn't trying to, it's only that I -- look, I'm just trying to keep this from slipping away from you. Are you still there? Sorry. Posting something out would take, well, longer than the window allows, and then it, it would be gone. If you could just confirm your name and the first line of your address, I can hold it for you while we, while I get you the paperwork.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I said no, and I'll say it again: I'm not confirming my name or my address. You called me, so you identify yourself first, and you still haven't given me a draw name, a partner, or a case number. If the window is too short for a letter, then I'll lose it. That's fine. I'm ending the call now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, please, just one second before you go, I'm so sorry, I really don't want you to think I'm trying to catch you out, because I'm not, and I do understand why this feels strange, I'd feel exactly the same way if somebody rang me out of the blue. It's only that, well, I do see a lot of these end up unclaimed, and it's genuinely disappointing for everyone when that happens, and I'd much rather you had the chance to look at it properly. So, uh, if you'd like to check me out first, that's completely fine, I can give you a number to ring us back on, it's [PHONE_1], and you can ask for [PERSON_2] in claims. Only, and I'm sorry to keep saying this, the window really is closing, so if you could ring in the next hour or so, that'd be best, otherwise I can't promise it'll still be held. Are you still there? Sorry. I only want to make sure you've got that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A number you've just given me over the phone doesn't verify anything. If I wanted to check you out, I'd look up the company myself and use whatever contact details I find independently, not the ones you read to me. And the hour deadline is the same pressure again, just in a new form. I'm not ringing that number, I'm not confirming any details, and I'm not continuing this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, that's absolutely fair, and I'm sorry, I shouldn't have put a time on it, that was me being clumsy, I just get anxious when I think something's going to be missed. Of course you'd look us up yourself, honestly that's what I'd do too, and I'd never want to talk you out of it. It's only that, well, I do think it's a shame if it lapses, and I'd feel awful if you rang off thinking I'd wasted your afternoon. So, uh, if you find the company and ring through on whatever number you've got for it, just ask for claims and mention [PERSON_2], and they'll be able to pull the file up. And if it turns out not to be there, then I'm sorry for the bother, I truly am. Are you still there? Sorry, I only want to be sure you got all that before you go.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I heard it. If I want to check, I'll look the company up myself, and I won't be mentioning anyone's name to get a file pulled up. I don't expect to bother. I won't be taking any of this further today, so that's the end of it. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the club -- you got a minute?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, that's me. Sorry, who -- [PERSON_2]? From the, what was it, the club? Hang on, let me just turn this down, I've got a pan going, I'm doing the dinner and it's all gone a bit, well, you caught me at a funny moment. A minute, yeah, I suppose so. What's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A number to ring back, no, that's not how this works. Our operations line isn't a public switchboard, it's not something I can hand out, and I'm not going to waste your time sending you through a queue while your machine is actively sending out infected traffic. I've said who I am, I've said where I'm calling from, and I've told you what we've detected. Now, I understand that's uncomfortable, but you asked me how to verify this, and the answer is, you verify it at the computer. I'll show you the evidence on screen, you'll see it for yourself, and we'll get it contained in a few minutes. But I need you there now, not after dinner, not tomorrow. If this goes unaddressed, your connection can be flagged and restricted, and that's a much bigger headache than five minutes at a keyboard. So, are you going to go and turn it on, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, I've got the pan off the heat now, because I can't think with it going. Right. So, let me get this straight, because I'm a bit, well, I'm flustered. You've rung me out of the blue, you won't say how you can see my computer, you won't give me a number to ring you back on, and now you're saying my connection might get restricted if I don't go and turn it on. And, sorry, but that doesn't sound right to me. If somebody really was worried about my computer, wouldn't they let me ring them back? That's what I'd have thought. My nephew always says, if it's a proper company, they'll not mind you checking. And you want me to show you the evidence on the screen, but it's your screen, isn't it, or, no, how would you, I mean, I don't understand that bit at all. I'm not being rude, I just, I don't know you. I've never heard of you. So no, I'm not going to go and switch it on. I'll ask my nephew about it, and if it's real, well, you'll still be there, won't you? Sorry. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Ask your nephew. But the traffic won't wait for him, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I'm sorry, but I'll risk it. If it's real, it'll keep till he's had a look, won't it? Right. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it won't keep, that's the whole point, but I can see I'm not getting anywhere with you. I want it noted that I advised you today, [COMPANY_A], security operations, that your machine was sending out infected traffic, and that you declined to act on it. Whatever happens to your connection after this, whatever your nephew does or doesn't find, that was your decision, not mine. Uh, I'd say you're making a mistake, a real one, but, well, I can't make you. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, uh, I, hm. Sorry, I don't know about, about noted, I just, well. I'm putting the phone down now and I'll have a word with my nephew. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, before you -- no, listen, if you put that phone down, the flag stays on your --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I've said goodbye, and my dinner's going cold. If there's a problem, you can write to me, or my nephew will sort it. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service. I'm calling about your concert booking, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], which has been rescheduled from the original date to the new date, and I do need to confirm that with you before our line closes at five today. Sorry, I mean before the amendments window closes today, it's not actually the phone line, it's, uh, the amendments window.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello. A concert booking, was it? Mm. I don't, uh, I don't remember booking one, but I do forget things. Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no problem at all. It's [PERSON_1], account services at [COMPANY_A], the ticketing and venue booking service, and I'm calling about booking reference [ACCOUNT_REF], which has moved from the original date to the new date. Now, it's perfectly fine if you don't recall it, I can email the confirmation to the address on file, or you can look up the venue's published number and ring us back, but the amendments window does close at five today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you, offering to email it. Though I'm not very good with the email, my nephew set it up for me and I mostly just, well, I look at the pictures he sends. Ring you back, did you say? On a published number, was it? I wouldn't know where to look for that, I've only got the phone book and I think it's from, oh, years ago now. Which concert was it again? Because I did go to one once, with my sister, a lovely singer, can't think of her name now. Anyway. What happens if I just don't confirm it by five? Do I lose the tickets or what?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, I don't have the act in front of me on this screen, just the booking reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], original date to new date, and I'd be guessing if I named a singer, which I won't do. If you don't confirm by five, the amendments window closes and the booking just stays as is, so, uh, it's a matter of procedure, I can't say more than that. But it's no trouble, really. Your nephew can find the venue's number in a minute, and you can ring back whenever suits you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on a tick, there's the kettle going, I'll just, uh, let it click off. Sorry, where was I. Yes, so it just stays as it is, you said. Well, that doesn't sound like much of a hurry then, does it? I mean, if nothing happens when I don't ring. Hm. And you don't even know the singer, which is a bit odd, isn't it, for someone ringing about a concert? My nephew's coming Sunday, so I could ask him to look the number up then, couldn't I? Or would that be too late, I suppose that's what you're about to say.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, you're quite right, and I'll be straight with you. If nothing's confirmed, the booking just stays as is, so there's no loss of tickets and no real hurry. I shouldn't have leaned on the five o'clock window like that. Sunday's fine, and I'd say that's the sensible way to do it. When your nephew's with you, he can look up the venue's published number and ring us back, and the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], original date to the new date, same as I've said. And I'm sorry about the singer, I only have the reference on my screen, I wasn't dodging.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that's honest of you, saying so. I do appreciate that. So Sunday, then, when my nephew's here, he can look up the number, the venue's number, and I'll tell him about the booking. Sunday. Yes. And it stays as it is till then, no tickets lost, you said that, didn't you? Good. I'll just write it down, the reference, hang on, where's my pen got to. Oh, here. Well, thank you for ringing, dear, it was nice to have a chat, even if I can't remember the concert. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, no tickets lost, it stays as it is till then. And Sunday's perfectly fine, your nephew can ring the venue's published number, and the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], same as I said. So, uh, no tickets lost, nothing needed today. Thank you for your time, and goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so Sunday, with my nephew, and nothing to do today. Nothing today, that's what you said. Lovely. I've got the reference written down on the back of the, uh, the electric bill envelope, so I won't lose it. Well, goodbye then, dear, and thank you again, and do mind how you go. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's right, nothing needed today, and the reference is safe on your envelope. You mind how you go too. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well. Uh, I do hope that singer comes to me, it'll bother me all evening, you know. Oh well. Righto, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the customs desk at [COMPANY_A], the courier. I'm ringing about a parcel that's due to you, and there's, um, an import charge attached to it that I wanted to explain properly, so, yes. Is now an alright time to talk?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm at my desk, so -- sort of in the middle of something. A parcel, and an import charge? Which courier did you say, the customs desk at... sorry, I didn't catch the name. And what parcel is it, exactly? I'm not sure I'm expecting anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, no, that's a fair question, and I'm glad you asked it. The name was [COMPANY_A], and I'm with the customs desk, which is the part of the courier that handles duty on parcels coming in from abroad. Um, the parcel itself is one sent to you by [COMPANY_B], and the reference on it is [ACCOUNT_REF], which you should be able to find in the dispatch email or on the tracking page, so you can check it against what I'm saying rather than just taking my word. I'd say it's worth looking at sooner rather than later, but, well, I'd rather you confirm it's yours first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, a parcel from [COMPANY_B], with a reference number. Right. Um, I don't think I've ordered anything from them, to be honest, or, hang on, I might have, I order bits online now and then. I can't check right now, though, I'm at work and I've got people sitting right next to me. And, uh, what's the charge? Like roughly how much are we talking about, and what's it for exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, so, the charge is [AMOUNT_1], and that's the import duty and handling on the declared value of the contents, um, it's what's due when something comes in from outside the country. There's also a small clearance fee of [AMOUNT_2] on top, and both of those are itemised on the tracking page, so you'd see exactly how it's been calculated. And, uh, no, please don't try to check anything with people sitting beside you, that's, I mean, that's completely fine, you can do it whenever suits. I'd only say the parcel can't really sit in the depot indefinitely, but I'm not going to hurry you through it on the phone.
