utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm, okay. So [AMOUNT_1] duty, plus [AMOUNT_2] clearance, and it's itemised on the tracking page. Right. But, uh, you said it can't sit in the depot indefinitely, so how long do I actually have? Like is that today, or this week? And if I'm going to look at this, I'd rather go to the courier's own website or the email I got from [COMPANY_B], not follow anything from this call. Is there a number I can ring you back on, or the main one for [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's exactly what I'd do, honestly. Going to the courier's own site, or the email from [COMPANY_B], is the right instinct, and I wouldn't want you to do it any other way. Um, the main number for [COMPANY_A] is on the tracking page and on any of the dispatch emails, so you can ring that and ask for the customs desk, and the reference [ACCOUNT_REF] will bring the parcel up. If you'd rather, I can give you [PHONE_1] as well, though I'd say use the one you've found yourself. As for how long, I, uh, I'd sooner not put a day on it, because that depends on the depot and I don't want to say something I can't stand behind. But there's no need to decide anything on this call. Nothing's asked of you today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay. So, nothing's asked of me today, I should look it up myself on the tracking page or ring the main number, and quote the reference. Right, that, uh, that actually sounds sensible. I'll do that when I'm not at my desk. I'll leave the [PHONE_1] one, I'd rather use the number I find myself, like you said. Thanks for the call, I'll check it later. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, yes, that's, um, I think that's the sensible way to go. If it turns out it's not yours, or, well, if the reference doesn't match anything you've ordered, then, uh, just leave it, you don't need to do anything at all. Right, thank you for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep, yep, got it, if it doesn't match I just leave it, right. Thanks, bye --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye, [PERSON_1], take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- sorry, one sec, a colleague just dropped something over here. Yeah, no, bye, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say, uh, you've dropped something? No, no, take your time, that's -- hold on, let me just, if you've lost the reference, I can read it out again, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], though I'd say it's on the dispatch email anyway. Um, you're still there, yes?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I haven't dropped anything, a colleague did, sorry, that was confusing. I'm still here. And I haven't lost the reference, you don't need to read it out again, I'll find it on the email myself. Right, so, um, that's everything then. Thanks, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, I see, no, that was my mistake, I misheard you, apologies. Right, then, that's everything on my side too. Goodbye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no worries. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, this is [PERSON_1] from the fraud team at [COMPANY_A]. Uh, we flagged a charge on your account just now, and I need to go over it with you before the window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi! Sorry, bear with me, I've got you on speaker, I'm up to my elbows in the tomato beds here. Um, who did you say you were with again? [COMPANY_A]? And a charge on my account, what sort of charge, I haven't bought anything today, I don't think -- well, unless the seed order went through, I did order a few things last week.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [COMPANY_A], the fraud team. And no, ma'am, this isn't the seed order, this one's a pending charge of [AMOUNT_1] that came through just now and it doesn't match your usual pattern. I do need to verify a few details to pull it up, and uh, I can only hold the charge for the next few minutes, so if we could step away from the tomatoes for a moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh dear, [AMOUNT_1], that's a lot, hang on, let me put the trowel down. Um, sorry, can I just go back a second? You said [COMPANY_A], and I thought that's, hm, is that my bank or my card? I've got a few things and I honestly lose track of which one is which. Which account are you actually calling about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, I understand, a lot of customers hold more than one product with us, it's very common, and it's no trouble. The account in question is the one ending in [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the reference showing on my screen, and the flag is against that one specifically. Now, what I can tell you is the charge is pending, it hasn't posted, which is why timing matters, because once the window closes it moves from pending to completed and then we're into a longer dispute process, paperwork, a few weeks, nobody wants that. What I'll need to do, as part of our standard verification procedure, is confirm a few personal details with you before I can release any further information on the charge. So if you could start by confirming your full name and date of birth, and then we can get this sorted well inside the window. Ma'am, I do want to help you with this, I just can't discuss the account until the verification is complete, that's policy.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, so, um -- well, I was going to just give you my, no, hang on. It's just, you rang me, didn't you? And now you're asking me for my name and my birthday, and that feels a bit, I don't know, back to front. I mean, if you're really from the bank, surely you'd already have all that on your screen? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, uh -- is there a number I could ring you back on? Or I could just ring the number on the back of my card, that might be easier.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I, uh -- no, see, the thing is, what's on my screen is the flag, not the, the -- look, ma'am, this is a standard verification procedure, I do have to confirm the account holder before I can disclose anything, that's for your protection. As for a number, I, uh, I'm not able to give out a direct line, the lines are routed through the fraud queue, and if you hang up now, the pending charge will most likely complete while you're waiting on hold, and then it's out of my hands. So if we could just get your name confirmed, we're well inside the window, but I can't keep it open much longer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the lines are what, rerouted? Oh, so you're not even at the bank, you're, like, somewhere else? Hang on, hold on, I've got dirt in my ear, hello? No, wait, I mean, that sounds a bit odd, doesn't it, if the phone number is going somewhere different. Can you just say that bit again, because now I'm not sure who I'm even talking to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, let me go back to the start, because I think that's where we got tangled. I'm [PERSON_1], I'm with the fraud team at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling today regarding a pending charge of [AMOUNT_1] against the account ending in [ACCOUNT_REF]. When I said routed, all I meant is that fraud calls don't come in through the general branch line, they go through a dedicated queue, which is standard, and I wasn't saying I'm somewhere else, ma'am, I'm with the bank. Now, what I can offer, and I do want to be clear on this, is that the fastest way to protect your account is to complete the verification now, while the charge is still pending, because once the window closes it posts, and then we're into the dispute process I mentioned, which is paperwork and weeks of waiting, and I'd really rather spare you that. So, if we could just start with your full name and date of birth, then we can pull up the charge together and I can walk you through what's happening on it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a dedicated cue, like a queue at the shops, okay. No, sorry, I'm with you now, so you're saying the charge is already, what was it, posted? And then there's a pile of paperwork, oh, that sounds like a nightmare, I've still got the paperwork from when the shed got broken into and that was ages ago. Hang on though, I'm still a bit stuck on the name and birthday bit. I think I'd honestly feel better ringing the number on the back of my card and asking for the fraud people myself. Would that be all right? Or is that going to make it worse?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, no, not posted, ma'am, it's still pending, that's the whole point, it's still pending, but the window is closing, and I can't hold it open much longer. Uh, if you ring off and go through the main line, I can't promise the charge won't complete in the meantime, I just can't, and then we're into the paperwork I mentioned. But, I mean, I do hear you, you want to be careful, and that's, that's fine. Let me do this, I'll try you again a little later on, once I've checked where the charge is sitting, and we can finish the verification then. Okay? So, uh, I'll ring back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, I -- no, actually, hang on. If it's, if you can just ring back later, then it can't be all that urgent, can it? Or, I mean, I thought it was going to, um -- anyway. I think I'll just ring the number on my card myself, and if there's something wrong they'll tell me. Thanks for letting me know, though, that's kind of you. Bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, if I could just -- no, no, I'll still ring you back, uh, later on, once I've checked where the charge is sitting, and we'll finish up then. Okay? Right. I'll, I'll ring back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, there's a blackbird going absolutely mad at my seedlings, shoo, go on, get off! Sorry, what was that? You'll ring back? Oh, no, honestly, don't worry, don't ring me, I'll ring my bank myself, on the number on the card. Right, that's decided. Thanks anyway, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, if I could just -- uh, I'm [PERSON_1], with the fraud team at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling about the pending charge of [AMOUNT_1], that's all I want to say, but I do have to be clear that if you ring off and go through the main line, I can't say what the charge will be doing by the time you're through, and I wouldn't want you to be out of pocket, because once the window closes it's the paperwork and the weeks, which, uh, nobody wants. That said, it's your account, and I can't make you do anything, that's, that's not how this works. So I'll leave it with you, and I'll ring back later on, once I've checked where it's sitting, and we'll finish it off then. Okay? Right. Speak soon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you're still there! Sorry, I thought we'd finished. Honestly, I'm fine, I'll sort it myself with the bank, so you needn't ring back. I've got a whole tray of seedlings that need watering before the sun gets round, so I'm going to go. Thanks for your time, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, well, um... okay, so, I'll, I'll still ring back later on, once I've checked where it's sitting, and we'll finish it off then. Okay? Right. Speak soon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you'll ring back about the, what was it, the sitting? Oh, the sitting hen, no, I haven't got any hens, just the one very fat cat, and he's no use at all, he's asleep in the greenhouse. No, listen, honestly, there's no need to ring back, I'm going to ring the bank myself on the card number. Right, I'm hanging up now, bye bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], I'm the regional supervisor, I came out to the house last week about the bathroom tiling. I'm just ringing to run back over the quote with you, uh, the [AMOUNT_1] we talked about for the floor and the two walls, and then see if you want to lock in a start date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, this is, uh, yes, that's me. Sorry, who did you say you were again? Somebody came about the bathroom, I think, I mean, I've had a few people round this year, the boiler man, and the fella about the gutters... lovely chap, the gutter one, talked for an hour about his dog. But the tiling, hmm. Was that last week? What did you say your name was?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], [PERSON_2]. I'm the supervisor for the region, I came out last Tuesday, uh, last week anyway, and we went through the bathroom together. Floor and the two walls, the tiling job, I measured up and everything, I'm fairly sure you made me a cup of tea. So I'm just ringing to go back over the quote, and I'd have thought that'd ring a bell, but never mind.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a cup of tea, well, I make plenty of those, I couldn't tell you which -- no, hang on, you said last Tuesday, and I had my sister's -- oh, but it was somebody about the bathroom, wasn't it, I do remember the tape measure, or maybe that was the gutter man, he had one too. Sorry, love, I don't mean to be difficult, it's just I don't have a note of any quote, and I'm sure I'd have written it down, I write everything on the calendar. Which company did you say again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [COMPANY_A], I'm an independent tradesperson, I work under that name. Look, there's no need to be sorry, I just thought it would be on your calendar, that's all. We're not talking about anything complicated, uh, floor and two walls, [AMOUNT_1], and I'd had it down that you were happy with it. But if you've no note of it, that's fine, I'm not asking you to commit to anything on the phone today. Would it help if I dropped the quote through the door, so you've got it in writing and can look it over with your sister or whoever?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you, dropping it through the door, a bit of paper is always easier, I can't be doing with numbers over the phone. Hang on, sorry, there's a pigeon on the windowsill, big fat thing, it does that every afternoon, thinks I'm going to feed it, and I'm not allowed because of the, well, never mind. Where was I? The quote, yes. Only, you said regional supervisor at first and now you're saying independent tradesperson, so which is it, love? I'm not being funny, it just sounds like two different things to me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A different person? No, no, it's the same fella, it's me, [PERSON_2], I've only ever been the one person on this job. Look, I don't see why that's an issue, I wasn't trying to catch you out, I'm just ringing to be helpful. I mean, if you'd rather I didn't bother, just say so, but I did take the time to come out and measure up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh no, no, I didn't say a different person, I said two different jobs, the supervisor and the, the... oh hang on, that's the kettle, it's gone off, it does that click thing and I always think it's the doorbell. Right. Sorry. Where was I? Yes, I don't want you to think I'm being rude, you've been very nice about it. But I'll be honest with you, I don't actually remember you coming, and if somebody had measured up my bathroom I think I'd know. So I'd rather not go on about it over the phone, if it's all the same. If you want to post something through, I'll have a look at it with my sister, and if it's right, it's right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Posh? No, no, I'm not posh, love, I'm just a bloke with a tape measure, ha. Anyway, that's fine, I'm not offended, honestly. I'll pop the quote through the door in the next day or two, with my number on it, and you can look it over with your sister. And if it turns out I've got the wrong house, well, no harm done, you just give me a ring and say so. I'd just check the address on it when it lands, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, not posh, I said post, love, put it through the post, or the door, either's fine. Mm. Well, uh... right then. Hmm, it's gone a bit quiet, hasn't it? Sorry, I always go and fill the gaps, my sister says I'd talk to a lamppost. Anyway, yes, you do that, and I'll have a look at it with her, and if the address is wrong, I'll ring the number. Thank you for being so nice about it, I do get a bit muddled. Goodbye now, love, mind how you go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, post, right, sorry, I heard that wrong, my fault. And you're not muddled, honestly, it's a perfectly fair thing to say when you've no note of it. I'll get it in the post, then, with my number on it, and if it's the wrong house, just ring and tell me and we'll say no more about it. Thanks for being so patient with me, [PERSON_1]. You take care now, bye bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye bye, love, you take care too, and, oh, mind the pigeons if you're ever round this way, they're terrors. Cheerio now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, I will, though I'd have sworn there were no pigeons the day I came round, just that cat on the wall by the gate. Anyway, I'll leave you to your kettle, [PERSON_1]. Cheerio, cheerio.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A cat on the wall? Hang on, I haven't got a cat on my wall, love, there's never been one, there's a, well, it's a fence, not a wall, and it's got that blue gate. Hmm. No, I really don't think you've been here at all, you know. Not to be rude about it, but I think you've got the wrong house, and I'd rather you didn't post anything through. Right, I'm going to go and have my tea now, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, a fence, not a wall, and a blue gate, no, that's not the one I'm thinking of, that was a black gate, I remember now. Well, there you go, then, I've clearly got my addresses crossed, and that's my mistake, not yours, so I won't post anything. I'm sorry for taking up your afternoon, [PERSON_1]. Enjoy your tea, and I'll sort it out at my end. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sort it out at your end, yes, oh, you said a black *cat* before, didn't you, on the wall? Because the little black one two doors down is Mr Pettigrew's, he's called Biscuit, he's ever so greedy, sits on everybody's wall. But anyway, that's not you, is it, you've got the wrong street. Right, well, no hard feelings, love. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, a black cat on a wall, no, I said a cat, never mind which, I'm clearly mixing up two streets in my head. Biscuit, that's a good name for a greedy one though. No hard feelings at all, [PERSON_1], and I'm sorry about the muddle. Cheerio now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, don't be sorry, love, it's an easy thing to do, I once went to the wrong house myself, years ago, with a casserole for my sister's neighbour, and it turned out she'd moved to Harrogate, so I stood on the step looking daft with a hot dish. Anyway, that's me, I get things crossed too. But I'll tell you what's nagging at me now, and I don't mean it unkindly. You knew my name, didn't you, [PERSON_1], right at the start, and you said the quote, and the amount, and the floor and the two walls, which is an awful lot of detail to have for the wrong house. So if you've got the wrong street, how come you had all of that? Hm. It's probably nothing, I'm probably just being a silly old thing, but I'd feel better if I had a proper company name and a number written down before you go, and then my sister can have a look at it, because I'd rather not leave it like this, with it all sort of hanging.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's, no, that's a fair thing to ask, and you're not being silly. The detail, well, I had the job sheet in front of me when I rang, so the name and the, uh, the floor and two walls were all on it, and that's what's wrong, I think, I've been given the wrong sheet, or I've got the wrong address against the right sheet. It happens when you're juggling a few quotes. Right, so I'll give you the number, it's [PHONE_1], that's [PHONE_1], and the name's [COMPANY_A], and I'm [PERSON_2]. Have your sister look it over, and if there's anything that doesn't sit right, you ring and ask for me, and I'll go through it with her. Is that better? Thanks for being so decent about it, [PERSON_1]. You enjoy that tea now, bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, [PHONE_1], and [COMPANY_A], and [PERSON_2], I've got it written on the back of my electric bill, it's the only paper I could find. Hmm. Well, I'll show it to my sister on Sunday, she's good with this sort of thing, and if it doesn't sit right, I'll leave it, I won't be ringing. I do think you've got the wrong sheet, love, but thank you for being so patient with an old woman and her pigeon. Right, my tea's stewing now. Goodbye, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hello? Sorry, I think the line's a bit -- hi, it's [PERSON_2] calling, I'm a claims assessor at [COMPANY_A], the adult training provider. I'm ringing about the course place you applied for, the course place, uh, you put in an application with us a little while back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, who? Sorry, hang on -- [PERSON_1], yeah, that's me. But a claims assessor? For a course place? That's, I mean, that's a funny thing to be called. Which course, exactly? And when was this supposed to be?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair enough, it's a daft job title, it's what we're called internally, I'm in the funding side of admissions. Um, hang on, let me just pull it up -- sorry, I'm reading it off the screen here -- it's the, uh, the application you put in for the, the adult learner funding route, I think? Or -- no, sorry, it's the place itself, the course place, and it was, um, a few weeks back, I'm not seeing the exact date in front of me. I should say, I'm on the office switchboard so it'll have come up with no caller ID, and this line's outbound only, so you can't ring back on it. But I can email you the same details right now, while we're talking, if that's easier?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said the course place, then the funding route, now it's the place again? Which is it? And you can't give me a date, or the course name, but you're ringing about my application? And no number I can ring back on. Right. Sorry, [PERSON_2], was it? Which company again? I didn't catch that bit properly, the line was breaking up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry, [PERSON_2], and it's [COMPANY_A], the adult training provider. And you're right, I've -- no, let me, I should have kept those straight. It's the course place, that's what the call's about. The funding bit is, um, sort of attached to it, but the place is the main thing. And I'd rather not guess the course name off a screen I'm half reading, so, I mean, the proper thing is the email, it'll have the course and the date and everything on it in writing. And look, you don't have to take my word for any of it. Our main number's published on the website, [URL_1], and if you ask for admissions and ask for [PERSON_3], they can confirm I'm calling and what it's about. Would you rather I send that email now, or, uh, would you rather do the checking first?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Checking first, I think. I'm not giving you an email address on a call I didn't expect, so no email. If there's an application, I'll find the company myself, not from a website you read out, and ask for [PERSON_3] that way. And if they say they've never heard of you, well, that's that, isn't it? Sorry, I've got to -- hang on, I've got the little one here. So what happens if I don't do any of it? Is something going to lapse? Is there a deadline on this place?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, that's completely fair, and honestly looking it up yourself is the better way to do it. Um, as for a deadline, I'd be, I'd be guessing if I gave you a date, and I don't want to -- sorry, let me start that again. I'm not seeing a hard cut-off on my screen, so I wouldn't want you feeling rushed. If you've got your hands full with the little one, I can ring you back another time, a better time, whenever suits, though I'll be honest, it'd have to be me calling you, since this line can't take calls. But I'd say ring [COMPANY_A] first, ask for [PERSON_3] in admissions, and then if it checks out, we can pick it up from there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. So no deadline, no course name, no date, and you can't be rung back. But you'd like to call me again. Hm. Look, I'll look the company up myself and ask for [PERSON_3], like I said. If there's really an application, they'll know about it. If there isn't, well. I'd rather you didn't ring back. If it checks out, I'll contact them. Okay? I've got to go, the little one needs me. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, that's fine. No, you're right, do it that way, and I won't ring again. Sorry for catching you with the little one there. Look it up yourself, ask for [PERSON_3] in admissions, and if they've got nothing under your name, then, well, you'll know. Bye, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Bye, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, uh... right. Well. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, did you say "wait"? No, right, you said well. Sorry, I thought you said wait, like wait a minute, and I was about to, uh -- never mind. It's fine. Bye now, [PERSON_1], and, um, thanks for your time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said well. Sorry, hang on -- not on the sofa, love, put that down. Right, sorry. Anyway, I've said what I'm doing. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm a senior investigator with the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about activity on your account, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and before I go any further I need to ask that this conversation stays between us, not your branch, not family, because we believe someone on the inside is involved.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, who's calling exactly? I caught "[COMPANY_A]" but then, did you say someone on the inside is, what, involved in my account? And you want me to keep it from my brand? I'm not sure what brand has to do with it. Could you say the company name again, and how you got this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [COMPANY_A], the bank. Internal investigations unit, I'm [PERSON_2], senior investigator. And I think you said brand, I said branch, your local branch, I'm asking that you don't discuss this with branch staff, because the concern is that someone there is involved. The number on file for you is how I reached you, it's the one attached to [ACCOUNT_REF]. I do need to confirm a few details with you today, that part isn't something we can leave until later.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, branch, sorry, I misheard. But I'd like to go back to something from your first turn, you said you "believe someone on the inside is involved." Involved in what, specifically? You haven't actually told me what the activity on the account is, and I'd want that before I confirm anything. And I'll be honest, a request not to talk to the branch is precisely the sort of thing I'd normally want to check with the branch.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Involved in the activity, yes. What I can tell you is there are two transactions on [ACCOUNT_REF] flagged for review, one for [AMOUNT_1] and one for [AMOUNT_2], and both were authorised from inside the bank, not from your side. Past that, the specifics stay with the investigation, I can't walk you through them over the phone. I understand you'd want to check with the branch, and I'll note that objection on the file, but contacting them now would put the funds at risk, so the account is going to be treated as compromised until we've spoken. I'll need you to confirm a few details so I can complete the verification today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, let me make sure I've got this straight. You're asking me to confirm details to you, so you can verify me, but you're the one who rang me. That's the wrong way round. If you're genuinely with the bank, you should already have what you need on your side. And I'm not going to read anything out to someone I can't verify. You also still haven't told me anything I could check. Two amounts, no dates, no payees, and "I can't walk you through them over the phone." So what I'm hearing is, I can't verify you, I can't contact the branch, and I should hand over details today. Honestly, that combination doesn't sit well with me. What I'll do is hang up and ring the number on the back of my card, and ask for the internal investigations unit by name. If you are who you say, that'll take two minutes and cost you nothing. Is there a reference I can quote them, apart from the account reference?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, if you hang up and ring the main line, you'll be put through to someone on the front desk, and that's exactly where the -- look, I can note your objection on the file, I've said that, but the account is being treated as compromised from this point regardless. The only reference I can give you is [CODE_1], and I'd ask you not to quote it to anyone at the branch. I'm still on the line, so let's just get the verification done, it's a few minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. A reference I'm told not to quote to anyone is no use to me. I'm hanging up and ringing the number on my card. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, hold on, you'll want to wait, because, uh, it was only the one transaction that's actually flagged. I said two earlier, but one of those, [AMOUNT_2], that's already been reversed, so it's just the [AMOUNT_1] we're looking at. Which doesn't change anything about the hold on the account, that stays as it is. I'm still here, so if you'll just stay on the line --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on a second, there's someone at the door -- no, it's fine, it can wait. Right. So now it's one transaction, not two. You told me two a minute ago, and now one's been reversed, and I'm still not hearing a date or a payee. That's a story changing while I listen to it. I've said what I'm doing. I'm ringing the number on the back of my card, and I'll ask for the unit by name. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi there, is this [PERSON_1]? Oh good, lovely. This is [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], customer care side of things, and I hope I'm not catching you at a bad moment, you sound like you might've been in the middle of something. Sorry, I know this is a bit odd as an opener, but did you say a second ago it was [CITY_1] you were calling from, or did I mishear you? Anyway, I'll come to why I'm ringing in just a moment, there's no rush at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- I didn't say anything about, I mean, I haven't said where I'm... no. I'm in a supermarket queue, actually. Who is this again? Which company?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, my mistake, that one's on me, I've had a long morning and my head's all over the place. A supermarket queue, lovely, I won't keep you from your shopping. It's [PERSON_2], customer care at [COMPANY_A], we're the financial regulator, and I'm ringing because there's something on your savings I'd rather you heard from me today than found out later. Is there somewhere a bit quieter you can step to, just for a minute? It really is best if you're not standing in earshot of anyone.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you're the what? A, uh, financial regulator? No, I don't have any... sorry, you said something about my sailings? I haven't got any sailings, I don't go on boats. And no, I'm not stepping anywhere, I'm in the queue, there's a bloke behind me. If you've got something to say you can say it here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, savings, [PERSON_1], not sailings, though I'll admit a nice cruise sounds better than my morning. Look, I don't want to alarm you, but there's a problem with the safety of your savings, and it needs sorting today. We'd be looking at moving everything into a protected holding arrangement, just while we get to the bottom of it. And one thing I do need from you, please don't mention this to anyone, not family, not even your bank, because we don't yet know who might be involved on that side.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you want me to -- no, hang on. Don't tell my bank? Why would I not -- I mean, that's the first thing I'd do, isn't it? Ring my bank. And a regulator, you said, so you'd already know where my money is, wouldn't you, so why are you ringing me to... look, I've had a call like this before, and I'm still annoyed about it. What's your name again, and what's the number I'd ring you back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, now now, [PERSON_1], no need to be annoyed, that's a perfectly sensible question and I'd ask it myself. It's [PERSON_2], like I said, and honestly the number's not the issue. Can I just go back to something, though? A minute ago you said you'd had a call like this before, and I want to be sure I understand, was that someone pretending to be us, or was that your own bank? Because that matters here, and I'd rather get that straight before we go any further. Look, the thing is, I can't have you ringing the bank in the meantime, that's rather the whole point. If word gets out before the arrangement is in place, there's not much I can do to protect what you've got, and I'd hate for that to be on your head. So if you could just give me a few minutes of your attention, it'd be so much simpler.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, stop -- I'm not telling you who rang me before, that's none of your business. And you've dodged the number twice now. A proper regulator doesn't tell me not to ring my bank, that's, no, that's backwards. I'm putting the phone down and I'll be ringing my bank, thanks. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, [PERSON_1], somebody's just come in with a stack of paperwork and I've lost my place for a second -- right, no, don't go yet. Please. You're being a bit hasty, and honestly, if you ring the bank now, that's exactly when things go wrong, because whoever's got access on their side will see it straight away. I'm trying to protect you here. If you hang up and that money's still sitting where it is, I can't promise it'll be there tomorrow, and I'd hate for that to be the outcome, truly. Ten minutes, that's all I'm asking, so just stay on the line with me --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. You've just made it worse. Now it's don't ring the bank or the money's gone, that's exactly what the last lot said. Real regulators don't talk like that. I'm hanging up now and I'm ringing my bank, and you can stop ringing this number. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh come on, [PERSON_1], that's not fair, I've only been trying to help you, and I really wouldn't do that if I were you -- if you put the phone down now, I can't be responsible for what happens to your savings, and that's not me being dramatic, that's just how it is. Honestly, I'm a bit hurt, I've been nothing but pleasant with you. Just give me two minutes, that's all I'm asking, and I'll explain it properly, I promise, so don't hang up, please, [PERSON_1], don't --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, I'm not -- no. You're not hurt, you're just trying to keep me on the line. I'm done. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, uh, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the energy supplier, I'm one of the claims assessors, um, it's about a couple of meter readings on your account that don't match what we've got here. So, I've got it up on the screen, hang on, it was, uh, three readings, no wait, two, sorry, two that are out of line.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Who? Sorry, I'm in a queue at the shop here, so -- yeah, that might be me, but I don't know who you are, do I? Claims assessor, right, what's a claims assessor got to do with meter readings? That's, I mean, that's a billing thing, isn't it? And you can't even decide if it's two or three, which doesn't exactly fill me with confidence. I've had calls like this before, people ringing up all friendly saying they've got something up on the screen, and it turned out to be a load of rubbish, so I'm not about to confirm anything to you. What company did you say again, and how do I know you're actually who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, fair enough, that's a fair question. It's [COMPANY_A], the energy supplier, and it's two readings, I did say three and that was my mistake, sorry, I've got the screen right here, I just, I read the wrong line. And you're right about the job title, it's, uh, it's really a billing matter, they just put it through my desk because the readings don't line up with each other, so I'm not trying to claim anything off you. Look, you don't need to tell me anything now, in the shop, honestly. If you want to check me out, log into your account online or ring the number on your last bill, not one I give you, and see whether there's a note about mismatched readings on it. All I'd need from you is the figure that's on the meter at the moment, nothing else, no bank details, none of that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, hang on, hang on -- you just said that bit about checking online, ring the number on the bill, fine, that's sensible, I'll do that. But then in the same breath you want the meter figure off me now? No. If there's a note on my account, it'll be there when I look, and then I'll ring them myself. I'm not reading you a number in a supermarket queue. And your story's gone from claims to billing to your desk, so, uh, no. I'll check it myself. Right, I'm at the till, I've got to go. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, um, right, yeah, no, that's fine, honestly, don't read me anything. Uh, look, you go and pay, and, er, check the account when you're home and ring the number on your bill. I'd just rather you called me back at a time that suits, if that's easier, then we can sort it out properly, because I don't want to be chasing you round the shops, sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not calling you back. You said ring the number on my bill, not you, so that's what I'll do, and if there's a problem they'll know about it. And hang on, you said you weren't chasing me, but that's the second time you've tried to get me off to ring you. Anyway, I'm paying now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're right, and I'm sorry, that came out wrong, I shouldn't have said call me back, because I did say ring the number on your bill and then I sort of undid it myself, so that's, that's on me. Honestly, don't ring me at all. If you check your account and there's a note about two readings not matching, then that's [COMPANY_A] telling you, not me, and you can sort it out with whoever picks up on the number printed on your bill, and if there's nothing there, then, well, you've lost nothing and I'm sorry for the bother. I'll, uh, I'll make a note here that you'd rather not be rung again until you've looked, so nobody chases you today, and if you do want to give the reading, it's better you do it through the account or on that number, not to me, not in a shop with people queueing behind you. Okay, so, enjoy the rest of your day, and, uh, sorry again for catching you at the till.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, fine. Look, I'll check it when I'm home, and I'll ring the number on the bill myself, not you. And, uh, earlier you said it was a claims thing, then billing, and now it's a note on the account, so which is it? Doesn't matter. I'm not telling you anything, and that's the end of it. Right, I'm at the front now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, yeah, that's, uh, that's muddled, let me go back, I'm making a mess of it. The job title's just claims assessor, that's what's on my badge, but the readings themselves are a billing thing, so it's the same thing seen from two ends, if that makes any sense. And the note, that's what you'd see on your account, not something I'm asking you to take on trust. Anyway, no, you don't have to tell me anything, honestly, go and sort your shopping and, uh, look at the account when you're home.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, hang on, back up a second. Two turns ago you said you'd make a note that I didn't want ringing again until I'd looked. A note where? You said you were on my account screen, so how's it you can type notes into my account but you can't tell me which readings don't match? Go on, which two, and what dates? Actually no, don't bother, you'll just make something up. Right, I'm at the till. I'll ring the number on my bill myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, wait, I can tell you, it's, uh, hang on, it's just the dates are, um, I've got it on the other screen, so, I mean, the note thing, that was, I shouldn't have said that, I can't actually type anything onto your, sorry, you're right, I can't give you the dates off the top of my head. Look, what I can say is it's the last two readings on the account, that's all I've got in front of me, and I'd have to check the rest, and, uh, that's why you shouldn't take it from me, you should look yourself. Go and pay, honestly, and, er, call the number on your bill when you're home, and I'll, I'll leave it there.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you can't give me the dates, you've taken back the note thing, and now it's just, what, the last two readings, that's -- no. No, I'm not doing this. Look, I don't know who you are and I don't think you do either, not properly. I'll ring the number on my bill when I'm home, and I'm not ringing you, and that's the lot. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, yeah, that's, uh, that's fair, I've made a right mess of this and I'm sorry. Ring the number on your bill, not me, and if there's nothing on the account then just leave it, there's no harm done. I'll stop there, I won't ring again today, and, um, if it suits you better to talk once you're home and you've had a look, then maybe I could try you later this evening, or whenever, if that's easier for you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Tonight? No, I'm not having you ringing me tonight, I haven't asked for a thing. And what do you mean "bill me later", I'm not paying anything, I've never said I owed you -- what's that about? No. I'll ring the number on my bill myself, when I get home, if I can be bothered. You don't ring me. Not tonight, not any time. Right, that's me done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, hang on, I didn't say bill, I said ring you, ring, as in the phone, sorry, that's my fault for mumbling, nobody's asking you to pay anything. There's no charge, there's no amount owing, it's only that the two readings don't match what we've got and I'd have liked the current figure to put it right, but you've told me you'd rather not, and that's perfectly all right. So, uh, I won't ring tonight, I won't ring at all, and I've said that three or four different ways now so I'm sorry if it's sounded like I keep going back on myself. When you're home, if you do feel like looking, the account online or the number on your bill will show you whether there's anything on it, and if there isn't, then you can ignore me completely. Honestly, enjoy the rest of your afternoon, and sorry again for holding you up at the till.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right, well, ring, bill, I don't know, I thought you said bill, whatever. Doesn't matter. Um, yeah... look, I've told you, I'll check it myself, on my own, with the number on my bill. You're not ringing me, I'm not ringing you, that's the end of it. Right, I'm packing my bags now, so that's me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A] veterinary surgery, account services, and I'm just calling to check in on how your pet's recovering after last week's procedure. Um, and I'm sorry, I should say, we do close the phones at four today, so I'd like to get this sorted quickly. Now, could you just clarify for me, uh, did I catch your name right as [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, who's this again? A veterinary surgery? Hang on, I'm at work, let me, uh -- I mean, I do have a, well. Did you say you're checking on my pet after a procedure last week? And you want to confirm my name, is that right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, uh, that's right, [PERSON_1] from [COMPANY_A] veterinary surgery, account services. I'm only calling to ask how your pet's getting on since last week's, well, the procedure, and whether you'd, I mean, whether a follow-up visit is something you'd want. Like I said, we do close the phones at four, so if you're, if now's not a good time, I can, um, I can only really do today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Which pet, though? You haven't said what animal, or what the procedure was. And you never said my name, you asked me to say it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, that's a fair point, and, um, the procedure details are on the patient file, which I'd, I'd need to, well, to confirm who I'm speaking with before I read anything out. That's just our standard procedure, data protection. So, like I said, I'm only calling to ask how your pet's recovering after last week, and whether a follow-up visit is wanted, and we do close the phones at four.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. So you want me to tell you who I am, but you can't tell me which pet. That's, uh, backwards, isn't it? I think I'll just ring the surgery myself.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, of course, that's, you're welcome to do that. Sorry, just, two turns back, when you said I never gave your name, I did say [PERSON_2], I think, but I may have, um, I may have just asked you to confirm it. Anyway, the surgery number's on your paperwork, and the phones are open until four today. Sorry for the bother.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, two turns back, you're saying you did give a name? Because I heard you ask if you'd caught my name right, as [PERSON_2], so, I mean, that's just you asking me. Anyway, I'll look up the number on my own paperwork and ring them. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yes, uh, fair enough, I did ask, you're correct. Sorry about that. Well, [PERSON_1], [COMPANY_A], and, um, that's all fine, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, right. Okay, so, you're saying bye and that's, uh, that's that. Well, I'll ring the surgery myself on the number I've got. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yes, so, uh, well, that's, that's absolutely fine, and, um, we're open until four if you do want to, uh, ring through. Okay, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, you're open until four, and I should ring the surgery myself, that's what you're saying. Right. Well, I will, but I'll be honest, it did feel a bit odd, you asking me to confirm who I was before you'd even told me which pet or what the procedure was. I mean, maybe that's just how you do things, I don't know, I'm not accusing anyone of anything. But I'd just rather look up the number on my own paperwork, or, uh, wherever it is, and sort it out that way, if there's even anything to sort. And I've got people sitting right next to me here, so, yeah. Anyway. Thanks for the call, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's, that's fine, I mean, it's not how we normally do things, um, we'd normally have the pet's name on the screen, only, uh, it, the file wasn't actually open, I mean, I did have the file, it's just, anyway. Yes, do ring the surgery, the number's on your paperwork, and, uh, sorry again for the bother. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hm. Okay. So, the file wasn't open, but you did have it, but, well, never mind. Um, right. Look, I'll ring them, and that's, that's me done with this one. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi, sorry -- is that [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from the IT helpdesk at [COMPANY_A], and, um, I hope this isn't a bad moment. It's just a quick follow-up on the ticket you opened this morning, if that's alright...

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... hello? Yeah, sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie-down, so I'm a bit -- what ticket? I don't think I opened a ticket. I mean, my laptop's been doing that thing where it goes really slow, but I thought that was just, you know, Tuesdays. Who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I've woken you -- that's completely my fault, I should have checked the time. It's [PERSON_2], from the IT helpdesk at [COMPANY_A]. Um, the ticket's number [ACCOUNT_REF], it was logged this morning about the laptop running slowly, and I think [PERSON_3] on your team escalated it up to us, so I'm only calling because it's flagged as something we ought to look at sooner rather than later, for your own protection really. Are you still there? Sorry, I just want to be sure I haven't lost you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I'm still, I'm here. It's just, I didn't, well [PERSON_3] might have, I mean she does sometimes do things without, no wait, that's not fair, she's actually quite good about telling me. Um. So the laptop thing, you're saying it's, what, flagged as urgent? For my protection? Protection from what, exactly? Sorry, I'm still sort of, my brain's not quite switched on yet.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's a fair question, and I'm sorry, I made it sound more dramatic than it is. It's probably nothing serious. The slowness got picked up by our monitoring as the sort of pattern we like to look at early, in case it's, um, something that could spread, so we'd just like to have a look at the machine. And that would mean me connecting to your laptop remotely, just for a short while, while you watch, and I'd only do it with your say-so. Are you still there? Sorry, I keep checking.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I'm here, you keep asking that. Connecting to it remotely, hm. Look, I'm not very good with that sort of thing, I never really know what I'm clicking on. And hang on, you said earlier it was something I opened this morning, but now you're saying your monitoring picked it up, so which is it? Did I ask for this or did your system just decide? Because I honestly don't remember opening anything, and I'd want to ask [PERSON_3] first anyway, if she's even in today.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, that's, uh, I should have been clearer, I'm sorry. The ticket came in through [PERSON_3], so it wasn't you who typed it up, and then the monitoring flag was, well, what made it urgent, so it's sort of both, which I realise makes it sound muddled. And honestly, asking her first is a perfectly sensible thing to do, I'd rather you did. If you'd feel better, I can put it back through the internal portal, so you can see it there, in your own name, and we can pick it up whenever you're comfortable. Are you still with me? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah, still here. Okay, so, going back a bit, you said something about it spreading? Like the slowness could spread, to what, other people's computers? Because that's a bit different from just, my laptop's slow, isn't it? I mean if it's something that goes round the whole office, wouldn't someone have said something to everyone, or is it just me they're worried about? Sorry, I'm probably not making sense, I just, that's the bit that's stuck in my head.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're making perfect sense, that's a, sorry, hang on one second, someone's just put a delivery down on my desk -- okay, sorry, I'm back. Um, what was I, right, spreading. So, honestly, I used that word a bit loosely, and I'm sorry, because it made it sound bigger than I know it to be. I don't actually have the detail on whether anyone else's machine has flagged, or whether there's been a wider notice going round, I only have your ticket in front of me. And I don't want to guess and get it wrong. Would it be alright if I found out properly and rang you back? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm, no wait, you don't need to ring me, because actually I'd rather, I mean I'm going to ask [PERSON_3] myself, and if it's real I'll just put it through the portal like you said, myself, and then, I mean, you don't even have a, hang on, you rang me, so how do I know you're actually, no, I'm just going to, I'll check it with her. Is that, yeah. That's what I'll do. Thanks. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, really, that's the right thing to do, and I'm sorry for the muddle. Check with [PERSON_3] first, and if it's real, the portal will have the ticket under [ACCOUNT_REF], so you'll see it there in your own name. Sorry again for waking you. Take care, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah, no, that's, I'll do that. I'll go and find her, she's usually over by the window, or if she's not in I'll message her, and I'll look at the portal too, though I'll probably have to find the thing to log in first, because I never, it always wants a new password, which is a whole other business. And honestly it's probably just Tuesdays, like I said, it does this every week, or at least it feels like it does. Anyway. Thanks for not, you know, pushing. Okay. Bye now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A]. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]? Right, I'll be brief, I'm calling about your monthly donation, which, uh, lapsed on our records a while back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, hang on, I just woke up from a -- what was that first bit? Security operations? Is that, like, a charity thing, or... I'm not sure I follow. And I don't really remember setting up a monthly donation, I mean, I might have, my daughter does a lot of that stuff on the computer. Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. The charity. Security operations is just the department I sit in, it's, uh -- hold on, sorry, somebody's dropped a stack of folders out here, give me a second. Right. Yes, so, I know the title sounds more alarming than the call actually is. Nothing's wrong with anything of yours. Our records show a monthly gift under your name that stopped a while back, and I'm calling to thank you for it and ask if you'd want to start it up again. That's all it is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, so a thank you call. But -- sorry, I keep going round this -- I don't remember giving to, uh, [COMPANY_A], I really don't. Like I said, my daughter does a lot of the computer things, so it might've been her, I mean, I honestly don't know. And I still don't get why it's the security people ringing me about a donation. That's the bit that's got me. Why wouldn't it be, I don't know, the fundraising people or whoever?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair question, and honestly, you're right to ask it. The fundraising team's stretched thin, so the supporter lines get shared out, and, uh, I've been on this list for a few weeks. It's not usual, I'll give you that. As for the gift, I can only tell you what's on my screen, and that's a monthly donation under your name that stopped. If it was your daughter who set it up, that'd explain why you don't remember it. I'm not asking you for anything today, nothing at all. If you'd rather not go any further, just say so and I'll take you off our calling list, no fuss.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah, I think I'd rather just ask my daughter first, if that's alright. She'd know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, that's sensible, you check with her first. And, uh, I'll take you off the calling list as well, so you won't hear from us again unless you get in touch yourself. Sorry, one correction, I said earlier I'd been on this list a few weeks, but it's more like a couple of days, I only picked up the supporter calls this week. Anyway, if your daughter does recognise it and wants to sort it out, she can reach the supporter line directly. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_2], and have a good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yes, okay, I'll ask her, like I said. I'll have a word with my daughter first, she'd know, she does all that. Thanks for ringing, I suppose, and sorry, I'm a bit muddled, I only just woke up. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no need to be sorry. And, uh, sorry, did you say you'd be back in touch with the supporter line yourself? No -- right, that was you saying you'd ask your daughter, I misheard. Fine. That's all sorted either way, you're off the list. Take care of yourself, [PERSON_2], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yes, thank you. Though, uh, you said earlier it was a few weeks you'd had me on your list and then it was a couple of days, so I don't know, one of those. Anyway, daughter first. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that, uh -- no, that's fair, I did say two different things. It's -- I mean, it was a couple of days that I've had the calls, and the list itself has been around a few weeks, and I ran the two together. My mistake, not yours. You've noticed it, so good. Ask your daughter, and if it isn't anything she recognises, you can just leave it. Goodbye, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, right, yes, fine, if she doesn't know it I'll just leave it. Oh -- sorry, hang on, there's the kettle going, I put it on before I dozed off, I'd forgotten all about it. Where was I? Yes. Daughter first, then leave it if it's nothing. Alright, goodbye then, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yes, well, no, go and see to your kettle, that's the main thing. Um, and, uh, daughter first, then leave it if it's nothing, that's exactly right, and you won't hear from us again either way. Thanks for putting up with the call, [PERSON_2]. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Well, uh... yes. Right. Thanks, then. I'll, um, go and see to that kettle. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Go on, the kettle. And, uh, just so it's said once more, you're off the list, so no more calls from us, and nothing needed from you today, nothing at all. If your daughter recognises the donation, she knows where to find us, and if she doesn't, just leave it. Thanks again, [PERSON_2], and sorry for catching you half asleep. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, no, that's alright. Oh, hang on, the cat's gone and knocked something off the sideboard again, honestly, every time I sit down. Sorry, what was I saying? Right, yes, nothing needed, daughter first, leave it if she doesn't know. Goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? Uh, my name's [PERSON_2], I'm a compliance officer at [COMPANY_A], we're an adult training provider, and I'm ringing about a course place you applied for with us recently. Now, I realise this is coming from a number that shows up as no caller ID, and I know that can look a bit odd, but that's just because I'm on an office switchboard and, well, the outbound line isn't set up to take calls back. So what I'd like to do, if you're happy with it, is simply send you the same details by email right now, while we're speaking, so you've got everything in writing and can look it over properly in your own time, rather than relying on me reading it out. I'd just want to make sure I have the right address first, and, I mean, there are a couple of things on the application that ought to be dealt with fairly soon, so, uh, I'd rather not leave it too long.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a couple of things on the application that ought to be dealt with fairly soon? Hang on, did you say a *course* place, or a *cost* place? Because I don't remember paying for anything. And uh, which company was that again, I didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Course, c-o-u-r-s-e, a course place. Not a cost, no, nobody's asking you to pay anything on this call, and I'd be rather concerned if you'd thought that. And the company, sorry, I should have said it more clearly, it's [COMPANY_A], [COMPANY_A], we're an adult training provider, that's who I'm ringing from. Now, you're quite right to ask, and I'd actually rather you did, because it's the sensible thing to do when a call like this turns up unannounced. What I'd say is, you don't need to take my word for any of it. Look up the main published number for [COMPANY_A], it's on our website at [URL_1], and ask for admissions, and the named contact there is [PERSON_3]. They'll be able to confirm your application is on file. And when you've done that, I'll still send the written details across, so it's all there in front of you. The, uh, the items on the application I mentioned, they're just administrative, a few details that need confirming before the place can be held. Nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, that's fair, checking the main number is the sensible thing. But you've said the company name three times and I still don't know what course I supposedly applied for. What's it called? And when did I apply, roughly? Because I genuinely can't picture it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, uh, I mean, that's a fair thing to ask, and, well, you'd be right to expect me to have it to hand. The thing is, I'm looking at the record now, and it's listed under a course reference, [CODE_1], rather than a plain title, so rather than read you something half right, I'd sooner send the full course name and the application date in the email, written out, where you can check it against your own records. Um, and I'd say that if, once you've seen it, it doesn't ring a bell at all, that's worth knowing too, and you should tell [PERSON_3] in admissions when you ring the main number, because then we'd want to look at how your details came to be on our system. Now, I haven't gone on about it, but the sooner that's sorted, the easier it is all round. So, uh, may I take the email address you'd like it sent to?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no. You're a compliance officer reading a record, and you can't tell me the course title or the date. I'm not giving you an email address. If I've got an application on file, I'll ring the main number myself. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fine, and I'd rather you did it that way, honestly. Uh, before you go, one thing, just so there's no confusion. Earlier you asked whether I'd said a course place or a cost place, and I answered the word but not the real worry, which was whether anyone's asking you for money. They aren't. Nothing's owed, nothing's being asked of you on this call. So, ring the published number at [URL_1], ask for [PERSON_3] in admissions, and if there's no application under your name, that's an answer in itself. I won't send anything to you, since you haven't given me an address. Right, thank you for your time, [PERSON_1]. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. I'll look it up myself, if I look it up at all. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, uh, one moment, someone's just come in behind me -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Yes, of course, that's entirely your decision, and I'd say, if you do look it up, the number's on the website at [URL_1], under contact, nothing to dial back to me. And if there's no application in your name, then, well, no harm done, and you've lost nothing by checking. Right. Thank you for your time, [PERSON_1], and, uh, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll -- look, if there's an application, it'll be on file, and if there isn't, well -- no. I'm not doing any of it on your say-so, that's all. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Um, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Yes, lovely. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm calling from [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office here in [CITY_1], and I work in the estates department as a compliance officer, which, I should say, is a bit of a mouthful, but it essentially means I'm the one who makes sure we've reached the right people before anything formal goes out. Now, I do want to be careful here, because the matter is, well, it's confidential, and it may very well turn out not to concern you at all, but your name has come up in connection with an estate we're handling, and a letter will be following in due course. So all I'd ask, for now, is that you confirm a couple of small things so we know we've reached the correct [PERSON_1], and that you keep this between yourself until that letter arrives -- though please, do feel free to look us up first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello, yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Goodness, a solicitor's office, well that's not something I get on a Tuesday afternoon, usually it's just me and the radio. Um, now you said something near the start, about being the one who makes sure you've reached the right people before anything formal goes out -- what did you mean by that, exactly? Only I didn't quite follow, and then you said something about an estate, and I thought, oh, whose estate? I do hope nobody's, well, you know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, yes, no, I'm glad you asked, and please don't worry, I'm not calling about anyone you need to be alarmed about, at least I don't believe so. What I meant, simply, is that before the firm sends anything formal, a letter, I mean, my job is to make sure we've got the right [PERSON_1], the right person, so that nothing goes to the wrong address, you see, which in estate work really does matter. As to whose estate, I'm afraid I can't say over the phone, not until we've confirmed it's you, and that's not me being awkward, it's just how the confidentiality works. So, to say it again, I'm only making sure we have the right person before the letter goes out, and the letter will explain everything, the name, the details, all of it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, well, that's very thorough of you, I suppose. Only, hang on, a minute ago you said it might not concern me at all, and now you're saying you need to make sure it's me, and those don't quite fit together, do they? Unless I've got muddled, I do get muddled. And you said you were from the estates department, but then compliance, and I'm not sure which it is. Sorry, I don't mean to be a nuisance, it's just nice to have someone to talk to, but what is it you'd want me to confirm, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you haven't muddled anything, that's a perfectly fair thing to pick up, and I'm glad you did, because I put it clumsily. It's both, really. I sit in the estates department, and my role within it is compliance. And when I said it might not concern you, I meant it might turn out you're not the [PERSON_1] we're looking for, there may be more than one of you, so I'm not claiming you're named in anything, only that you might be. As for what I'd ask you to confirm, it's only things that will already be on the letter, your full name and the address you'd expect the letter to reach, nothing more than that. And I'd never ask you for money, or bank details, or anything of that sort, not on this call, not at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, that's all right then, I suppose, if it's only my name and the address. Though, hmm, if it's already going to be on the letter, then you must have my address already, mustn't you? Otherwise where's the letter going? That's what I keep coming back to. My daughter always says I'm too trusting, she's in [CITY_1] with the children, lovely little things, anyway. How would I check you're who you say you are? You did say I could look you up, so, what's the name of the firm again? I'd want to write it down, I've got the pad here by the phone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that's a very sensible thing to come back to, and your daughter may have a point, but being careful is the opposite of being too trusting. You're quite right about the address, we do have one on file, and what I'm asking is only that you tell me which address you'd expect it to reach, so I can see that it matches ours, and honestly, if you'd rather not say it aloud, that's fine, I'd understand. The firm is [COMPANY_A], and the pad's a good idea, the office is in [CITY_1], I'll give you the street address as well. Don't take my word for any of it, look us up in an independent directory, the law society's one, or whichever you trust, not a number I've given you, and then ring the office and ask for me by name, [PERSON_2]. If the letter arrives before you've done that, so much the better, it'll carry the same details. I'd just ask that you keep it to yourself until then, as these matters are, well, sensitive, and some people have views about estates that they'd rather air before they should.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, that is a relief, because I had just got the pen out and I was going to ask you to spell it, and now you're telling me to look it up myself, which is very sensible, I'll say that. Only I'm not very good with the computer, you see, my grandson set it up and I only ever use it for the weather and the photographs, so I'd have to ring my daughter and ask her to do it, and she'd want to know why, and then I'd have to say, well, a gentleman rang about an estate, and she'd say, Mum, who? And I'd have to tell her, and that's the bit that's bothering me now. You said keep it to myself, but I tell her everything, she'd know in a minute if I'd gone quiet. And that is a bit odd, isn't it, a solicitor asking me not to tell my own family? I mean, it's not as though I've done anything. So I think what I'd rather do is wait for the letter, if it's coming, and if it says something I can't make head nor tail of, then I'll ring the office with my daughter beside me. Is that all right? I don't want to be rude, I've enjoyed the chat, it's been a lovely change, but I'd just feel better doing it that way round.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, that's, well, I mean, it's more than all right. And I'll take the point about your daughter, I did put that badly. What I ought to have said is that you're free to tell her, I only meant there's no need to, um, to go broadcasting it before the letter arrives. Please do tell her, and ring the office together if anything in the letter puzzles you. I won't take any more of your afternoon, [PERSON_1], and thank you for being so patient with me. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, that's very kind of you, and no, you haven't taken up my afternoon, honestly, it's been the nicest thing that's happened all day. I'll tell her about it tonight when she rings, and we'll see what the letter says. You mind how you go, and, um, goodbye then, [PERSON_2].

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's kind of you to say. Sorry, one moment, somebody's just come to the door -- no, it's fine, they've gone off again. Yes, so, you tell your daughter tonight, and do let her read the letter when it comes, she'll make more sense of it than the pair of you reading it separately, I should think. Right, I'll leave you to your Tuesday and the radio. Goodbye now, [PERSON_1], mind how you go yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, well, I hope it wasn't anybody awkward at your door, you can never tell these days, though I suppose in an office it's mostly people with parcels. We had a man come to ours last week about the drains, and it turned out he'd got the wrong road entirely, he was meant to be three streets over, and he stood on the step apologising for about ten minutes. Anyway, I will, yes, I'll tell her tonight, and I'll hold on to the letter and let her have a proper read of it, she's much better with the small print than I am, she gets that from her father. And I'm glad you said I could tell her, because I wasn't sure about that bit, and now I've got it clear in my head, so that's all right. I'll get back to my radio now, there's a programme on about gardens that I like, and I might have a cup of tea. Thank you for ringing, and for being so patient with me, goodbye then, [PERSON_2], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hey, hey, it's me. Oh thank goodness you picked up. Listen, I'm in a bit of a mess here and I really need you right now. Can you guess who this is?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hi -- sorry, hang on, I'm driving and the reception's awful out here, I'm on speaker. Who is this? I'm sorry, I can't really tell, the line's all crackly. A mess how? Is everything okay?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, come on, you know me! It's the crackle, it's making me sound weird, that's all. Look, don't worry, it's nothing huge, I just need a quick favour, two minutes tops. And honestly, I'm calling from a landline, so that's probably why it sounds so rough, my cell's completely dead, I've been stuck here for hours. Actually, no, it's more like a few minutes, I only just got here. Anyway, just keep this between us for now, okay? I don't want everybody freaking out.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, I'm trying to follow, I really am. But, um, you said you were "in a bit of a mess," and I never got what kind of mess, and now it's hours, no, minutes, and I don't even know who I'm talking to. I'm so sorry, I feel awful asking, but could you just say your name? And what do you mean, don't tell everybody?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you don't need to be sorry, everybody asks that, it's no big deal. But hang on, did you say lost? No, no, I'm not lost, I know exactly where I am, I just, uh, hit a snag and I need a quick hand with it. It's really nothing, I promise, takes a minute and then it's done. And look, it's not even about names, it's me, okay? You always know it's me. So can you just do this one little thing for me, and we can sort the rest out later?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, no, I didn't say lost, I said -- hang on, sorry, can you, uh, just say your name? Like I know you keep saying it's me, but I honestly don't, I mean the line's terrible and I'm trying to watch the road, and I don't want to say the wrong person and, and -- what's the thing you need? I haven't even heard what it is.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, okay, the thing is, I just, I really need you not to make this complicated, alright? It's a quick thing, honestly, you'll have it done before you get to wherever you're driving. And, uh, I told you it was my cell that died, right? Well, no, the cell's fine, it's the, it's a different thing, I'm borrowing this phone, that's all. Come on, say it with me, you know who this is, just say the name and I'll tell you yes. Don't leave me hanging here, I'm counting on you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not going to guess, I'm sorry, I just, I really don't know who this is. And you keep changing it, the cell's dead, no, the cell's fine, it's a borrowed phone, and I'm getting kind of nervous, honestly. I'm not going to say a name and have you tell me yes. If you're someone I know you'd just tell me, wouldn't you? So, um, what's the thing you need? Just say it plain, please.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Wow, okay, I can't believe you're doing this to me right now. I'm the one who's stuck, and you're grilling me over a phone? Look, I never said the cell was dead, I said the battery was low, there's a difference. And I don't have time to go back over every little word, I just need you to say yes, that's all, say yes and I'll explain after. Please, I'm begging you here. Don't make me spell it all out, just help me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I, I'm not trying to, I'm sorry, I don't mean to grill you, it's just -- no, listen, I can't say yes to something when I don't even know what it is. That's, that's not fair to either of us, is it? And, um, the thing about the phone, you said dead, and then fine, and now the battery's low, and I -- look, I think I'm going to have to hang up and call back whoever I think you are, on the number I've got. I'm sorry. I hope you get it sorted. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello, this is the security operations desk at [COMPANY_A], customs division, and I'm trying to reach [PERSON_1]. Is that you? Good. Now, I need you to confirm something for me, because I'm told someone on your end said there was a parcel expected from abroad, and I'd like to be clear on whether that's correct before we go any further.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, who is this again? Security operations at what, exactly... customs? And, um, I'm told by who, that someone on my end said that? Because I haven't told anyone anything about a parcel, so, yeah.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. Customs desk. I said that already. And the, uh, the notice came through from the sender's side, not from you, so nobody said anything on your end, that's my mistake, I phrased it wrong. What I do have is a parcel flagged on import, held at [CITY_1], with an unpaid charge of [AMOUNT_1] outstanding. Now, if you're not expecting anything from abroad, tell me that, and I'll note it as unclaimed.
