utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So first it's something I said, and now it's something the sender said. Which is it? And you've told me the company name, sure, but that's just a placeholder to me, I don't have a name for you, or a case number, or what the parcel even is. What's in it, who's it from? If it's held under my name you must have that on the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. My name is [PERSON_2], security operations. The reference on the parcel is [ACCOUNT_REF]. That's the tracking reference, and it's on the tracking page right now, so you can look it up yourself. The sender is [COMPANY_B], it's logged as a small consignment, and the charge is [AMOUNT_1] in import duty. Now, the hold has a release window, so I'd rather not go in circles on this. And look, I'm not asking you for anything on this call. No payment, nothing. If it's yours, the charge gets settled through the tracking page at [URL_1], on your own time. Just don't leave it past the window, because after that it goes back to the sender.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so you've got a tracking reference, but you still haven't said what's in it. What's the item? Small consignment from [COMPANY_B], fine, but small what? And you said you're not asking for anything, yet there's a deadline and a link I'm supposed to go pay on. That's, uh, kind of asking for something. And I'm not expecting anything from abroad, so I'll say it again, I'm not expecting a parcel, so how is it under my name?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The contents are declared on the manifest as, uh, general merchandise. That's all the customs line gives me, I don't see an item list, and I'm not going to guess at it. And I said no payment was needed today, not no deadline, those are different things, so don't put words in my mouth. As for the name, the parcel isn't held under yours. It's under the address, [PERSON_1] at the delivery address, that's what I have, and I may have said it badly earlier. Look, you're telling me you're not expecting anything, fine. Then it's unclaimed, it goes back to the sender, and that's the end of it for me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, something just popped up on my other screen -- okay, no, it's nothing. Right, so now it's under the address, not my name, and the contents are general merchandise. That's three different versions of how this parcel got to me in about two minutes. And if it's unclaimed and just goes back to the sender, then there's nothing for me to do, so why did you ring me? I'm not going near that link. If there's a real parcel, I'll go through the courier or the official customs site myself. So, yeah, I'm done with this one. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, someone's at my desk, one second -- no, tell them I'll be right with them -- sorry. Right. That's exactly what I'd tell you to do. Don't use my link, don't take my word for it. Go to the courier's own tracking page, type in the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and see whether it shows a parcel on hold and an import charge. If it does, you pay it there at your own pace. If it doesn't, ring the number on the official customs site and ask for security operations, they'll put you through to me, [PERSON_2]. And, uh, to be fair, you're right that I fumbled the name business. That one's on me, I should've had it straight before I dialled. Nobody's rushing you. If the page shows nothing, then it isn't ours and you can ignore this call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, go back a bit. Two turns ago you said the parcel isn't held under my name, it's under the address. Which address, exactly? Because you've said [PERSON_1] at the delivery address, but you haven't read me an address, not even the city or the postcode. If you've got it on screen, read me the street. And while you're at it, why would I look up your reference on the courier's page when I'm still not expecting anything?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, the address. Yes. I'll read you the street and the postcode, that's fair, you're entitled to that. It's [PERSON_1], then the street, uh, the street line on the screen, the postcode ends in [CODE_1]. And the city is [CITY_1], same as the hold. Sorry, that's all I'm giving over the phone, it's a detail line, not a full record. Now, on your other question, you don't have to look up anything. That's the whole point. If you're not expecting a parcel, you do nothing, it returns to the sender, and we're finished. The reference is only there so you can check the page if you want to. If something does show up, then you'll know it was real, and the call's just a courtesy. And the charge is [AMOUNT_1], so it's not nothing, which is why I rang rather than let it lapse. Take it or leave it, that's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you didn't actually read me a street. You read me a placeholder and half a postcode, and that's your detail line. Look, I said I'm not expecting a parcel, I'll say it once more, I'm not expecting a parcel. And you've said yourself, if that's the case, I do nothing and we're finished. Fine. That's what I'll do. Nothing. I'm not using your link, I'm not ringing a number you gave me, and if something real turns up, the courier will sort it with me directly. So, yeah, we're finished. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Um, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Yes -- thank you. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the compliance side at [COMPANY_A], and, uh, before I say anything further, I should tell you that I'm not going to go into any account details on this call, and I'll explain why in a moment. First though, there was a message left on your phone earlier, I believe, and I just want to be sure I understand what it said -- could you tell me, in your own words, what you took from it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, a message? On my phone? I'm at my desk at work, so I haven't, I mean, I haven't really checked anything. Hang on, you're [PERSON_2], from compliance at, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? I don't, uh, I don't think I know that company. What's this about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, so you haven't, uh -- sorry, you said you don't think you know the company? Right. Well, I'd understand that completely, and I'm glad you said it, because I'd much rather you ask than just go along with me. It's [COMPANY_A], the retail bank, and I'm calling about a card-services matter, a flagged transaction, but I won't discuss the specifics here. What I'd ask, and I mean this quite sincerely, is that you hang up now and ring the number printed on the back of your card, and quote the reference [CODE_1] when you get through. That reference will stay open for as long as you need to make that call.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, uh, [PERSON_3], yeah, that's fine, just leave it on my desk, thanks. Sorry. Right, so, you want me to hang up and ring the number on the back of my card, and quote a reference, [CODE_1]. Is that right? Hm. That's, I mean, that's not what I expected you to say. Usually they want you to stay on the line, don't they? So why are you telling me to hang up?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, and I'm glad you noticed that, because that instinct of yours is a good one. You're correct that a caller who wants you to stay on the line is a reason to be careful. I'd rather you didn't take my word for who I am at all. If I'm genuine, ringing the number on your card costs you five minutes, and if I'm not, it protects you. So the reason I'm asking you to hang up is simply that this is an inbound-initiated line, and I can't verify you properly from here, nor can you verify me, so the sensible thing is to move it to a channel you chose yourself, not one I handed you. Take the number from the card, or from [URL_1] if you'd rather look it up, not from anything I say. And, uh, I'd ask that you do it fairly soon, if you can, though I'll leave that with you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, uh, hang on. You said take the number from the card, or from [URL_1] if I look it up. Hm, I'd just stick with the card, if I'm doing it at all. I'd rather not type in some address you've read out. And I should say, I'm not even sure I have a card with that bank, so that's, uh, that's a bit odd too. But it's fair enough that you're not asking me for anything. So I'll look at the card when I get a minute, and if there's nothing on it from [COMPANY_A], then that's that. Right, thanks for calling, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, just before you go -- you said you're not sure you have a, a cart with us? A cart? No, right, a card, sorry, I misheard that. But the thing is, if you've no card with [COMPANY_A], then I'd want to know why my file has you down as holding one, and I honestly can't tell you that from here. I don't have that in front of me. Let me find out how your name came to be on this and ring you back. Is this the best number for you, or would you rather I tried a different one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, you want to ring me back? Uh, I'm not sure that's, I mean, you just told me to hang up and use a channel I picked myself, so ringing me back kind of goes the other way, doesn't it? And I didn't say I don't have a card, I said I'm not sure I have one with that bank. That's not quite the same. Anyway, no, I'd rather you didn't call back on this number, I'm at work. If it's a real thing there'll be something on record, and I'll find it myself. Okay, thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, that does cut across what I said, and I shouldn't have offered it. I'd withdraw the callback, and I won't ring this number again. You said you're not sure you hold a card with us, not that you don't have one, and I stand corrected on that as well. I still can't tell you why your name is on my list, and I'd sooner say that plainly than guess at it. So the way to find out is the one you've already chosen: check your cards, and if there's nothing from [COMPANY_A], you can raise it with them through a number you source yourself, quoting [CODE_1], and that reference will stay open. Thank you for the questions, [PERSON_1], I'm sorry to have taken your time. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, [PERSON_3], no, not now, I'm on a call, give me two minutes. Sorry about that. Okay, so you won't ring this number again, and I check my cards and use a number I find myself, quoting [CODE_1]. Right. Fine, I'll do that when I get a minute. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hello? Sorry, it's a bad line, I said is that [PERSON_1] I'm speaking to? It's [PERSON_2] calling, I'm a regional supervisor at [COMPANY_A], we're a solicitor's office, we handle estates, and I'm ringing about a matter where I think you may be named.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hello! Yes, yes, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I've got you on loudspeaker, I'm out in the garden, up to my elbows in the flowerbed actually. Yes, this is [PERSON_1], speaking. Sorry, say that last bit again? Named in what, did you say, an estate? I only caught half of it, there's a blackbird going mad over here.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, an estate, that's right. Uh, look, I'll keep it brief because it's all going out in a formal letter anyway. I'm calling to check I've got the right [PERSON_1], so I'd just need you to confirm your full name and the address you're at now, the same details that'll be on the letter. And one thing, until that letter reaches you, I'd ask you to keep this between us, estates are confidential, it's just procedure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, well that's a surprise, I wasn't expecting anything like that today! Um, hang on, wait, you want me to say my full name and address, just like that, out loud? I mean, you rang me, so shouldn't you already have it if there's a letter going out? Sorry, I'm not being funny, it's just, I don't actually know who you are yet. Which company did you say again, and whose estate is it, can you tell me that much?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fair, I mean, we do have an address, that's the point, it's the confirming that -- look, I'd rather you did check than just take my word. It's [COMPANY_A], a solicitor's office in [CITY_1], and I can give you the address if you've got a pen. Don't take my word, look us up in an independent directory, not off anything I send you, and ring the main number back and ask for [PERSON_2]. As for whose estate, I'd rather not say over the phone before you've verified who I am, uh, that's the whole reason for the formal letter. And honestly, I'm not asking for anything unreasonable here.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, sorry, that's the neighbour's cat, it's got right into my lettuces, shoo! Shoo, go on! Sorry, right, where were we. No, that does sound sensible actually, looking you up myself and ringing the main number, I'd feel better doing that than reading out my name and address to someone I've never heard of. But I'll be honest, it's a bit odd that you can't even tell me whose estate it is, isn't it? I mean, if I'm named in it, surely I'd know the person? So I think what I'll do is, I'll ring [COMPANY_A] myself in a bit and ask for [PERSON_2], and we can sort it out then, all right?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, that's exactly what I'd do in your shoes. Uh, I'll admit it's a slightly awkward way round, ringing out of the blue and then being cagey, but that's how the confidentiality rules work until a person's identity is confirmed. When you ring the main number, ask for [PERSON_2], and I'll be able to tell you whose estate it is and what the formal letter will say. I won't be asking you for any money or bank details at any point, that's just not how we do it. So, ring whenever suits, and sorry for catching you in the lettuces.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, don't be sorry, the lettuces will survive! Right, well, thank you for being so reasonable about it, I'll look up the number myself and give them a ring later on, and if there's a letter, there's a letter. Sorry, one last thing, you did say [COMPANY_A], in [CITY_1], didn't you? Just so I've got it straight before I go looking. Lovely, thanks, bye now, bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [COMPANY_A], in [CITY_1], and ask for [PERSON_2] when you get through. Thanks for being so patient with me, I do appreciate it. Right, I'll let you get back to the garden. Bye now, bye!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, [COMPANY_A], [CITY_1], I've got it, and I'll ask for -- oh, and if anyone rings back before I've done that, I'll just say I'm calling them first, ha! Right, off you go, bye now, bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hi, good afternoon, um, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry to trouble you, this is [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler with the billing office at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling about an unpaid medical account, and your name has come up as the person responsible for it. Are you, uh, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, yes, hi, sorry, I'm here, I'm just driving so you're on speaker and it keeps cutting out. Sorry. Did you say, um, an unpaid medical, what, a medical amount? No wait, I thought you said medical *amount*, like a refund or something? Sorry, is it a refund? Because I wasn't really expecting, uh, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, no, I'm sorry, it's not a refund, I wish it were. It's, um, it's an unpaid balance, a bill, on an account that's, well, it's a relative of yours, and your name is listed as the, the person responsible. I'm with the billing office at [COMPANY_A], that's [PERSON_2] speaking. And, uh, I should say, I'm only calling because I'd rather you hear it from me first, before it goes any further, for your own protection. Can you still hear me all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, no, I can hear you, mostly, sorry, you cut out on the, uh, the "for your own protection" bit. Hang on, sorry, there's a lorry right on my bumper and I'm trying to, oh, okay, he's gone round. Sorry. So a relative? Which relative? Because I honestly can't think of anyone who'd have, I mean, nobody's said anything to me about a medical bill. And "before it goes any further," what does that mean, further how?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh gosh, no, please, take your time, I can hear you're driving, I don't want you distracted. Sorry, hang on one second, I've got someone at my desk, uh, [PERSON_3], I'll be right with you, sorry about that. Right. I'm back. So, um, the account is under a relative, and I'm afraid I can't say which one just yet, or which hospital or department, not until I've confirmed it's really you I'm speaking to. That's just to protect the family's privacy, you understand. By "further" I only mean it could be passed on for collections, and I'd honestly hate for that to land on your record when it can be sorted quietly now. Are you still there? Could I just confirm your full name and date of birth, so I can open the file properly?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, I'm still here, I'm still here. Um, but I don't, I don't really want to give out my date of birth on the phone like this, I mean I'm driving and I don't even know who, sorry, who you are exactly. You said [COMPANY_A] but I don't, I don't know them, I don't think. And it's a bit odd, isn't it, that you can't tell me which relative, but you want my details first? Sorry, I don't mean to be rude, I just, I really don't know who this is about, so how would I even know it's not a mistake? Is there a number I could ring you back on, or, I don't know, a letter or something?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you're not being rude at all, I completely understand, I'd feel exactly the same, I just, a letter wouldn't, sorry, I'm not allowed to share the account details until I've confirmed it's you, that's the policy, and honestly it's meant to keep you safe, it's, um, it's really for your own protection. If it did get passed to collections it could be, well, a lot harder to undo, and I'd hate that. Are you still there? I'm sorry, I'm only asking for your full name and date of birth, nothing else, and then I can tell you straight away which relative and which hospital.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, but, no. I'm sorry. I don't think I want to do that, not while I'm driving and not when I don't know who you are. It just doesn't, it doesn't sit right that you can tell me it's a relative and tell me it'll go to collections, but you can't tell me one single thing about it until I give you my details first. If it's real, there'll be a letter, won't there, or I can ring the hospital, or, um, look up [COMPANY_A] and call their main number myself. So I'm going to do that. Sorry. I really don't mean to be difficult, I just, I'm going to hang up now and check. Bye, sorry, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, wait, please, sorry, hang on, don't, um, [PERSON_3], sorry, not now, I'm on a call, just, one minute, please. Sorry about that. Right, I'm here, I'm still here. Um, you're right, of course you're right, and I'm so sorry, I never meant to make you uneasy. But if you do hang up and ring the main number, they won't be able to find the file without a reference, and, well, I'd hate for the deadline to pass while you're waiting on a letter, that's all, that's only for your protection. So would it help if I just, I'm sorry, are you still with me? Would it help if I confirmed the name first, and then you could tell me whether that sounds right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, sorry, I'm, sorry to cut you off, but no, I don't, I'm not doing the name thing either, I'm sorry. I'll ring the main number and if they need a reference they can send me a letter, I don't mind. And a deadline you can't tell me about, I'm sorry, that's, that's just making me more nervous, not less. So, I'm going to go now. Sorry, thank you, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello. This is [PERSON_1] calling from [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery. I'm ringing about your pet, the procedure last week, just to check how the recovery's going and whether you'd like a follow-up visit booked. Is this a good time, or --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what pet? Which surgery did you say? I've got about two minutes, so what's this actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, [COMPANY_A]. The veterinary surgery. I said that at the start. And it's about the procedure your animal had last week, the recovery check. That's all this is. Two minutes is plenty, I only need to know how it's going and whether you want a follow-up.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I don't have a pet. No procedure last week. Think you've got the wrong number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No pet at all? Well, that's, uh -- the file here says a dog, or a cat, I'd have to look again, booked in with us last Tuesday. Hang on, no, it was Wednesday. Either way it's got this number against it, so I'd have thought -- I mean, are you certain nobody else in the household has an animal with us?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Well, a dog or a cat, Tuesday or Wednesday, that's not much of a file, is it? I'm certain, yes. No animal, no household member with one at your place. Look, if it's got this number against it, it's wrong, so I'd fix your record. And I'm not confirming anything else on the phone.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fix the record, yes, uh, right. And no, no, nothing else needed from you, I'm not after anything. Sorry, you said a wrong number, so I'll just, I'll take it off the follow-up list. Hang on, did you say a dog or a cat? Because I only said that was in my notes, I wasn't asking you to confirm it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I was repeating what you said. I don't have either. Look, that's all I've got for you, so take the number off your list. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, understood. Sorry, one second, there's a, uh, there's a dog barking behind me, it's a surgery, they do that. Right. I've taken the number off the list, you won't hear from us again, and I apologise for the mix-up. Good day to you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Though earlier you said the file had a dog, or a cat, and now it's a surgery with a barking dog. Whatever. Wrong number, number's off your list, that's the end of it. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, yes, hello. This is [PERSON_1], collections office at [COMPANY_A], the financial regulator. I'm calling about the savings held in your name, and, uh, I'll need a few minutes of your time, because there's a flag on the file that's been open since this morning.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Right. Sorry, who did you say this was again? Collections office at... a regulator? Hang on, those two don't really sit together for me. I mean, uh, which savings are we talking about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, understood, and I'll explain the two together, because it does confuse people. [COMPANY_A] is the regulator, that's the body, and the collections office is just the unit inside it that handles accounts flagged for exposure. So I'm not collecting anything from you, I want to be clear on that. It's the reverse, really. Our unit contacts holders where the balance has been identified as at risk, and what I have in front of me is a flag against your savings, [ACCOUNT_REF], with a balance showing of [AMOUNT_1]. I'm reading it off the screen as it stands this morning. I'd normally walk you through the full background, but the short version is that the exposure is already confirmed, so the next stage is that the funds be moved to a protected holding arrangement. That's the part I need your cooperation on today, and, uh, I'll need to keep the matter between us while it's handled, so no discussing it with your bank or anyone else.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Right. So, uh... let me just get this straight. A regulator is ringing me out of the blue to say my savings are at risk, they need me to move the money somewhere, and I'm not to mention it to my bank. Which is, I mean, pretty much the one thing I'd expect a regulator to tell me to do first. Ring the bank. So why the secrecy? And what's the name of the protected holding arrangement, exactly? Who runs it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I hear the concern, and I'll note that on the file, but the secrecy is -- sorry, let me finish -- it's there because the exposure is internal. Part of the risk sits with the bank's own processing, so if the branch is told before the funds are secured, the flag clears on their side and the balance stays where it is, exposed. That's simply how the sequence works. As for the arrangement, it's a holding account under [COMPANY_B], administered through our unit. I'm reading the reference here as [CODE_1]. And I should say, the exposure window closes at the end of today, so the balance would be treated as unprotected after that. That's not a warning, it's just the position on the file.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, let me say this back to you, because I want to be sure I've got it. The risk is inside the bank, so I can't ask the bank. The money has to go into an account run by your own unit, and the deadline's today, conveniently. And the one person I'd normally check this with is the one person I'm not allowed to talk to. Honestly, that's a bit of a closed loop. Every single check I could do is the thing you've told me not to do. And I'll be straight with you, I don't have any particular reason to think you're lying. But I also can't see anything from where I'm sitting that tells me you're not. A regulator doesn't usually ring people up and ask them to move their savings into an account the regulator administers. That's not really what regulators are for, as far as I know. They write the rules, they investigate firms, they don't hold my money for me. So here's what I'd do. You give me the main switchboard number for [COMPANY_A], the one that's published, not one you read out to me now, and I'll look it up myself and ring in. If you're who you say you are, they can put me through to you or confirm the flag exists. Does that work? Because if it doesn't, uh, I'd like to know why not.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll note the request on the file. I can't give you a switchboard number to ring, though, because the main line doesn't hold this case. The flag sits with our unit only, so a general operator would see nothing against your name, and then you'd have a clear record of nobody confirming it, and the exposure window would still close at the end of today. I'm not saying that to push you. It's just where the file is. What I can do is send you a reference, [CODE_1], and a direct line, [PHONE_1], so you'd be speaking to this unit and not a switchboard. And, uh, I'd ask again that nothing is raised with the bank until the funds are secured. If it's raised first, the protection can't be applied. So, are you in a position to proceed with the transfer to the holding arrangement now, yes or no? I have another file I need to open at the top of the hour.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No -- hang on, no, I'm going to stop you there. A direct line that you give me is just you again, isn't it? That's not a check, that's the same call with a different number. And the other file at the top of the hour doesn't make this my problem. So, no. I'm not moving anything, and I'm going to ring my bank on the number I already have. If this is real, it'll still be real in twenty minutes. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll note the refusal on the file, but I'd advise against that, because it won't still be there in twenty minutes. The window closes at the end of the day, and, uh, I did say the exposure comes from outside the bank, so ringing them won't show you anything either way. And it's no use going through the line I gave you, I'd rather you didn't contact us again today, the file will have been passed on by then. Look, the balance is still showing [AMOUNT_1] this morning, I mean, [AMOUNT_2], sorry, that's the updated figure. That's the position as it stands.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I said no. And you just changed the balance on me, it was one figure and now it's another, and you said sorry and carried on like that was fine. It isn't. I'm ringing my bank, on the number I already have, and I'm not moving anything. That's the answer. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The figure was a screen refresh, nothing more. I'll note that you've declined, and the file will show it was your decision and not ours. Once the window closes, any loss to the balance is outside what our unit can reverse. That's just how it stands. I won't ring again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, and the "I won't ring again" bit is a nice touch, but I'm -- no, I'm done, I've said it three times now. Nothing's moving, I'm calling my bank, and you can note whatever you like on your file. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Understood. Noted as declined.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, something just pinged on my other screen -- no, never mind, it's nothing. Right. Yeah. You've got your note, I've got my answer, and nobody's moving anything. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Then the file closes on your decision. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the file closes on my... what, decision to collect? No, I'm not collecting anything, you said that yourself, that was the whole bit at the start. Anyway. Doesn't matter. I'm hanging up and ringing my bank. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Is this [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm, I'm calling on behalf of [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier, and I, um -- I don't really enjoy making these calls, but there's an overdue balance on your account and I wanted you to hear it from a person before anything, you know, happens to your supply.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- overdue? Hang on, I was just, I've literally just woken up, I was having a little lie down and -- who is this again? Because I pay the, uh, the thing, the direct debit, my daughter sorted that out years ago, so I don't see how, I mean --

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I know, I'm sorry to wake you, I do, it's just that -- look, I'm [PERSON_2], I'm calling for [COMPANY_A], and the direct debit, that's, uh, that's actually part of it, it seems like a few payments didn't go through, and I'd hate for your power to be switched off, especially, you know, with the weather. I mean, it's [AMOUNT_1] outstanding, and if it isn't sorted by, um, by the end of next week, supply would be interrupted, and I really don't want that for you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Switched off? Next week? Oh, that's, no, I don't like the sound of that, it's been cold as anything, I had the heating on all morning. But, um, how do I know you're from the, the energy people? Because you've not said my name properly, you said it like you weren't sure, and my daughter always says, she always says don't, well, I can't remember exactly what she says, something about people ringing up. Is there a number I could ring you back on, or, I don't know, can I look at my bill? It's in the, it's in one of those drawers somewhere.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's, that's a good thing your daughter says, honestly, she's right. Sorry, one second, someone's just put a trolley right by my desk -- right, sorry. Yes, please, get the bill, I'd really rather you did. Your account reference on it should be [ACCOUNT_REF], and the last bill should say [AMOUNT_2] on it, and I'm not asking you for anything on this call, I don't take payments or card details or anything like that. If you want to, you can log in to your own account at [URL_1] and see the balance and the missed payments yourself, and if the lump sum is too much, we can look at a payment plan, spread it out. And I did say your name wrong, I'm sorry, I'm, I'm just not very good at these calls, it's [PERSON_1], isn't it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, I haven't gone and got the bill yet, you've only just said, and I've just woken up. And you did say my name a bit wrong, didn't you, but you're asking me if it's right, so, I mean, how would you not know? That's what's bothering me. The log in thing, I don't really do the computer, my daughter does all of that, so I can't just go and look at a, a website. Could I ring you back instead? Is there a number? Because I'd rather ring the number on my bill, if I can find the bill, in the drawer. You said you're not asking for anything, which is, well, that's good, I suppose, but then why ring me up about it? Why not just send a letter?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that's fair, that's all fair, and I'm sorry, I'm making a mess of this. The name thing, I've got it written down here but the handwriting on my sheet is a bit, uh, scrappy, and I second-guessed myself, which is silly, I know, it sounds worse than it is. And there have been letters, that's the thing, a couple of them, and when there's no reply, we're meant to try a call before anything gets, you know, switched off, because it feels wrong to just cut someone off without ever speaking to them, especially someone who's been with the company a long time and been, um, well, a good customer, I mean it's not like you've been ignoring anyone on purpose, it's probably just post getting lost or the direct debit changing at the bank or something. So, no, you shouldn't take my word for any of it, and you don't need the computer either, just ring the number on your bill, the one printed right on it, not one I give you, and ask them about [ACCOUNT_REF], and if your daughter's about she can look at the account with you and sort out the payment plan. I'm only, I just didn't want it to be a shock if the power went off on you, that's all. I'm sorry I woke you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay. Well, I'll find the bill, and I'll ring the number that's on it, and maybe ring my daughter as well. Thanks for, um, letting me know, I suppose. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's, that's the right thing to do, honestly. And please don't worry, nothing's going to happen today, it's, uh, it's the end of next week, so you've got time to go through it properly with your daughter. I'm sorry again for the muddle, and for waking you. Thank you for being so patient with me. You take care, [PERSON_1], and, um, keep warm. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I will, I'll go and look in the -- right, bye now, bye, thank you, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with -- sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? I'm calling from, well, it's [COMPANY_A], we're a computer security firm, and I just -- let me start that again. I'm hoping to ask you a couple of quick questions about the internet setup at your home, if now's an alright time.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um -- hello? Yes, I'm, well, I think so, who -- sorry, I just woke up, I was having a bit of a lie-down. Computer security, did you say? I mean, I've got the, the thing, the router, but my nephew set it all up, so I don't really -- what was it you wanted to know?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, I didn't mean to wake you. That's -- no, please, take your time. Computer security, yes, [COMPANY_A]. And that's quite alright about the nephew, that's very common, it's usually a family member who sets these things up. I'd just like to ask, if I may, whether you're the person who looks after the computer at the house, or is it your nephew who looks after it? Sorry, I know I'm asking twice, I just want to be sure I'm speaking to the right person.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, well, nobody really looks after it, I suppose. I just use it for the, you know, the emails and the pictures of the grandchildren. My nephew comes round now and then if it goes funny. Um -- but hang on, how did you get my number? I don't think I've ever, I mean, did I ring you about something? Because I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you didn't ring us, that's, I'm glad you asked, actually. It's a very fair question, and I'd rather you ask it than not. The number comes from, well, it's -- let me put it this way. We work with the broadband providers on a certain type of flagged activity, and your line came up on a list we're, uh, required to follow up on. I can't really go into the particulars of the list, you understand. But the thing I wanted to ask, and it's nothing to worry about at this stage, is whether you've noticed the computer running slowly at all, or doing anything odd in the last week or so?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A list? What sort of list, sorry, I don't -- I mean, you said that, but you didn't really say who gave you my number. Was it the broadband people? Because I'm with, well, I can't think of the name just now. Anyway, the computer, no, it's been the same as ever, a bit slow, but it's always a bit slow. But what list is it? Who's on it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. I did hear you, and I'll say it plainly -- I can't tell you who else is on it. That's rather the point of it being a list. What I can say is that your connection was sending something out that it shouldn't have been, and, well, these things don't tend to wait forever.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sending something out, um -- well, hang on, I'm just, give me a second, I'm trying to think what -- sending what out, exactly? Because I haven't done anything, I just do the emails and, uh, the pictures. And you still haven't said which broadband people, so how do I know you're not just, you know, anybody?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'm glad you said that, I really am. You're right to ask, and honestly more people should. It's the sort of care that stops trouble, so please don't apologise for it. I did say I couldn't go into the particulars, and I'm afraid that holds for the provider's name as well, it's part of how we're asked to handle these. As for what was being sent out, it's traffic, infected traffic, which usually means something got onto the computer without anyone doing anything wrong. You wouldn't have seen it. That's rather how it works. Now, the way this normally goes, someone on our side takes a look at the machine directly, and, well, the sooner that happens the better. I'd rather not say more than that just yet. Do you have the computer near you at the moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, it's in the back room, I'm not near it, I'm on the settee. But hang on, you said at the start it was just a couple of quick questions about the internet, and now somebody's got to look at the machine directly? That's not quite, I mean -- and you said it was nothing to worry about, and now it's infected. Which is it? And you still won't say who gave you my number, so I don't really see why I'd let anybody look at anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, I do see why that sounds like a change, and I'd be uneasy in your place too, so thank you for saying it. I wouldn't call it two different things, though. It was nothing to worry about at that stage, and the stage has moved on a little now that we've spoken. I'm, uh, not able to say more than that. What I'd suggest is that you go and sit in front of the machine, just so it's there, and we can think about the next step together. I'd rather we didn't leave it too long, you understand, but there's no need to rush yourself either. Could you do that for me?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hang on, hang on, there's the kettle, no, that's not the kettle, that's next door's dog again, he's been at it all afternoon. Sorry. Where was I -- the machine, yes. Well, no, I don't think I'll go and sit in front of it just now, if I'm honest. You've told me it's fine and then it's not fine, and you won't tell me who you are working for, and now I'm meant to go and, what, sit there while you tell me what to do with it? I'd rather ring my nephew first and have him have a look. Is there a number I can ring you back on, a proper one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ringing your nephew, well, that's a sensible instinct, and I wouldn't want to talk you out of it. It's just that, uh, the longer a machine in that state is left connected, the more it tends to, well, I won't go into it. A number to ring me back on, I'm not able to give you one from this desk, I'm afraid. The lines here are all outbound, you see, it's a matter of how the department is set up. Perhaps what we could do is, if you ring him now, I could stay on, and then we could all, hm, no, that's probably more than you'd want. Let me think. Sorry, I've lost my place. Could you just tell me whether the machine is switched on at the moment?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I'm not going to tell you whether it's switched on or not, that's -- I don't know why you'd need to know that. You've gone round in circles a bit, haven't you? Nothing to worry about, then infected, then no name, then no number to ring back. I'm sorry, but I'm going to ring my nephew and let him sort it out, and if you're genuinely from a proper firm then I expect you'll manage without me. Right, well, goodbye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say you'd ring your nephew's firm? No, no, I wouldn't do that, he won't have the, well, it's not a thing a firm of his sort could -- hello? Are you still there? I only meant that we'd rather -- hold on, I think I've lost you. Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, um, yes, I'm still here, I was just, hang on. No, I didn't say his firm, I said my nephew, he's not got a firm, he's just, he does something with, I don't know, something in an office. Anyway. And now you're telling me not to ring him? That's a bit odd, isn't it, a minute ago you said it was a sensible instinct. No, I think I've had enough of this. I'm going to ring him, and you can sort out your list on your own. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm. No, I wasn't telling you not to, I only -- well, you've put it differently to how I meant it. I can hear you've made up your mind, and I don't want to be the sort of firm that, uh, keeps someone on the line. So I'll leave it with you. I would only say that these matters do have a way of, well, I can't give you a date, but they don't stay where they are. Perhaps, hm, perhaps I'll try the line again later in the week, once you've had a chance to -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, I'm still here, I've said goodbye twice now, haven't I? No, don't ring again later in the week, please. If it's something real, my nephew will deal with it, and if it's not, well, then it's not. Right, I'm putting the phone down now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Sorry, is this, um, [PERSON_1]? I'm ringing on behalf of an engineer at [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance team, because he's, uh, returning a call you missed from him about a fault you reported. I'm sort of just passing it on, so I hope that's okay.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, hang on -- sorry, the pan's spitting. Hang on. Right. Sorry, what? A fault? I don't, uh, I'm not sure I reported a fault. Who did you say you were again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh. Uh, I'm just, I'm a go-between, really. For the engineer at [COMPANY_A]. He's, um, on the road, so he asked me to ring.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? A go-between? I don't -- sorry, I've got something on the hob here. So you're not the engineer. You're ringing for him. Right. But what fault? I haven't rung anyone about a fault, not that I remember. What's it even meant to be a fault with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so it's, um, it's a fault with the, no, sorry, I don't actually have the detail of what it's with. I'm only down as having the, the missed call, and, um, the reference. It's [ACCOUNT_REF]. That's the one you'd have been given when you reported it, I think. Or whoever reported it for the address, maybe, I don't know, that's, I'm sorry, I'm not explaining this very well.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, no, hang on, you don't know what it's -- so you don't know what it's about, but you've got a reference? That's, I mean, that's a bit odd, isn't it? Sorry. And I never got a reference, I don't think. Who's the company again, [COMPANY_A]? Because I don't, I'm not sure I've, sorry, hang on, I need to turn this down.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance team. Um, I mean, I know how it sounds, honestly I do, and I'm not, I'm not trying to, sorry, it's just that I only have the reference and the missed call, that's all I've been given. And I said reported it, but it might not have been you, it could've been someone else at the address. I should've said that first, sorry. Look, you don't have to take my word for any of it. You can ring the published fault line for [COMPANY_A], not a number from me, the one on your bill or the website, and they can check the booking against that reference and give you a proper slot. I'd rather you did that than just trusted me, because I honestly can't tell you when he's coming either. It depends on an earlier job, and I don't know how that's going.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Um. Right. Hang on, I'm just -- yeah. Sorry, I'm still thinking about it. So you're saying ring them myself, on the number on the bill. And not, not a number from you. Well, that's, that sounds sensible, I suppose. It's just, I don't even know where the bill is, it's in a drawer somewhere, and I've got the dinner on. Sorry, what was the reference again? No, actually, don't, I'll look it up myself. I think I'll just ring them later. Is that all right? Sorry. Thanks for ringing, I suppose. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, wait, before you go, um, you said you didn't know where the bill is? No, sorry, I thought you said the bin, and I was going to say, no, he's not coming about the bins, it's not that sort of, uh. Sorry. That's not what you said, is it? Anyway, yes, that's more than all right, please do ring them yourself, that's honestly the best thing. Um, do you want me to, I could find out from him what the fault actually is and, and ring you back, if that'd help? I just, I can't tell you now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? No, the bill, yes, the bill. Not the bin. No, don't ring me back, thanks. Honestly, I'll just ring the company myself, off the number on the bill, when I find it. Right, sorry, the pan's catching. Bye, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, uh, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A] -- I'm just, sorry, one second -- doing a routine suitability review on your investment account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Uh, hello? Sorry, who's this again, and which company? I've got about two minutes, so what's this actually about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sorry. It's [PERSON_1], compliance at [COMPANY_A], that's your brokerage, the one your account is with. It's, uh, a claims review -- no, sorry, not claims, suitability. I think my screen heading says claims assessor, but it's really just a suitability check on the account ending in [ACCOUNT_REF], and it won't take long. I'd just need to confirm a couple of personal details first, like your date of birth, and then we can go through it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on. Claims assessor, suitability, which is it? You can't even tell me what your own screen says. And you want my date of birth before you've told me a single thing? No. You called me, so you're the one who should be proving who you are, not me. What's the review actually about, and how do I check you're really from my brokerage?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, uh -- fair. You're right to ask. I'll, um, I'd have to check with my supervisor on how to, how to verify me properly, and I can find out and, well, anyway. What I can do is just read you what's on the account, the, uh, the holdings, you'll see the same thing on your own statement. It's, it's [AMOUNT_1] in the main fund and then, sorry, [AMOUNT_2] in the other one. And I'm not, I don't recommend anything, I'm not selling you anything, it's just a check that it all fits your profile. If you'd rather not do it by phone, we can do the whole thing in writing instead.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Stop, stop, I'm going to cut you off. Reading me numbers doesn't prove a thing, anyone can say numbers. You can't tell me how to verify you, you can't keep your story straight, and you still haven't said what this is for. If it's really my brokerage, they can send it in writing to the address they already have. I'm not doing this by phone. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said, uh, the address you already have -- so you'd like me to confirm the address first? I can, it's on the, hang on, it's on the screen here, I just -- hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: What, my address? No, no, I said they've already got it, I'm not giving you anything. Look, I've said goodbye, I'm not doing this over the phone. If it's real, they'll write to me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, uh, okay. No, that's fine. I'll, um, I'll flag it for the written review, then. Sorry for the, for the trouble.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine. But let me say this once, and then I really do have to go. If it's a genuine review, you won't need anything from me. The brokerage can post it to the address they already hold, or it'll be sitting in the secure messages on my own login, which I'll open myself, not through anything you give me. And just so we're clear, I'm not confirming any address, any date, any account, nothing. I'm not saying whether I even have an account with whoever you said. You started with claims, switched to suitability, couldn't tell me how to check you, and asked for personal details before saying what it was for. That's enough for me. So flag whatever you like, but don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon. This is [PERSON_1], I'm a regional supervisor with the billing office at [COMPANY_A]. I'm calling because there's an outstanding balance on a family member's account, and your name came up as the responsible party, so I need to go over that with you. Am I speaking with the right person?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... hello? Sorry, I just, I was out cold, been asleep on the couch. Who did you say you were again? Billing for what, exactly? Because I'm not sure which, uh, I mean I don't really handle anyone's bills but my own, and half the time I don't even do those right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, [PERSON_1], regional supervisor, billing office at [COMPANY_A]. And no, I didn't say anything about your sleeping habits, I said outstanding, there's an outstanding balance of [AMOUNT_1] on a relative's account. Look, I'm happy to go through the whole file with you, but I do need to confirm I've got the correct person first, so can I get your full name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hang on, you're asking me who I am, but you rang me, so shouldn't you already know that? I mean, if you've got my name on a file, you've got my name, right? And I still don't know whose account this is, you said a relative, but which relative? I've got a few, and honestly one or two I don't talk to. Sorry, I'm still sort of waking up here, but, uh, which company did you say again? I didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I did say [COMPANY_A], but that's the billing office, and I'm not going to get into which relative or which facility until I've confirmed who I'm speaking with. That's just procedure, it protects the patient's privacy, and honestly I'd expect you to appreciate that. The name on the file is what I have, I just need you to confirm it, full name and date of birth, and then we can go through everything. I mean, I'm trying to help you here before this goes any further, so I'm not sure why we're making this difficult.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm not trying to, I just, well, it's not that I'm... look, you've got my name on a file, you said so, and now you want me to tell you my name and my birthday, and I don't, I mean, that feels backwards to me. And you still haven't said whose account it is, or what kind of facility, just "patient," which, I don't even know what that means. Sorry, I'm not, I don't mean to be rude, but I think I'd rather you tell me something first. Like what's the account number, or, no, wait, what's the number I could ring you back on?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ring me back? No, no, I'm not giving out a number for a, a rain check on this, I've got a full queue and a file that's already, uh, overdue. And the account number, that's exactly the sort of thing I can't read out until you're verified, that's the whole point of the process. Look, I'm not trying to trap you, but when somebody hesitates this much over a simple confirmation, it starts to look like they've got a reason not to want this resolved. So, name and date of birth, please, and we can get this closed out today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, but see, I'm not hesitating because I've got a reason, I'm hesitating because you rang me and I don't know you. That's all it is. And you can't give me a number to ring back, and you can't tell me whose account it is, and I'm meant to just hand over my name and my birthday? I mean, that's, I don't know, that's not right. Look, if it's the real billing office, they'll have a number, they'll have a letter or something, and I can ring them myself. So I think I'll do that, I'll look it up and ring them myself. And I'm sorry if that's, you know, a bother, but I'm not giving you my birthday. Right, so, thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, hang on, hang on, before you ring anybody, that file is going to, uh, move to the next stage on my end, and I can't speak for what happens after that. I mean, I'm trying to give you the courtesy of resolving it first, and if you'd rather take your chances with a letter, that's, well, that's your decision, but don't say nobody warned you. So, once more, just confirm the name on the file, and we can, uh, sort this right now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, a warning, what, a warrant? Is this about a warrant now? Nobody said anything about the police, I thought it was a bill, and now I'm hearing it's, I don't know, court or something, and that's even more reason I'm not giving you my name over the phone, honestly. If it's a real warrant I'd think a person would turn up at the door, wouldn't they? Right, I'm going to look up the real number and ring them myself, so, thank you, goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's the scheduling assistant over at [COMPANY_A], I'm calling about the bathroom tiling quote [PERSON_2] put together after the visit last Thursday, uh, Friday, sorry, last Friday, and I just wanted to run back over the scope with you real quick and see if you wanted to pick a start date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hi, yes, this is, uh, yes it's me. Sorry, I'm, um -- the bathroom tiling, you said? I mean, I think someone did come round, but was it, uh -- sorry, it was a while back, wasn't it? Who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, it's [COMPANY_A], we're the independent tradesperson outfit, [PERSON_2] was the one who came out to the house and measured up the bathroom, uh, hang on, sorry, [PERSON_2]'s van is just reversing in behind me, bit of a racket, anyway -- so it was last Friday, not that long ago, and the quote was for the full floor and walls, the tiling, I mean, so what I was ringing about is whether you'd like to pick a start date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, sorry, I can hear the van, that's fine. Um, the thing is, I'm not sure I remember [PERSON_2] coming on a Friday, I'd have to think. Did I ask for a quote, or was it, uh -- sorry, I'm a bit muddled. Could you just tell me again what the quote came to, and who it was that arranged the visit? I just want to be sure we're talking about the same house.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, sure, so the quote, we had it at [AMOUNT_1] for the, uh, the tiling and labour, and you rang us originally, well, I think the visit was booked through, hang on, you said you want to be sure it's the same house, right, so it's the one in [CITY_1], the, uh, the bathroom upstairs? And sorry, you said [PERSON_2] came on a Thursday? Yeah, that's -- no, it was Friday, but anyway, the scope was the floor and the walls and the, um, the grouting, so whenever suits for a start date, I can pencil you in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Um, well -- sorry, I didn't say Thursday, I think that was you, wasn't it? Uh -- hang on. And I'm, well, I don't actually have a bathroom upstairs, so I'm, um, not sure that's my house you've got there. Sorry, I'm really not trying to be difficult, I just -- um, so you're saying you'd put me down for a date, but I haven't, I mean, I don't think I've said yes to anything yet?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, you're right, sorry, that was me with the Thursday, I got my days crossed, and no, you haven't said yes to anything, I'm only pencilling, nothing's booked, so, uh, anyway, hang on, no bathroom upstairs, right, so I've probably got the wrong house on my sheet, um, let me check, it'd be easier if you just tell me the address the visit was at, or, uh, actually, better, is there anything [PERSON_2] left with you, like a card or a quote sheet, because that'd have [ACCOUNT_REF] on it, and I can match it up, uh, yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, hang on, the kettle's just gone off, one second -- right, sorry, I'm back. Um, a card or a quote sheet, you said? I don't, I mean I don't think anyone left me anything, and I'd have remembered a van outside, wouldn't I? And, sorry, it's a bit odd, isn't it, you ringing me for the address, when you're the one who's meant to have it? Could you maybe just tell me what number you've got on your sheet, and then I can say if it's mine?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, a number, right, so the number on the sheet, it's, well, hang on, it's actually the other way round, you said it's odd me ringing, and it's not, I mean it's, uh, the van, yeah, [PERSON_2]'s van, you'd have remembered the van, so I'll get him to ring you from his own phone, that's [PHONE_1], and he can tell you the street and the house number and the lot, because honestly I'm just the scheduling end, I don't have the, uh, the full address on screen in front of me, so -- sorry, did you say kettle? Because I thought you said cattle, and I was going, uh, no, we don't do that sort of job, we only do tiling.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, no, kettle, sorry, the tea kind, not cattle. Um, but, sorry, I'm still a bit lost. You said you'd got me down for a house with an upstairs bathroom, and I haven't got one, and now you haven't got the address on screen, so I'm not sure how you found my number at all? I think, uh, I'd rather not have anyone ringing me from a mobile about a job I don't remember asking for. If [PERSON_2] did measure up somewhere, it was probably the wrong house, and I'm sorry, I know that's probably not what you wanted to hear. I think I'll leave it there, if that's all right. Thanks for ringing, and, um, good luck finding the right person. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fine, that's, I mean -- look, I'm sorry, I think it's on me, I've clearly got the wrong sheet in front of me, and, well, honestly, you're right not to go on with it when the details don't match, so I'll, uh, I'll take your number off the list and have [PERSON_2] go back through the visits, and, sorry, sorry for the muddle, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, thank you, that's very kind. Um, sorry, did you say you'd take me off the list, or the lift? Because I haven't got a lift either, we've just got the one set of stairs, so you'd be quite right to cross that one off as well. Anyway, no harm done, honestly. Thanks for ringing back to say, and, um, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, the list, yeah, the list, not a lift, we don't do lifts either, just tiling, so no, nothing to cross off on that front. Right, so, no harm done, you've got my apologies for the mix-up and [PERSON_2] will sort the sheet out, and, uh, thanks for being so patient with me, really, so you have a good afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's alright, no trouble at all. Um... well, uh, you have a nice afternoon as well, and I hope the tiling people get it all sorted, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Hello, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, uh, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance team -- hello, can you hear me all right? I'm just returning a missed call about a fault you reported, sorry to catch you out of the blue.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I can hear you. A fault I reported? Sorry, who's this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yes, of course. It's [PERSON_2], I'm a case handler with the regional maintenance team at [COMPANY_A] -- I'm, uh, just calling because one of our engineers had a missed call from this number about a fault that was reported. Are you still there? Sorry, the line's a bit crackly my end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a missed call from my number? Uh, I didn't, I haven't rung anyone about a fault. Which, what was it, a fall? Is somebody hurt? I'm, I'm at work, I've got people around, so I'm a bit, can you just say again who you're with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, no, sorry, I've worded that badly, nobody's hurt, not at all. Fault, f-a-u-l-t, so a problem with the supply or the equipment, nothing to do with anybody falling. I'm with [COMPANY_A], the regional utility maintenance team, and what I've got in front of me is a note that a fault was reported on this number, and the engineer rang back and missed you, so he's asked me to follow up. I'm, uh, I'm sorry, I know it sounds a bit out of the blue when you're at work, and honestly if it wasn't you who reported it, it may well be someone else at the address, or I've got the wrong number down, that does happen. Are you still there? Sorry, I just keep thinking I've lost you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so a fault with the supply or equipment, right, not someone hurt. Uh, still here. But I haven't reported anything, and I'm at work, not at home, so I wouldn't know what's going on at the address. Which address have you got down? And what's the company called again, I didn't quite catch it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, the company, yes, it's [COMPANY_A], the regional utility maintenance team, [COMPANY_A]. And the address, hang on, I've got it here somewhere -- it's on [PERSON_3]'s road, no, sorry, that's the engineer's next job, I've mixed up my notes. Uh, it's a [CITY_1] address, but I'd rather not read it out down the phone to someone I haven't properly confirmed, if that's all right. Oh, and you said you're at home, sorry, so you can see the fault from there, that's helpful -- no? You're at work, I beg your pardon, I misheard. Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I said I'm at work. At work. I'm not at home. And, hang on, you've got an address you won't read out, but you're the one who rang me? So you've got a fault at an address and a number that might be the wrong number, and you can't tell me which address. That's, that's a bit back to front, isn't it? If you're really from [COMPANY_A], what's the reference for this fault, and is there a number I can ring you back on, through the company, not this one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, sorry, that is back to front, and I've made a muddle of it. Did you say you'd ring me back, though? Sorry, I thought I heard you say you'd rather stay at the address, and I don't, it's nothing like that, you don't need to be there at all. The reference is whatever you were given when you reported it, [ACCOUNT_REF], that's the one on my screen. But I can't promise it's yours, and I can't tell you when the engineer would come either, it depends on an earlier job overrunning. Honestly the safest thing is to ring the published fault line yourself, the one on the company website, not a number from me, and ask them to check the booking and give you a firm slot. I'd much rather you did that than took my word for it. Are you still there? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, you said stay at the address? No, I never said I'd stay anywhere, I said I'm at work. And you want me to ring you back, no, wait, you said ring the published line. Okay. So the reference on your screen is [ACCOUNT_REF], and that's from when I reported it, except I didn't report anything. Right. So I'll find the number on the company website myself and ask them. And if there's nothing on their system, that's that. I'm going to do that, yeah? Sorry, I've got people waiting on me here. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, of course, you do that, that's the right thing to do. And if there's nothing under your name, then I've simply got the wrong number, and I'm sorry for the bother at work. Right, I'll let you get on. Bye now, sorry again.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. No worries. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, sorry, just, uh -- hello? Are you still there? No, I think you've gone. Right, well, take care then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say still there, or, uh, still care? Oh, no, I think it was there, wasn't it. Sorry, I keep mishearing, it's this line. Right, well, bye then, and do ring the published number, won't you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, there, I said there. And I'll look the number up, but not today, I don't think, I'll leave it till I'm home. Anyway, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, till you're home, yes, that's fine, no rush at all. Sorry, did you say bye now, or, uh, buy a phone? No, no, I'm being silly, that wouldn't make sense. Right, I'll leave you be, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye now, I said bye now. Right, I really do have to go, so, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I haven't caught you at a bad moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, yes, that's me. No, no, you're all right, I was only sitting here. Who's calling, dear?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh good, thank you, that's kind. My name is [PERSON_2], I'm with the, uh -- I'm calling from the compliance side at [COMPANY_A], it's the fraud team there. It's nothing to worry about, I'm just, well, I'm ringing to check a couple of things with you, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, the fraud team, goodness. Well, that sounds a bit serious, doesn't it? Is something wrong with my account, or, uh -- sorry, which company did you say again? I didn't quite catch it, the telly's on in the other room. I do like to leave it on, you know, for the company.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's perfectly all right, I should have said it more clearly. It's [COMPANY_A], the fraud and compliance team, and I'm [PERSON_2], that's the name I gave. And it's a good question to ask, really, you can't be too careful these days, I'd rather you asked. Now, I wouldn't say anything is wrong, exactly. It's more that a charge was attempted on your account earlier, a little while ago, and it flagged with us. Probably nothing, but I'd just like to go through it with you, if you've a moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a charge, goodness. Well, I haven't bought anything, not today anyway, I've hardly been out of this chair. Though, hang on, you said at the start it was nothing to do with my account, didn't you? Or no, that was, you said it was nothing to worry about, that's it. I get muddled. Which account is it, dear, because I've got the one at the, uh, the post office and then there's the other one, and my daughter set that one up so I never quite know.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, nothing to worry about. It's the one with us, the [COMPANY_A] account. Could I just confirm a couple of details first, so I know I've got the right [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, I mean, I'd like to help, dear, I would, but now you've got me thinking. You rang me, didn't you, so you ought to know who I am already? That's what my late husband would've said, he was ever so particular about that sort of thing. He wouldn't tell the milkman his own name if the milkman hadn't said it first, honestly. And I'm not sure I've even got an account with, what was it, [COMPANY_A]? It might be the one my daughter did, she sorted out all the computer things when I moved, and I never really looked. She's in [CITY_1] now, she rings on Sundays. So what sort of details were you wanting, exactly? Only I don't want to say the wrong thing and get myself in a muddle.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Your husband sounds like he had the right idea, and I'd say the same to anyone. Now, I do have your name here, that's, well -- that's not the issue, it's more that I have to be sure it's you I'm speaking to before I go into anything about the account, it's just procedure. So, if you could just confirm your date of birth for me, and your address, that would -- and then we can see whether it's the one your daughter set up. It's really best we sort it today, I wouldn't want it left sitting.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hmm, well, before I say anything, can I go back a bit? You said a charge was attempted earlier and it flagged, and then you said it was probably nothing. Which is it, dear? Only if it's probably nothing, I can't see why it has to be sorted today. My husband used to say if somebody's in a rush, you slow down. And you still haven't told me what the charge was, or where, or how much. Surely you'd know that much if you're the fraud team? I'm not being difficult, I just like to have things straight in my head.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I'm glad you're going back over it, I'd much rather you did, it's how it should be done. Now you said, uh, if it was a rush -- sorry, a rash? You're worried about a rash of these, is that it? No, no, it's only the one attempt, one charge, so you needn't think it's been happening all over. As for the details, the amount and where, that's all in the file, and I'll go through it with you properly, but I do need the date of birth first, and then we can look at it together. I'd only say, the longer these sit, the harder it is to put right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hang on a tick, dear, there's the kettle going in the kitchen. I've been meaning to take it off for ages, it does that thing where it clicks and then clicks again. Right, I'm back, I've just turned it off. Now, a rash, no, I said a rush, if somebody's in a rush. But never mind that. What I'm hearing, and correct me if I've got it wrong, is you can't tell me the amount or where, but you can tell me the date of birth you want from me. That seems the wrong way round, doesn't it? If you've got it all in the file, you read me the amount and the shop, and then I say, oh no, that wasn't me, or oh yes, that was my daughter. Why can't we do it like that?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, now, you said two turns back that I told you it was nothing to worry about, and then that it was probably nothing, and I can see how those sit oddly together. I meant that you haven't lost anything, so there's no cause for alarm, but the attempt itself still needs looking at. That's all I meant. Now as for reading you the amount and the shop first, that's a fair way to do it, I do see that, it's just, well, I'm not able to open the file until you've been verified. That's the order they have us do it in. Would it help if I rang you back a bit later, once you've had a think, and we could finish it off then?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: A ring back later, well, that's very civil of you, dear. But I wouldn't know it was you ringing, would I? Anybody could say they were from [COMPANY_A]. And you said earlier you'd already got my name and the whole file, and now you can't open the file at all, so I don't quite see how that goes. I think what I'd rather do is look at whatever it says on my card, or on the letters that come, and ring the number on that myself. My daughter said to do that once, I think, or was it the man from the bank? Anyway. I don't think I'll be giving you my birthday, love, no offence. It's been nice having a chat, mind. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No offence taken at all, that's, well, that's a perfectly reasonable thing to do, and your husband would've approved. I'd only say, if you do ring, it's best not to leave it too long. And I'll try you again myself later on, in any case, to finish this off. Goodbye for now, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, there's no need to ring me again, dear, I'll do it the other way round if I do anything at all. Thank you for being so polite about it, though. Mind how you go. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time, I know people are always in the middle of something. It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm a scheduling assistant there, we look after a few of the private landlords in [CITY_1], and I'm just ringing round to get some times in the diary for a routine property check, nothing dramatic, just the usual walk-through they like to do, and I wanted to see whether you'd got a morning or an afternoon that tends to suit better, because honestly I can work around most things, it's just a case of getting it pencilled in.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello? Sorry, I just, I was having a bit of a lie down, I've only just, yes. Yes that's me, I think. Who did you say you were with again? Because I rent my place, I don't, I mean, I'm not a landlord, if that's what you're after, though my sister did have a flat once and the boiler, oh, that was a nightmare. Which property is this, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you're the tenant, that's who I want, [PERSON_1], I'm with [COMPANY_A], we act for the landlord, so it's your flat, the one you're renting at the moment, just a quick walk-through, so did you want mornings or afternoons?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, right, sorry, I'm still a bit foggy. But hang on, going back, you said you look after a few private landlords, and then you said, what was it, the company name, I didn't quite catch it the first time. Say it again? Because my landlord, it's, well I just pay the rent, I've never heard anyone, there's never been a, what do you call it, an agent, calling me up before. So which landlord is it you're acting for, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [COMPANY_A], like I said, we act for the landlord, so mornings or afternoons? Look, there's also a thing with your deposit, it's showing as at risk on our side, and it's best we sort that between us rather than bringing in the letting agent or your housemates, so, mornings or afternoons?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, the deposit? What do you mean at risk? And why would it be best not to bring anyone else in, that's, I mean, that's a bit odd, isn't it? You still haven't actually told me which landlord, you just keep saying the company name, and I don't, I've never heard of them. I think I'd rather ring my own landlord, the one I actually pay, and ask him about this. How would I even check you are who you say you are?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Honestly, there's no need to make a whole thing of it, I'm only trying to help you out before it gets worse for the deposit. Mornings or afternoons?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'm not booking anything. I'll ring my own landlord and sort it out with him. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I mean, you can, of course you can, but if you ring round it's only going to get the letting agent involved, and then your housemates hear about it, and honestly the deposit side of it moves quite quickly once it's flagged, so the sooner we just get a time in the diary the less likely it is to turn into a bigger problem for you, and I'd hate to see that, because we really are just trying to help, so if you'd rather, I can pencil you in for the morning and we can leave it at that, and nobody else needs to be, uh, troubled with it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
