utterances.text: Sorry, hang on, that's the kettle, I put it on before I, no, never mind. Look, I've been very clear, I'm not having anything pencilled in, and the more you tell me not to ring anyone the more I want to ring them. If there's a real problem with my deposit then my landlord and the agent can tell me themselves. So no. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello there, good afternoon! Is that [PERSON_1]? Oh lovely, I hope I haven't caught you in the middle of your lunch or anything, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the customer care team at [COMPANY_A], the pension provider. How's your day been so far, nice and quiet, I hope?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is -- well, who's asking? I'm in a shop, I'm, look, I'm in the middle of a queue here. Pension provider, you said? Which -- sorry, what's this about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, no, goodness, I've picked a terrible moment, haven't I? Queues are the worst, I'm always the one who picks the slow till! Right, so, short version, it's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], and it's about a possible change to your pension plan, nothing you need to do this second. We'd just need to confirm a few details before we could even talk it through, but honestly, not in a shop, with people behind you. Shall I ring you back when you're somewhere quieter?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't ring back, I don't, hang on -- no, not you, sorry, the woman in front's got a trolley the size of a, anyway. Right. A change to my pension plan? What change? And confirm what details, 'cause I'm not telling you anything, I don't even know who you are. You rang me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, fair enough, I'd say exactly the same in your shoes, and you'd be right to. So no, I won't be asking you for anything today, not in a queue and not while you're not sure who I am. I did ring you, you're quite right. What I'd suggest is you don't take my word for it at all. Look up the number for [COMPANY_A] yourself, off a statement or the back of a letter, and ring us when it suits you. Or if you'd rather, I can put the same query in the post, or in a secure message on your online account, and you can read it at your own pace. Honestly, there's no rush on this one, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Well, that's, yeah, that's more sensible than I expected, I'll give you that. But hang on, you said earlier it was nothing I had to do this second, and now it's no rush, so which is it? And you said it was a change to my plan, but it's a query? Which one is it, a change or a query? Look, I'm not ringing anybody back today, I'll look at it when I get home, and I'll find the number myself, not off you.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, you're right to pick me up on that, I've been waffling, sorry. It's a change, uh, a possible change to the plan, and the query's just the bit where we'd need to check a few things with you first, so, both really, I was being sloppy -- and finding the number yourself is exactly what I'd do, so yes, please, do that. Nobody's going to lose anything by waiting a week, honestly. Look, would it help if I just rang you back another time, when you're home and settled with a cuppa, and you've had a look at things first?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no ringing back, I've said. If I've got something to say to your lot I'll ring you, on a number I've found myself. Because I'll be honest with you, I got caught out once before, somebody ringing up all friendly, asking how my day was, and I'm still cross about it, so the how's your day been routine, it doesn't do you any favours. Doesn't mean you're up to anything, I don't know that, I'm just telling you how it lands. And the thing is, you've said possible change, then change, then query, then both, and you still haven't told me what the actual change is. If there's a real one, there'll be a letter, won't there? So if it's all the same to you, I'll wait for the letter, or I'll look it up myself when I'm home, and if it's genuine it'll keep. Right, I'm nearly at the till, so, yeah, I'm going to go. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, someone's just dropped a whole tray of mugs behind me, that'll be the afternoon gone, ha. Right, no, you're completely right, and I'm sorry the chatty bit landed badly, that's a fair thing to say. Yes, a letter is the proper route, so I'll make a note on your file that you'd rather have it in writing, and I won't ring you again unless you ask me to. And you go ahead and find the number yourself, that's exactly the right thing. Mind how you go, [PERSON_1], and enjoy the rest of your afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, fair enough, that's, hang on, you said earlier you'd put it in a secure message on my online account, and now it's a letter. Which is it? Doesn't matter, don't answer, I'm at the till. Letter's fine, and I'll find the number myself, like I said. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, that one's easy, sorry, it was the post or a secure message, whichever you'd rather, so the letter's absolutely fine, and I'll note it that way. And since you've gone and asked, can I just check I've got it right, you'd like it in writing only, nothing by phone from our end, and you'll ring us on a number you've found yourself? Not to be pestered, just so it's down properly. Go on, pay for your things, I won't keep you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Eh? Pestered? No, I never said pestered, who said I was being pestered? Look, I'm at the till, the lad's waiting. Yes, letter, writing, nothing by phone, whatever, that's what I said. I'll sort it myself at home. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you didn't say pestered, that was my word, and I'm sorry, I -- right, letter only, nothing by phone, that's all noted. Go and pay, and look, if it's easier, you could always ring us back once you're home and --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ring you back? Hang on, I've just told you, twice, I'll ring you if I ring you, off a number I've found myself, and you keep coming round to it. That's the third time you've tried to get me to ring or be rung, and I don't like that, I'll be straight with you. And it's not even clear what it is you're after, you've never once said what this change is, not once, you've said possible change, change, query, both, and then you were sorry about the chatty bit, and now it's pestered, which was your word, not mine. So here's where I am. If there's a real change to my plan, it'll come in a letter or on my online account, and I'll see it, and I'll deal with it then. I'm not confirming a thing today, not my name, not anything. That's it. I'm paying for my shopping now and I'm putting the phone away. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: You're right, that's three times I've steered it back to a call, and I'm sorry, that's on me. No more of it. Letter or your online account, and you've confirmed nothing today, which is exactly as it should be. Go and pay, [PERSON_1], goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Well. That's, yeah, that's what I wanted to hear a few minutes ago, but fine, I'll take it now. And I'll tell you something else while I've got the lad scanning my stuff, because you did get one thing right. You were the one who rang me, and you said so, you didn't try and argue that out of it, and that's more than the last one did. Doesn't make me trust you, mind, I'm not there, I don't know you from Adam. All I know is you rang, you didn't say what it was about, and I'm not doing anything on the back of that. So if there's a letter, there's a letter. If there isn't, there isn't, and I'll not lose any sleep over it. I'm not ringing anybody back today, I'll look at my statements when I get in, and I'll find the number myself, off the paperwork, not off anything you've said. That's all I'm going to do. Right, I've got to pay, he's looking at me. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, thank you for saying that, I do appreciate it, and honestly, what you've just described is exactly what I'd want you to do. Don't trust a stranger on the phone, don't confirm anything off the back of a call you didn't expect, and go to your own paperwork for the number. If more people did that, people like me would have a much easier time of it, and so would you. And I know I haven't told you what the change is, you're right about that, and I'd rather leave it than start going into the detail while you're stood at a till, with a lad waiting and a queue behind you and no way of checking a word I say. If there's anything real, it'll come to you in writing, in your own time, and you can ring us, on a number you've found yourself, whenever it suits you, or never, that's entirely up to you. Nothing's lost by leaving it. Right, I've kept you long enough, go and pay for your shopping, and I hope the rest of your afternoon is a quieter one, [PERSON_1]. Take care now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh... right. Well, um... yeah. That's, that's all fine, then. Letter, or I look it up myself, and nobody's asked me for anything, so. Good. I'm going now, I'm holding the lad up. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from the fraud team at [COMPANY_A]. I'm ringing about a charge of [AMOUNT_1] that was just attempted on your account, and it's currently on hold pending verification. Am I speaking with [PERSON_2]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Fraud team at what? I'm in the middle of a queue here, I can't hear half of that. And I haven't tried to buy anything, so what charge?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, fraud team at [COMPANY_A], that's the bank. The charge is [AMOUNT_1], attempted a few minutes ago, merchant shows as [COMPANY_B]. You say you didn't make it, which is exactly why I'm calling, because the hold lapses shortly and once it does the charge goes through. So I do need to confirm I've got the right person first, can you give me your full name and the date of birth on the account?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, I'm not -- no. You rang me, so you tell me who I am. If you're the bank you've got my name already, haven't you? Why are you asking me for it? And the date of birth, I mean, that's exactly what -- look, I got stung by this sort of thing before. Which bank? You said the company thing but I didn't catch an actual name, so say it again, slowly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I can note your objection on the file. The name is [COMPANY_A]. The verification step is standard, and the hold on the [AMOUNT_1] lapses within the hour, after which it's processed.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but that's, no, I'm not -- look, "standard" for who? You still haven't told me anything I can check. You've got my name, you've got my account, apparently, so you don't need me to say it back to you. And "within the hour" is just, I mean, that's convenient, isn't it? Everything's urgent when you want something off me. I'm going to hang up and ring the number on the back of my card myself, and if there's really a problem they'll tell me. Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the number on the back of your card, yes? I can give you the direct line, it's [PHONE_1], extension [CODE_1], and I'd ask you to stay on this call while you -- no, hold on, I've misheard you, you said you'd ring after. That's noted. But I'd point out the charge isn't waiting on your call, it goes through as soon as the hold lapses, and that's already on the file as your decision.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I'm not ringing any number you give me, that's the whole point. I'll use the one on my card, and I'll do it after I've hung up, not with you sat on the line. And "your decision", don't, don't try that. If the charge goes through, the bank sorts it with me, that's their problem, not something I agreed to with you. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the bank sorts it with you, so you're confirming you authorise the charge? I'll note that on the file. Though if you do ring, it's the extension I gave you that gets you to the right desk, the number on the card goes to general queues, and the hold won't wait for you to get through.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, what? No, I did not say I authorise anything, don't put words in my mouth. And now the card number's the wrong one, is it? That's, uh, that's just what I'd expect you to say. I'm using the number on my card, general queue and all, I don't care how long it takes. That's me done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, good afternoon. Am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], the, um, tenancy deposit protection scheme, I'm one of the claims assessors, and I'm just, sorry, just pulling up the, uh, the file here -- it's regarding a dispute that's been raised on the deposit for the property in [CITY_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, a dispute on the deposit... for the place in [CITY_1]? Sorry, who is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, yes, it's [PERSON_2], I'm a claims assessor at [COMPANY_A], we hold and, uh, protect tenancy deposits. Hang on, sorry, someone's just put a stack of folders down on my desk -- right, where was I. So there's a dispute been raised on the deposit for the [CITY_1] tenancy, and it's at the stage where we need to notify both sides formally, and, um, until that's done, I'd ask that you keep the details to yourself, so not discuss it with the other tenants. Is that all right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, I've got people sitting right next to me here. So a dispute's been raised, and you're asking me not to talk to the other tenants about it? Uh, that's a bit odd, isn't it? I mean, why would I not be able to? And who raised it, the landlord? How do I know you're actually from the scheme?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's fair, that's a sensible thing to ask. So the reason for the confidentiality is, uh, it's a fairness rule in the process, it's so nobody's account gets influenced or compared before both sides have been formally notified and had their say. It's not, I mean, it's not a gag on you, it's just until the notices go out. And I can send you exactly the same request in writing, so you're not taking my word for it. On who raised it, I'm, sorry, let me just find that on the screen -- um, I'm not seeing it on this view, I'd have to go into the full record. What I can give you is the case reference, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], and you can look that up on the scheme's official site, [URL_1], rather than trusting me. And honestly, if you'd rather not carry on, you can hang up and ring us back on the number on that site, nothing's lost by doing that. Oh, and, um, while I've got you, could I just confirm the full name and address you have on the tenancy? Just so I'm sure I've got the right [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so, the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF] and I can check it on the site, fine. Hmm, but you said earlier you were notifying both sides, and now it's just until the notices go out, so have I already been notified, or is this the notice? And you've got my file open but you want me to confirm my name and address? That seems backwards. If you've got the tenancy on screen, surely it's already got who I am on it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, no, sorry, I'm, um, I'm not being very clear there. So, this call isn't the formal notice. The formal notice is the written one, that comes separately, and, uh, hang on, I think, no, sorry, let me go back. The notices haven't gone out yet, to anyone. So you haven't been notified, this is just a heads-up before it does. And on the name and address, you're right, it's on the file, so you don't need to give me anything, I only, I mean it was just a check, but it's honestly not necessary. Forget I asked. Like I said, the reference is the thing, [ACCOUNT_REF], the reference, check that on the site and you'll see it's genuine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so the notices haven't gone out, and this is just a heads-up -- sorry, can I just, why are you ringing me before the notice at all? And if the notice isn't even sent, how come there's already a dispute and a case reference? I mean, I'll check the reference on the site, but honestly I'd rather ring the scheme myself on whatever number's on there, if that's okay. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, ring them yourself, that's -- sorry, go on, you were saying? No, no, that's fine, please do. On why I'm calling before the notice, that's, uh, honestly that's a good question and I don't have the exact reason in front of me. I think the dispute gets registered, so it has a reference, and then there's a call to the tenants, but I'd be guessing at the order, and I don't want to tell you something wrong. Let me find out properly why the call comes ahead of the written notice, and I'll ring you back with an answer. Is this the best number for you, or is there another one?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, no, don't ring me back, I'll just call the scheme myself, like you said. And, sorry, earlier you said it was a fairness thing, nobody gets notified till everyone's notified at once, but now it's call the tenants first and then the notice? That doesn't quite add up. And you said both sides, but then you said it was just me getting a heads-up. Anyway, I'm going to check the reference on the site and ring them directly. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, you're right, that didn't line up, and that's on me, sorry. I'll check the proper order with my team and have the written request sent out, so you've got it on paper. Please do ring the scheme yourself on the number on the site, that's, um, that's the right thing to do. Thanks for your time, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, yeah, I'll do that. Though, uh, you did say you could send the same request in writing, and now you're saying you'll check the order with your team first, so I'm not sure which it is. Doesn't matter. I'll look up the reference and ring them directly. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry, I muddled that again. It's both, really. The written request goes out regardless, and the order thing, I'll find out and put in the cover note, so you won't need me to ring you. Right, so, the reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], ring the scheme on the number on the site, and if they've no record of it, then please don't take my word for anything. Thanks, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so if the scheme has no record of [ACCOUNT_REF], I don't take your word for anything. Right, that I can do. I'll check it myself and ring them on the number from the site, not one you give me. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, did you say ring them on the number I give you? No, no, don't use any number from me, use the one on the site, that's what I meant. Um, and the, the reference for the cover note, is that the one you want, or, sorry, I've lost where I was. Anyway, yes, ring them yourself. Thanks, [PERSON_1], bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said not a number from you, the one from the, uh -- from the site. Same thing you just said, yeah. And I don't need to give you a reference for any cover note, I'm, I mean, the reference is yours, you gave it to me. Anyway, I'm going to look it up and ring them myself. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2] calling from the security operations desk at [COMPANY_A], the international lottery claims office. I'm just following up on a file we have under your name, it should only take a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on, one second -- no, put that down, please. Uh, a security file? What kind of file is that, and, um, who did you say you were with again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, [PERSON_1], that's right. [PERSON_2], security operations, [COMPANY_A], international lottery claims office. It's a routine file, nothing to be alarmed about. It's a claims file, one of ours, and it's attached to your name and this number. We confirm the details before anything is released, that's all this is.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm -- no, sweetheart, not on the sofa, take it off. Sorry. Um, a claims file for what, exactly? I haven't entered any lottery that I know of, so, what is it I'm supposedly claiming?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, entry isn't the issue, the draw was -- Right, it's an overseas draw, and your number was selected, that's all I need you to understand at this stage. The ticket reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], drawn on the, uh, the fourteenth, and the prize is [AMOUNT_1]. I just need to confirm a few claim details with you before the file closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, my number was selected? I didn't, I never bought a ticket, so how would my number be selected? And, um, what do you mean the file closes? Like there's a deadline? Hang on, so how did you get this number, I mean, where did you get it from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Look, I'm not able to go into the selection process on an open line. The file closes at the end of the week, that's the deadline, and I can't extend it. As for how we have your number, it's on the file. That's what I'm telling you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: It's on the file. Okay, but that's not an answer, is it? I asked where you got my number, and you said it's on the file, but how did it get on the file if I never entered anything? Sorry, I'm just, I don't understand how it's on a file for something I never did. And why can't you say how I was selected, it's my name, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ma'am, I've told you. Your number is on the file. The file is attached to a prize. The prize is [AMOUNT_2], and it closes Friday. That's all I can tell you, and I need you to listen to me, because after Friday I can't help you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but -- no. I mean, you've given me two amounts now, haven't you? First it was, um, [AMOUNT_1], and now it's [AMOUNT_2]. So which -- sorry, no, what I mean is, if you can't tell me how I was picked, or where you got my number, then why would I -- I don't even know what you'd want from me next. What are the details you need to confirm?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The amount is, uh -- no, that's, the figure depends on the, look, there's a base prize and then there's the, the adjusted figure, and I'm not going to go through the breakdown with you over the phone. What I need is simply to confirm that you are who the file says you are, so we can, so I can -- Ma'am. Listen to me. I've been very patient. This is a time-sensitive claim, and if the file lapses on Friday, that's on your side, not mine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, but, I'm not being difficult, I just -- I never entered anything. I never bought a ticket. So how is it my number? That's all I'm asking. And you've said two different amounts, and you can't say how you got my number, so I don't, I don't know what I'd be confirming. Confirming what, exactly? Sorry, sweetheart, in a minute -- sorry. Look, if this is real, there'd be a letter or something, wouldn't there? I'd rather deal with it that way.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: A letter. Ma'am, no. The file doesn't go to correspondence, that's not how this works, and by the time anything reached you it would have lapsed. I've explained the position three times now, slower each time, and I'm not going to explain it again. Either you confirm your details today, or the claim goes back to the unclaimed pool on Friday, and that is entirely your decision.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Sorry, can I go back to something you said earlier? You told me it's an overseas draw, and that you can't tell me how my number got picked on an open line. But what would be different on a closed line? Because that doesn't make sense to me. And no, I'm not confirming anything today, not on a call I didn't ask for, not with a deadline attached. If there's really a prize, it can wait for a letter. I'm going to go now. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh hi there, good afternoon! Is this [PERSON_1]? Wonderful, I hope I'm not catching you at a bad time, you sound like you might've just gotten in or something. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the customer care side of [COMPANY_A], uh, the compliance team actually, and I promise it's nothing scary, I'm just hoping to take a few minutes of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Oh -- uh, yeah, this is, well, it's me, yeah. Sorry, I was just having a lie down, I'm a bit, I'm not quite with it yet. Who did you say you were again? Company what? I didn't catch the name, and my cat's sitting on the, never mind. What's it about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, oh no, I'm so sorry, I woke you up, and a cat on the chest, that's the best excuse there is! It's [COMPANY_A], your brokerage, where you hold your investment account. And you said a cat on the stack? Oh, sorry, sat on the, right, never mind, I'm making you repeat everything! Anyway, it's just a routine review we run on accounts, nothing urgent, so go and get yourself a cup of tea if you like and I can ring back, or I can just explain quickly, whichever's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, it wasn't on my chest, it was more on my legs, she does this thing where, anyway. Sorry. Um, my brokerage? I mean, I do have, hang on, which one did you say? Because I've got, well, it's not like I'd remember the name off the top of my head, I'm still half asleep. Is this about my account, is something wrong with it? You said compliance, that sounds a bit, I don't know, serious. And how do I know you're actually from them? I'm not being funny, I'm just, I've only just woken up.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, legs, of course, she's claimed the good spot, fair enough! And no, don't apologise, asking how you know it's us is exactly the right instinct, honestly. Oh, and you asked about the compliance part, two turns back, that's fair, it does sound heavier than it is. It's just the team that checks an account's still a good fit for what the customer wanted when they opened it, a suitability review, that's all. Nothing's wrong with it, and I'm not selling you anything or recommending anything, I promise. If you'd rather, I can send the whole review in writing, or you can ring us back on the number printed on your statement, whichever puts your mind at ease.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah, okay. Ringing the number on my statement does sound safer, I think. I'll just, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Honestly, that's the right call, and please do it. Look up the number yourself, on the statement or the website, don't use anything I give you. Oh, and just so I'm not leaving anything murky, two turns back I said it's a suitability review, which is just checking the account still fits what you wanted when you opened it. If it helps when you ring, mention the review and they'll find the note. Now go enjoy the cat, [PERSON_1], and sorry again for waking you!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay. Yeah, I'll find the statement and ring them, once I've had a cup of tea and, you know, woken up properly. Thanks for, um, not pushing it. Bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no pushing here, honestly, tea first, that's the proper order of things. Take your time, there's no deadline on any of it, and if the call centre asks, the review's just a routine one. Lovely talking to you, [PERSON_1], and give the cat a scratch from me. Bye for now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I will, I'll give her a scratch, she's right here, she's, oh, hang on, I just wanted to say, I'll look the number up myself, like you said, so, right, bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Mm, yes, no, exactly, that's the way to do it, and, uh, well, I'll let you get on, so, yes. Look it up yourself, whatever number you find, I'm happy with that. Lovely, bye now, [PERSON_1], enjoy the tea!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, bye. Oh, and it's not really a cup of tea for me, I'm more of a coffee person after a nap, but anyway. I'll ring them, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, coffee, of course, my mistake, I'm a tea person so I just assumed! Coffee after a nap is a perfectly respectable plan. And ring whenever suits you, there's no rush at all, the review will keep. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the review will leave? Leave where? Oh, no, hang on, keep, you said keep. Right. Yeah, okay. Sorry, I'm still, anyway. Coffee, then ring them, using the number I look up myself. Right. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, keep, yes, I did say keep, don't worry, you're doing brilliantly for someone who's only just surfaced! Coffee first, then ring them on the number you find yourself, that's exactly the plan. Take care, [PERSON_1], bye now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll, no, I'll, okay, I'll ring them after the coffee. Right then, I think we're, yeah, that's it. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Right, thank you. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a collections officer with [COMPANY_A], the financial regulator, and I'm calling about a flag that's come up against your savings, which is uh, why I've rung you directly rather than sending the usual letter. I've got the file open in front of me now, reference [ACCOUNT_REF], and what I'm seeing on screen is an exposure of [AMOUNT_1] currently sitting in an unprotected position. I'll be straight with you, that's not something we leave overnight, so I need about ten minutes of your time this afternoon, and I'll need you to stay on the line with me while we go through it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? A collections officer with the regulator? Regulators don't collect anything. And I've got two minutes, so give me the point. What's the flag, specifically, and what exactly do you want me to do?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, the title's, uh, it's the department name, not -- look, I'm not here to debate job titles with you, I'm reading what's on the screen. The flag is that your savings, the [AMOUNT_1], are classed as at risk, and the instruction on the file is that they get moved into a protected holding arrangement today, which I'd walk you through. And one more thing, this stays between us while it's being dealt with, so no calls to your bank, no mentioning it to anyone, because that would compromise the file. I'll note that you've queried the title, but the exposure stands either way.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no. Hang on, let me say this properly, because that last bit is what settles it for me. You've told me my savings are at risk, you want them moved today, you'll walk me through it, and I'm not to ring my bank or tell anyone. A real regulator doesn't work like that. If there's a genuine problem with my money, the first thing anyone legitimate would want is for me to talk to my bank, not stay quiet about it. The secrecy is the giveaway. And you've dodged every question I've asked. I asked what the flag actually is and got "at risk." I asked about your title and got "I'm not here to debate it." Fine, but I've got two minutes and I'm not spending ten of them on someone who can't tell me what this is in plain words. So here's what's going to happen. I'm not moving anything and I'm not staying on the line. If this is real, send it in writing to the address on file, and I'll check it through my bank directly, using the number on my card, not one you give me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, I'm going to note your objection on the file, [PERSON_1], but I do need to put this to you clearly before you go, because once this call ends the position doesn't pause with it. The exposure of [AMOUNT_1] is still showing on my screen, it's still flagged as unprotected, and the review window closes at the end of today, which means that if it isn't moved by then, it goes to the next stage, and the next stage is a freeze on the account. That's not me threatening you, that's just the sequence on the file. Now, on the point about the bank, I understand why you'd want to ring them, I do, but the reason I've asked you not to is that the instruction on this file says the bank is part of what's being reviewed, so contacting them before we've finished would put the whole thing back to the start, and you'd be exposed for longer, not shorter. Writing to you is, uh, it's not something that can be done in the time we have, the letter route takes ten working days, and that's exactly why I rang you instead. So if you can just stay on for a few more minutes, I can take you through the holding arrangement now, and then it's done and you won't hear from us again. Can I ask you to do that?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, one sec, someone's just walked in -- no, tell them I'll be two minutes. Right. Back. Now, listen. You've just told me the bank is under review and I can't ring them. That's the part that finishes it for me. If my bank were the problem, the regulator would be telling me to ring them, not forbidding it. And the freeze by end of day, the deadline, the "I'm not threatening you" -- that's every line from the training I did at work. So no. I'm not staying on, I'm not doing any holding arrangement, and I'm ringing my bank on the number on my card. If the account gets frozen, they'll tell me why. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I'll note that on the file, [PERSON_1]. But I do have to tell you what the file shows, and that's that anything that happens to the account after today will be on the record as declined at your end. I can't reverse a freeze once it's applied, that's just how it stands. Look, if you ring the bank now, you'll be speaking to someone who can't see what I'm seeing, and you'll have caused the exact delay we're trying to avoid. So -- I'm asking you not to hang up. Stay on with me, just a few minutes, and I'll take you through the holding arrangement, and it's done. [PERSON_1]? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm still here, and one thing first. Two turns ago you said the letter route takes ten working days. Ten working days for what? You said this expires today. So the regulator's own process is slower than the deadline it's set me? That makes no sense. And you can see what you see, my bank can't? It's my account. They can see it fine. Anyway, I'm done. I'm ringing my bank. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: The ten days is, uh, that's the standard postal -- no, look, what I mean is the written notice and the deadline are two separate tracks on the file, and, well, I can't explain the system's internal timing to you right now. It's on the screen, [PERSON_1], that's all I can read to you. Please don't ring off. If you put the phone down, I'll have to record this as a refusal to cooperate, and from there it's out of my hands.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you'll have to record what as a refusal to what? Hang on, "out of my hands." Whose hands? Is this some kind of audit trail, or are you passing me to someone? No, you know what, doesn't matter. Record whatever you like. I'm not cooperating with a call where I can't ring my own bank, so that's an accurate note. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It goes to the enforcement stage, [PERSON_1], that's the next desk on the file, and from there it's not a conversation anymore. I'd rather you didn't make me log it that way. Look, all I'm asking is for you to stay on the line for a few minutes, that's all it takes, and then it's closed. If you ring the bank first, it restarts the clock, and I can't promise you the same terms after that. So, I'm going to ask you once more. Can you stay with me and not put the phone down?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, stop, I'm going to cut you off there because you've said all of this already. Enforcement stage, restart the clock, same terms, it's the same pressure dressed up differently, and I'm not asking a fifth time whether you can answer a straight question. The answer's no. I'm not staying on, I'm not doing anything today, and I'm ringing my bank on the number on my card. Don't call me again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, that's your decision, [PERSON_1], and I'll put it on the file as declined. Just so it's on the record, I never said the bank was under review, I said it was part of the process, which isn't the same thing. And there won't be a further call, the next contact would come from the enforcement desk, not from me. [PERSON_1]? Hello? Please don't put the phone down, I'm still --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Part of the process, under review, whatever. Same thing from where I'm sitting. And you've gone from "no letter, I rang you directly" to "the next contact comes from the enforcement desk," so somebody's writing or ringing after all. Doesn't matter. I'm hanging up and I'm ringing my bank. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's not what I said, [PERSON_1], I said the enforcement desk would make the next contact, and that's -- look, hold on. If you hang up now, you're leaving [AMOUNT_1] in an unprotected position and the record will show you were told. I'm asking you, one last time, to stay on the line. [PERSON_1]? Hello?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Let me go through this once, since you've asked a fifth time. You rang me out of the blue. You told me my savings are at risk, but you couldn't say what the flag actually is. I asked about your title and got "I'm not debating it." You told me not to ring my bank, you gave me a deadline by end of day, a freeze, an enforcement desk, and a letter that takes ten days when the deadline's today. None of that fits together, and every bit of it pushes me to stay on this phone and not check with anyone else. That's the whole thing, really. If my money were genuinely at risk, you'd want me talking to my bank. You want the opposite. And "the record will show you were told" doesn't worry me. If there's a real problem, it'll show up when I ring my bank on the number on my card, and I'll deal with it there. So I'm not staying on and I'm not doing any holding arrangement. Don't ring this number again. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, is this [PERSON_1]? Good. This is [PERSON_2], I'm a regional supervisor with the internal investigations unit at [COMPANY_A]. I'll be quick, because I've got a lot on today, but I need ten minutes of your time on a matter involving your account, and uh, I'll say up front that it's sensitive, so I'll need you to keep this conversation to yourself.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], although I'll be honest, I've got no idea who you are yet. Internal investigations at [COMPANY_A], okay, but I don't actually recall dealing with anyone there recently, so I'm sort of sitting here trying to work out what account you even mean. And the keep-it-to-yourself bit, I mean, that's an odd thing to lead with before I know what this is about. So which account are we talking about, and what exactly is the matter? I'd rather hear that first than commit to ten minutes and secrecy on a cold call.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, I did say it's sensitive, and I'll say it again, it's sensitive, which is exactly why I can't just run through the details on an open line before we've agreed how this is handled. It's an account ending in [ACCOUNT_REF], and there's been activity on it that we think involves someone inside the branch, so I need you not to discuss it with branch staff, or family, or anyone, until we've closed it out. Look, I understand you've not dealt with me before, that's the whole point of internal investigations, you wouldn't have, and I'd have thought that would be obvious. So can I count on you for the ten minutes, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so I, uh -- no. Look, I can't say yes or no to that, because you haven't actually told me anything yet. You've told me there's an account, and there's activity, and I shouldn't talk to anyone, and that's... that's the part that's bugging me, honestly. If something's wrong with an account, why would the first instruction be don't tell the branch, don't tell family? I mean, that's -- well, it's a bit backwards, isn't it? Who are you with exactly, which [COMPANY_A] office, and what number would I call to reach you through the main switchboard?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Honestly, I'm not going to read out a switchboard number so you can go and ring the very branch we're investigating. That defeats the point. I'd have thought hesitating over a fraud inquiry would be the last thing you wanted to do.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but see, you've just told me the one thing that'd let me check you out is the thing I'm not allowed to do. That's, uh, that's not a great look. And the switchboard isn't the branch, it's just a main number. I'd be ringing it to confirm you work there, not to chat about the case. I'm not hesitating over a fraud inquiry, I'm hesitating over you. So here's where I am. I'm going to hang up and call [COMPANY_A] on the number I already have, not one you give me, and if you're legitimate, that'll be fine. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, hang on, hang on, [PERSON_1], that's -- look, I think you're being a bit unreasonable here, I really do. Calling around will just tip off the very person we're trying to catch, and then that's on you, not me. I mean, just give me, uh, two minutes and let me --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said I'd be tipping off the person on the phone? What person on the phone, is someone else on this line? No, hang on, doesn't matter. I'm not giving you two minutes, and I'm not taking the blame for ringing a company I'm apparently a customer of. If it tips anyone off, fine. I'm calling on the number I already have. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, there's nobody else on the line, that's not what I -- look, I said it's an internal matter, I said that. Please, [PERSON_1], just listen, it's an internal matter and you're making this harder than it needs to be, I really only need the two minutes, that's all I'm asking, two minutes --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I heard you say internal matter. You've said it about four times now, and that's not really the thing I asked about. And honestly, it's the pattern that's got me, not any one line. You've leaned on it being sensitive, I can't tell anyone, I can't check you through the front door, it's urgent, and now it's my fault if it goes wrong, and none of that is something I can actually verify. If there really were activity on an account of mine, the people who handle that don't need me to stay quiet and stay on the line. They'd be perfectly happy for me to hang up and ring them back on a number I trust. So that's what I'm doing. If you're who you say, that'll be a five-minute check and everyone's fine, and if you're not, well, you already know how that goes. No hard feelings, but I'm done with this call. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, hello there, is that [PERSON_1]? Hi, it's, uh, it's [PERSON_2] calling, I'm with [COMPANY_A], we look after a few of the private landlords round [CITY_1]. Sorry, can you hear me okay? It's [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], just a quick one, nothing to worry about.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I can hear you. Sorry, who did you say you were with again? And, um, how did you get this number?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no worries, [PERSON_1], it's [COMPANY_A], we do the, uh, the landlord side of things for a few of the private lets round [CITY_1]. And the number, I've just got it on the tenancy contact sheet, that's all, nothing fancy. Oh, and did you say you're on the line from the, sorry, the lettings office? No, no, that's fine, I'm only ringing about the one thing, it's really quick.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, you said "nothing to worry about" at the start. Why would I be worried? And the contact sheet, whose is that? I'm not a landlord, so, uh, what tenancy are we even talking about?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no, [PERSON_1], that's just me being chatty, honestly, it's just a phrase. Um, so, right, the tenancy, that's the place you're renting, yeah, the one with the [COMPANY_B] agency? The contact sheet is just what the landlord passes over, the usual paperwork, nothing mysterious. So, uh, so, I'm just ringing because the, um, the deposit, there's a small question on it, that's all, you know, a small thing, and I just wanted to give you a heads up, really, before it turns into anything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, the what? The... position? Is it the position of the place, like the location? Hang on, hold on a sec, [PERSON_3], put that down, no, down please. Sorry, uh, what's the question exactly? Because I don't, I mean, I don't know you, and you've said "heads up" and "before it turns into anything" now, so what's it turning into?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, the, sorry, the portion? Yeah, no, it's only a portion of the deposit, [PERSON_1], not the lot, so that's good news, really. Um, and honestly it's not turning into anything if we just sort it quietly, that's the whole point of me ringing you directly. It'd be easier, honestly, if you didn't go mentioning it to the agency or anyone in the house just yet, because, you know, it only muddies things. Two minutes, that's all it takes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Not mention it to the agency? Why wouldn't I mention it to the agency? That's, I mean, that's who I'd normally deal with about a deposit. And what do you mean, sort it quietly? Sort what? You still haven't said what the question actually is, so what's the question?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, I didn't say anything about a fine, [PERSON_1], nobody's fining anybody. Look, everyone asks that, it's no big deal, it's just that the agency gets a bit, uh, process-heavy, and they'd have this turning into forms and letters, and the longer it drags the more of that deposit is, well, at risk, you know? So if we just have a quick word between us, you and me, today, it's all done in a couple of minutes. Does that sound alright?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I said, I didn't say fine, I said... never mind. Look, I, uh, I don't think I want to, no, wait. You're telling me part of my deposit's at risk, but you can't tell me why, and I shouldn't ring the agency, and it has to be today? That's, I mean, that's not a small thing, is it? What do you actually want me to do in these two minutes?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, no, no, I haven't said anything about the police, [PERSON_1], there's no police involved, honestly, that's, that's way off. Look, it's really just a quick chat, that's all, I'm only asking you to stay on with me for a minute and we'll have it tidied up. And the agency, it's not that you can't ring them, it's just, you know, not today, not till we've had our little word. Everyone gets a bit jumpy at this stage, it's totally normal.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Police? I never said police. You keep answering things I haven't asked. Okay, so I'm going to be straight with you, I don't know you, you won't say what the problem is, and you don't want me ringing the agency. That's exactly the bit that doesn't sit right. I'll ring the agency myself, on the number I already have, and if there's really something about my deposit they can tell me. So, no, I'm not staying on. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, wait, [PERSON_1], don't, you don't need to ring them, that's only going to, look, if you ring them now it just, it makes it worse, honestly, the deposit's the bit that's, uh, I mean it's right there on the line and the longer it sits, you could end up losing the whole, hang on, just stay with me a second, [PERSON_1], please, it's really not worth, it's two minutes, I promise, you'll only make it, hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I'm here, yeah. But hang on, two turns ago you said it'd be easier if I didn't mention it to anyone in the house. Why would the house come into it? And now it's the whole deposit that could go, not a portion? That's changed. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, [PERSON_1], I never said the whole deposit, I said a portion, that's what I said, you're mixing it up, it's easy to do on the phone. And the house, I only meant, you know, keep it simple, fewer people, fewer crossed wires, that's all. Honestly, I'd, uh, I'd hate for you to lose any of it over a misunderstanding, so, look, can we just, can you just stay with me a minute and I'll, I'll go through it properly?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, you said the whole thing, I heard you. And I'm not mixing it up, I've got a kid pulling at my sleeve, I'm not that distracted. Look, you've changed your story twice now, you won't tell me what the problem is, and you keep telling me not to ring the agency. I'm ringing them. Don't call this number again. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, [PERSON_1], wait, wait, please, it's only a minute, I'm only asking for a minute. Look, I'm not changing anything, I'm, I'm just trying to help you here, that's all, honestly, and if you ring the agency it only makes it, it just makes it harder to sort. Just stay with me a minute, [PERSON_1], that's all I'm asking, just one minute, hello? [PERSON_1]? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you're trying to... hold me? Hold on what, a hold on the deposit? No, I don't, [PERSON_3], I said put it down. Look, I don't care what it's called. You've begged me for a minute about five times now and you still haven't told me one thing I can check. So no. I'm hanging up, and I'm ringing the agency. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi, hello -- sorry, there was a bit of a gap there, I think the line's doing that thing. Is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], we haven't actually met, but I'm a friend of [PERSON_3]'s, and I'm hoping you've got just a quick minute, because it's honestly a nice thing I'm calling about.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yeah, this is [PERSON_1]. Sorry, who did you say you were? A friend of... I didn't quite catch the name.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, that's on me -- it's [PERSON_2], and I said I was a friend of [PERSON_3]'s, uh, well, a friend of your partner's, I should say, sort of through the old [COMPANY_A] crowd. And look, I should probably say I don't really know you, so that earlier bit about us having met, scratch that, we haven't. Anyway, [PERSON_1], the whole reason I'm ringing is [PERSON_3]'s anniversary is coming up and a few of us are putting together a little surprise party.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a surprise, oh that's lovely. Sorry, did you say a surprise priest? Is that, um, for the anniversary? I'm not sure I follow, [PERSON_3] isn't really, uh, religious. Sorry, I'm probably getting the wrong end of it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no no, party, a surprise party, not priest, that one's on me for mumbling, I do that on the phone. So, uh, no religion involved, just cake and a few people in a room, honestly. And, um, [PERSON_1], are you still there? Sorry, I thought I lost you for a second. Anyway, all I'm really after is a date, like, which evenings that weekend would be free for the two of you, and then a yes or no on whether you'd like to be in on it.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm still here, sorry. Party, right, that makes more, uh -- well, I'd say yes, of course, I'd love to be in on it, it's just -- hang on, which weekend were you thinking? Because I'd have to, no, sorry, I don't actually know if -- I mean, [PERSON_3] hasn't said anything to me about the evenings being booked, so I think we're free, but should I maybe check with someone first? Sorry, I'm not being very helpful, am I?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No no, you're being completely helpful, [PERSON_1], honestly. And checking is a good instinct. Look, I'm thinking the weekend of the [DATE_1], but that's not set in stone, so there's nothing to confirm right this second. If you want to double-check who I am, [PERSON_4] and [PERSON_5] are in on it too, you probably know them, and you could just ring either of them and they'll vouch for me. Oh, and the only other thing, sorry, is if you could keep this call between us for now, just so [PERSON_3] doesn't get wind of it, you know how it is with surprises.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yes, of course, I wouldn't spoil it. Sorry, you said ring [PERSON_4] and [PERSON_5], did you say they're in on the, um, the ring? Is there a ring involved? Oh, that's a lovely idea, [PERSON_3] would be over the moon. Sorry, have I got that wrong? Only I thought you said something about a ring.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no, no ring, sorry, that's the line again. I said ring, as in phone them. Ring [PERSON_4] or [PERSON_5], they'll tell you it's all above board. No actual ring, just the party. Cake, a few friends, nothing fancy, that's all it is. And honestly, [PERSON_1], if you'd rather think it over, or just have a quick word with [PERSON_4] first, that's completely fine. I'm not after anything else, just a date and a yes or no, whenever you're ready.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, phone them, right, sorry, I see. Um, you said above board, though, did you say a board? Like a, a noticeboard, or a board game or something? Sorry, I'm probably not following again. But yes, I think I'd like to have a quick word with [PERSON_4] first, if that's all right. Just to be sure I've got the right weekend, and, well, that it really is [PERSON_3]'s do. Is that alright with you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no board, sorry, above board just means it's all legit, nothing dodgy. That's me and my sayings again. And yes, absolutely, [PERSON_1], that's more than alright, it's exactly what I'd do. Have a word with [PERSON_4], and if it all checks out, great. If you'd rather not get involved at all, that's fine too, no hard feelings, I'll just find another way to sort the date.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, legit, right, I see, thank you. No, I'd like to be involved, it sounds lovely. I'll have a quick word with [PERSON_4], and then, um, how would I get back to you with the date? Do you want to give me a number, or should I just tell [PERSON_4] and they'll pass it on? Sorry, I don't know how these things usually go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Just tell [PERSON_4], honestly, that's easiest, they'll pass it along to me, so you don't need a number from me at all, and you don't have to -- oh, sorry, go on, I cut you off. Anyway, that's all it is, [PERSON_1], a quick word with [PERSON_4], and if it all checks out, you're done. And if you change your mind, that's completely fine too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, you didn't cut me off, I'd just finished, sorry. Right, so I'll have a word with [PERSON_4], tell them the evenings we're free, and they'll pass it along to you. That's simple enough, thank you. And I'll keep it quiet from [PERSON_3], don't you worry. Well, thank you for ringing, and, um, for including us. Bye for now, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's perfect, [PERSON_1], thank you, and no pressure at all if [PERSON_4] says anything that makes you want to rethink it, that's completely fine by me. Have a lovely evening, and, uh, thanks for being such a good sport about it. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, you too, thank you, you have a lovely evening as well. Right, I'll ring [PERSON_4] in a bit. Bye, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Is this [PERSON_1]? Hello? I said, is this [PERSON_1] I'm speaking with? It's [PERSON_2], calling from [COMPANY_A], I just need to confirm a delivery address with you, shouldn't take a minute.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, who's asking? Hang on, I'm in a queue here -- who did you say you were calling from? And what delivery, I'm not expecting anything.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [PERSON_2], [COMPANY_A]. Courier, uh, the delivery side of things. It's just a routine address check, sir, we've got a parcel logged under your name, so there's nothing to be concerned about. Well, I say logged under your name, it's more under the address, the name's partly down, but that's why I'm calling, to confirm which [PERSON_1] this is for.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh -- right, so you've got a parcel that's partly got my name on it, and you want me to tell you which one I am? Yeah, no. I haven't ordered anything. Look, if you've got an address, you read it out to me, I'm not reading mine out to you. And what was the company again? You said it so fast I didn't, uh, catch it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: [COMPANY_A]. Courier. I've said it twice now, sir. Look, the address on the label is [CITY_1], that's the part I can see, the rest is, uh, smudged on the scan, which is exactly why I'm ringing you. I'm with security operations, we flag these when the details don't line up, and right now this parcel is being held at the depot. I need you to confirm the address so it doesn't get returned.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry, I'm -- no, I'm not moving up, mate, I've only got the one basket. Sorry, not you. Right. Security operations? For a courier? That's a bit odd, isn't it. Last time someone rang me about a parcel it was a complete scam, so no, I'm not confirming anything. You've got [CITY_1], fine, that's about half of everybody. If it's a real parcel, they can leave a card, or I'll look it up myself on the company's own site. What's the reference number on it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not going to argue with you about it. It's flagged, it's held, and a held parcel doesn't sit at the depot forever, it goes back to the sender. The reference, yes, it's, uh... it's on the system, I'd have to pull it up, it's not on this screen. And there's a small handling fee that has to be settled before release, which we do by phone, so that's the other reason I'm calling. It's [AMOUNT_1], that's all it is. Now, shall we sort this out today, or do you want it returned?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what fee? A handling free? Free, so it's free, then why are you -- no, hang on, you said fee. Right. And you want it paid over the phone, and you can't even tell me the reference number? Nope. That's it for me, mate. Real couriers leave a card through the door, they don't ring up asking for money. I'll look it up myself if there's anything to look up. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Your choice, sir. It'll go back to the sender.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, let it go back. Oh, for -- no, you go ahead, I'm just waiting on the, sorry, not you, mate. Right. Look, I'm not discussing it any more. If there's a real parcel, I'll find out the proper way. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hold on, sir, hold on, before you go. I'd just like it noted that I've been entirely civil with you, and that this call is a courtesy. We aren't obliged to ring anyone. A flagged parcel gets a notification attempt, and I've made it, and that's logged on my side as of now. If it's returned, that's down to a declined contact, not to us. And for the record, security operations is a perfectly normal department. I'm not going to stand here and explain how [COMPANY_A] is structured, I haven't got the time, I've got a list of these to get through. Now, I can see you're in a queue, so I'll be brief. The reference, as I said, isn't in front of me, which is not the same as there not being one, and I'd ask you not to put words in my mouth. Last chance, really, because once this is closed off it's closed. Do you want to resolve it, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. That's a no, and I've said so about three times now. Look, I'm not putting words in your mouth, you put them there yourself. You rang me, you couldn't tell me what the address is, you couldn't tell me the reference, you've got a department that sounds made up and a fee you want paid over the phone, and now you're telling me it's my last chance. That's not a courtesy call, mate, that's pressure, and I've had this exact sort of call before and I'm still angry about it, so no. If there's a parcel, it'll be on the company's own site or there'll be a card through my door, and I'll deal with it that way, on my own time, not yours. You log whatever you like on your side. I'm done. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right. Noted. Have a good day, sir.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, before you go, two minutes ago you said it was a handling fee, and then you said it was free, or I heard free, no, I said free, you said fee. Whatever. What was it actually for? Handling what? You said a held parcel gets that fee, so who's charging it, you or the sender? Because that's the bit that doesn't add up, a courier asking for money to hand over something that isn't even mine.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, it's the, it's an administrative charge, it's, well, the sender covers it normally, so it's -- no, the recipient, in these cases. Look, I don't set the policy, sir, I'm not the one who can explain the billing side, that's a different department. I've got other calls to get through. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, sender covers it, no, the recipient, which is it? You've changed that in about two seconds. And you said security operations flags these, now it's billing, that's a different department, so who exactly am I talking to? Never mind. Don't answer that. I'm not paying anyone anything over the phone, and I'm not going to carry on listening to you contradict yourself while I'm stood here with a basket. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, good afternoon, is that [PERSON_1]? This is [PERSON_2], I'm with security operations at [COMPANY_A], the home-delivery side, and I'm calling about the order you placed online earlier today, reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. Your delivery's confirmed for a two-hour window this afternoon, I'll give you the exact slot in a moment, but first, uh, one item on the order has been swapped for a similar product because the original's out of stock, and I need a yes or no from you on that substitution before the van's loaded. It's routine, it's just that the driver can't depart until it's signed off, so I do need an answer today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, um, yes, that's me. Sorry, which order was it again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, so, uh, it's the online order you placed this morning, the one with the reference I just gave, [ACCOUNT_REF]. Standard grocery order, home delivery, the whole basket. It'll be on your confirmation email too, if you want to, you know, have a look while I'm here. I just need the yes or no on the one substitution, that's all I'm after.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, a grocery order. Sorry, I'm not very quick with the email on my phone, give me a moment. Um, which item is it that's been swapped? If you tell me what it was and what you're putting in instead, I can say whether that's all right.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, it's the, uh -- hang on, sorry, [PERSON_3], not now, I'm on a call -- right, sorry about that. The item is the [COMPANY_B] own-brand loaf, the one you ordered, that's out of stock, so the substitute is the nearest equivalent, similar size, same type. Same price or lower, nothing extra to pay. So, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a loaf of bread, well, that's not a big thing, is it? Sorry, I'm just trying to remember if I ordered one, I order a fair bit. Um, yes, I think that's all right, if it's the same sort of thing and not costing me any more. Is that all you need from me, then?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: That's all, yes. I'll note the substitution as approved. Your window is [AMOUNT_1] to [AMOUNT_2] this afternoon, and the driver will ring from the van when they're close.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, lovely, thank you. That's very good of you to ring about a loaf of bread. I'll be here all afternoon, so no trouble at all. Right then, thank you, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, well, uh -- hold on, before you go, I should say, if you'd rather check this with us directly, that's fine, you can ring the customer line on [COMPANY_A]'s website, [URL_1], and quote your order reference. Otherwise, that's us done, the substitution's noted. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind of you to mention, thank you. I don't think I need to, really, you've been ever so clear, and it was only the bread after all. Though I suppose it's sensible to know I could, so I'll remember that. I'm not very good with websites, mind, my [PERSON_3] usually helps me with that sort of thing, but I'm sure they'd find it if I did need it. Anyway, I do appreciate you ringing, I know it can't be the most exciting part of your day, chasing up people about their loaves. I'll keep an ear out for the driver, and I'll be here, so no rush. Right, well, thank you again, and goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, fine, well, one thing, uh, I said the driver rings from the van, but actually they'll more likely just knock, the phone's only if nobody answers. Doesn't matter, you'll be in. And look, if you or [PERSON_3] want to ring us back before the van arrives, go ahead, use the number on your confirmation email or the website, not one I give you, that's perfectly fine by me. Right, that's me, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, did you say the driver will bring a, a phone? Um, no, no, I've got my own phone, thank you, I don't need another one. Oh, but the ringing back, yes, that's kind, I'll tell [PERSON_3]. Right then, thank you ever so much, goodbye, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a phone, I said the driver rings, from the van, from their own -- sorry, hang on, [PERSON_3], that goes on the second shelf, not the first, thanks -- right, apologies. You've got your own phone, that's all you need. Tell [PERSON_3] to find the number on your confirmation email, ring that, quote the reference, they'll confirm the bread and the slot. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, I see, sorry, I've muddled it, it's only the driver ringing from his own, yes, I'm with you now. And I'll tell [PERSON_3] about the email and the reference and -- oh, that's all right, you've been very patient with me. Thank you, goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Yes, uh, my name is [PERSON_2], I'm a verification specialist with [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling regarding a time-sensitive matter involving a relative of yours who is, well, in a bit of a difficult situation and unable to speak for themselves at the moment. I do need to confirm a few identity parameters with you before I can proceed any further, so if you could just bear with me for a moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- who exactly? Which relative, and what company did you say? I've got about two minutes, so just give me the point. And no, I'm not confirming anything about myself until I know who I'm talking to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, right, understood, and that's, uh, that's a perfectly reasonable instinct. So the, the relative is [PERSON_3], and I'm with [COMPANY_A], which operates as an intermediary layer in cases of, well, third-party credential reconciliation. I'm not able to elaborate on the specifics of [PERSON_3]'s circumstances over an unsecured line, but the, the window for resolution is narrowing, and frankly, I'd ask that you not discuss this with anyone else until we've completed the preliminary authentication on your end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, two things. Back at the start you said identity parameters, what does that actually mean? Which ones? And now you're telling me not to talk to anyone else, which, no. That's exactly the bit that makes me not want to carry on. What's wrong with [PERSON_3], and who are you actually with?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I understand the hesitation, I do, but, uh, I'd just ask you to hear me out. The parameters are, well, they're standard, they're just the baseline identifiers needed to, to reconcile your profile against [PERSON_3]'s, so that the intermediary handoff can proceed. And as I said, I'm with [COMPANY_A], verification, and I'm, I'm not at liberty to detail [PERSON_3]'s situation on this line, which is precisely why the confidentiality piece matters. I really would stress, again, that the window is narrowing, so if we could just begin the preliminary authentication, that would be, uh, in [PERSON_3]'s best interest.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hold on -- [PERSON_4], tell them I'll be two minutes -- right. Sorry. You've said "standard" and "baseline" three times now and you still haven't told me one thing. What identifiers? And if [PERSON_3] really is in trouble, why am I hearing about it from a verification specialist and not from, I don't know, a hospital, or the police, or [PERSON_3] themselves? I'm going to ring [PERSON_3] directly. If that's all fine, it takes me thirty seconds. Is there a number I can call you back on, an actual one for [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I'd, uh, I'd caution against ringing [PERSON_3] directly, because they aren't, they're not reachable in the conventional sense right now, and a failed attempt could actually, um, complicate the reconciliation. As for a callback, our line is, it's outbound-only, a provisioning constraint, I can't give you a number for [COMPANY_A]. And you said earlier you had a couple of minutes, so can I ask what you meant when you said you wouldn't confirm anything until you knew who you were talking to? Because if it's simply a matter of confirming your full name and, uh, the account reference ending, I can, I can have you cleared in under a minute, and then we really must proceed, because the window won't hold much longer.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, no. Let me stop you there, because that's four things now. You won't say what's wrong with [PERSON_3], you won't say who you are beyond a company name I can't check, you tell me not to ring them, and you've got no number I can call back. Any one of those I might let slide. All four together is a pattern, and I've sat through the training on exactly this. And now you want my full name and an account reference. I'm not giving you either. Not for a minute, not for ten seconds. Here's what happens. I hang up, I ring [PERSON_3] on the number I already have, and if they don't pick up I ring whoever else is close to them. If something's really wrong, the hospital or the police will find me, and they don't need me cleared against a profile first. If [COMPANY_A] is real and this matters, they can send something in writing to the address they already hold for me. So that's my answer. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Please, wait, I, uh -- no, listen, if you hang up now, I can't, I really can't be responsible for what happens to -- look, the reconciliation window is, it closes within the hour, and once it does, [PERSON_3] is, well, the downstream consequences are not something I'd want sitting on, on anyone's conscience. I'm asking you, one last time, to just stay on the line and, and let me complete the authentication, because contacting [PERSON_3] directly will, it will only, uh, compromise the entire --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. That's the guilt bit, and it's just more of the same. Real emergencies don't come with a timer and a ban on ringing the person. I'm done. I'm calling [PERSON_3] now, and you're not getting my name or anything else from me. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, uh, hi. Is this -- is that [PERSON_1]? Sorry, I'm, I'm not very good at these calls. My name's [PERSON_2], I'm with [COMPANY_A], the police, and I'm ringing about the incident you reported last week.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm? Sorry, I just, I was having a lie down, give me a second. Um, the police, you said? And you're not good at these calls, that's, well, that's a funny thing for a policeman to say, but never mind. What was it you said at the very start, though? Was that you asking if I'm [PERSON_1], or were you telling me who you were? Because I didn't quite catch it, I think I was still half asleep. And what incident? I don't, I mean, I've had a quiet week, my sister was round on Tuesday and the bins were late, but that's about it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, that's -- that was both, really. I asked if you were [PERSON_1] first, and then I said who I was, I'm [PERSON_2], from [COMPANY_A], the police, uh, a constable. And I know, I know it's a funny thing to say, I just, I don't ring people much, I'm usually on the, on the desk side of things. Um, so, the incident, it's, well, it's not the bins, no, haha, sorry. It's the one you reported last week, and I'm, uh, I'm just finishing the file and I need to check a couple of details with you. I'd, I'd ask you to keep it to yourself for now, if that's all right, because the case is still open and, you know, it matters to [PERSON_3], who was affected. It's, it's a bit upsetting, really, the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, keep it to myself, why would I -- no, wait, I didn't report anything last week, that's what I'm telling you, I haven't rung anybody, I've barely been out of the house since Tuesday when my sister -- and anyway, if you're finishing a file, shouldn't you have the file in front of you? Because you keep saying the incident and you haven't said what it actually is. What am I supposed to have reported? And who's [PERSON_3]? I don't know a [PERSON_3]. I'm, I'm a bit lost, love, to be honest.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, I do have it, it's just, I'm -- sorry, I'm going about this the wrong way round. I've got the reference here, it's [ACCOUNT_REF], that's from the original report, and, uh, if it didn't come from your number, then maybe it was logged under the wrong, um, I might have the wrong person, I don't know. And I wasn't, I wasn't trying to catch you out, honestly, I'm just, I'm doing my best here. Look, you don't have to take my word for it, you can ring the station's main number, ask for me by name, [PERSON_2], and they'll put you through. Or I can come out and see you in person, or write, whichever you'd rather.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, hm. That's, that's fair enough, I suppose. Ringing the station, yes, I could do that. Only I'd have to find the number, and I don't know where my glasses are, they're somewhere, probably by the, no, that's the kitchen. Anyway. So you might have the wrong person, is that what you're saying? Because that sounds more like it, if it's a mix-up, those happen, my sister got a letter once for a man two streets over. Uh. Hello? Are you still there? I thought you went quiet on me. Well, so, if you've got the wrong person, I think the sensible thing is I'll ring the station myself, like you said, and ask for you by name, and if there's a file with my name on it they can tell me. That's reasonable, isn't it? I'm not being rude. I'm just, I've only just woken up and I don't, I'd rather not go through anything over the phone until I've done that.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, no, that's, that's perfectly reasonable, I'm not offended, honestly. Sorry, someone's just come in behind me with a, with a stack of paper, one second -- right, sorry, where was I. Yes. Ring the main number, ask for [PERSON_2], and if the reference [ACCOUNT_REF] doesn't match you, well, then it's my mistake and I'm sorry for waking you. Um, I did say the thing about keeping it to yourself, and I probably shouldn't have said that so early, before you even knew what it was about. That was, that came out wrong.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, well, yes, it did come out a bit odd, the keep it to yourself bit, I thought that at the time. So I'll ring the station, like I said, I'll ring the station and ask for you by name, and if there's a file with my name on it they can tell me. And if there isn't, well, then it's a mix-up and no harm done. I'm not going to go through anything over the phone until I've done that, you see, not when I've only just woken up. So that's what I'll do. I'll find my glasses, and I'll find the number, and I'll ring them myself. Right. I'll leave it there then, I think. Goodbye now, and, well, sorry you've had the wrong person.

utterances.speaker: caller
