utterances.text: No, that's, I mean, you've no need to be sorry, you've done exactly what -- what I'd tell anyone to do. Um, before you go, though, could I just -- no, sorry, that's not, it's fine. Actually, you'll want to know when the report was logged, won't you, so they can find it quickly, and I, uh, I haven't got the date in front of me, I only have the reference. I could find that out for you, if you like, and ring you back, or I'll just leave it, and you ring them, whichever's easier.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, don't ring me back, love. I'll ring them myself, they can find it without a date. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, of course, you ring them, you ring the station, that's, that's best, yes. Sorry, I'll not ring you back then, I just, I thought it'd help, but you ring them yourself, like you said. Um, [PERSON_2], that's who you ask for, [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A]. And, well, I'm sorry again about the, about the mix-up. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I've got that, [PERSON_2]. I'll, well, I'll ring them, I mean, I'll find the number first, and then I'll ask, no, I'll just ring the main one and see what they say. Right. That's, that's all then. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, wait, sorry, just one thing before you go, because I think I muddled you earlier. When you said you'd ring the station, I, I said ask for me by name, but I might be on the desk side, or I might be out, so if they say I'm not in, just give them the reference, [ACCOUNT_REF], and ask who's got the file. That's, that's what I meant. Sorry, I'm not explaining it well. Anyway, you go and find your glasses, and I'll, uh, I'll leave you be.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, all right, if they say you're not in, I'll give them the reference and ask who's got it. Though I'll look the number up myself, mind, I won't use one off you. Right, that's me. Goodbye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, I'm just calling to see how your pet's getting on after last week's -- sorry, did you say something? Anyway, I'm just calling to check on recovery and whether you'd like a follow-up visit booked, and we do close our booking lines at four today, so.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, hello? Sorry, I just woke up, I was having a little lie-down. No, I didn't say anything, I don't think. Last week's -- hang on, I haven't actually been to a vet in ages, I mean, not last week anyway, the cat's fine, she's just been sat on the radiator all day. Which surgery did you say you were? Because I think I always go to the one on, uh, [CITY_1] road, and that's not the name you said.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, that's fine, sorry to wake you. So this is [PERSON_1] at account services, [COMPANY_A], the veterinary surgery, and I'm just calling to check on recovery after last week's procedure and whether you'd like a follow-up booked. Uh, if it's not your pet, it may be a records mix-up on our side, but I do need to confirm that before four o'clock today when the booking lines close, so.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Well, a mix-up, yeah, that's probably it, because there wasn't any procedure, I'd remember that, she hates the carrier, it's a whole performance. Um, what do you need to confirm exactly? Because I'm not sure I want to be, you know, confirming things when I don't even know it's my vet calling. Can I just ring the surgery myself, on the number I've got? Sorry, I've only just woken up so I'm a bit slow, but that seems the sensible thing, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, that's -- sorry, I didn't mean to talk over you, but yes, ringing the surgery on the number you've got is exactly what I'd do, and honestly the procedure is we only confirm with the registered owner, so there's nothing you'd need to give me. I'm [PERSON_1], account services, [COMPANY_A], checking on recovery and whether you'd like a follow-up, and if it's a mix-up on our records, I'll flag it, but the booking lines do close at four, so if you did want to ring, it'd be before then.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, well, I will ring them then, on the number I've got, because I'm not really, I mean, I don't know who you are, no offence. And like I said, there wasn't any procedure, the cat's fine, she's on the radiator, so it's probably a mix-up like you said. Yeah, I'll just ring my own vet, the one on [CITY_1] road, and ask them. Thanks for calling, anyway, sorry I was a bit slow, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the cat's on the, uh, the tractor? No, radiator, right, sorry, bad line. Anyway, yes, no offence taken, you ring your own vet. Just one thing before you go, was it [CITY_1] road the surgery's on, or are you thinking of a different branch? Because I can't actually see from here which of our sites would've had your record, so I'll find out and call you back.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, I don't think I said which road, did I? I said the surgery on [CITY_1] road, yeah, but I didn't say it was a branch of yours, you're the one who said branch. And, uh, you don't need to ring me back, honestly, I'll ring them myself. Actually, no, wait, did I even say it was the vet on [CITY_1] road? I'm sure I said I haven't been in ages, so I don't know why I'd have gone and, anyway. Bye, thanks, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, you did say [CITY_1] road, I just -- it's fine, there's no need for me to ring back, you've got it, you ring your own vet. I'll find out which record this was and, uh, flag it on our side, and if there's anything to follow up, I'll call you, but otherwise you won't hear from me. Sorry again for waking you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, okay. I'll ring my own vet, then. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hi, uh, hello. Sorry, is this -- am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Okay, good. So, um, my name's [PERSON_2], and I'm calling on behalf of someone over at [COMPANY_A], the software retailer, because, well, they asked me to ring about your account, and I'm, I mean, I'm not the one who normally does this kind of thing, I'm sort of helping out, so forgive me if I'm a bit all over the place. I just wanted to check first that I've got the right person before I say anything else, because I'd hate to bother someone who isn't, you know, who isn't the account holder.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yes, hi, this is, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], sorry, I'm driving, you're on speaker and the reception's a bit rubbish out here. So who, um, who did you say you're calling from again? Sorry, I missed the company name, I think it cut out. And, uh, what account is this? Because I'm, I'm not sure I've got anything with a software retailer, but I might have, I don't know. Sorry, I know that sounds daft. Just, who is it you're calling from?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, no, that doesn't sound daft at all, sorry, it's me, I rushed it. It's [COMPANY_A], they sell software, you know, subscriptions and, and licences and so on. And I'm not actually, uh, I'm not calling from them exactly, I'm sort of passing a message along for a person there, [PERSON_3], who asked me to get in touch. utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, that's kind, thank you, but I can't really pull over just yet, there's, um, there's a bit of a lane closure and nowhere sensible to stop, and honestly it's only the reception that's bad, I can hear you fine, mostly. Sorry, I'm babbling, I always do that when I'm a bit nervous behind the wheel. But I'm, I'm sort of stuck on the, the who of it, if you don't mind. You're not calling from [COMPANY_A], you're passing along a message from [PERSON_3], who works there, and, and I don't think I know a [PERSON_3], and I'm still not sure I even have an account with them. I mean, I might, I've signed up for a few things over the years, you know, trial subscriptions, that sort of thing, and I never remember to cancel them. So, uh, when you say a problem with a payment, what, what actually is the problem? Like, which payment, and for what? Sorry, I just, I'd rather know what we're talking about before I, before I say anything, you know? And is there, is there a way I can check this is real, like ring the company myself afterwards? Sorry, that sounds terribly rude, I don't mean it to.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not rude at all, honestly. Um, you said you'd rather know what we're talking about, and, right, yes, so it's a, a double billing. utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon, this is [PERSON_1] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], your energy supplier. Uh, am I speaking with the account holder? I do need to be upfront, we've found two meter readings on file that don't match, and I'd like to get that sorted before our billing run closes today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, depends who's asking, really. You said [COMPANY_A], right? Which meter are we talking about, electricity or gas? And what are the two readings that don't match?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fair questions, and, uh, yes, [COMPANY_A], account services. It's the electricity meter. Our records show one reading from the last bill and a second one logged later that's lower than the first, which shouldn't happen, and I'll be honest, that mismatch is on our side, not yours. I'd rather not read figures out over the phone, though, since I haven't confirmed who I'm speaking with. All I'd need from you is the current figure on the meter, nothing else, and, um, we do want that in before today's billing run closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you said the bill's gone up on the meter? No, hang on, you said lower. Okay. So the reading's lower than before, which can't happen, fine. But you won't tell me what your readings are, and you haven't confirmed who I am either, so you've got me down as the account holder without a name. What name have you got on the account?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, lower, that's right. And no, I can't give you a name either, that's the verification procedure, I'm not permitted to disclose account details before the account holder is confirmed. Look, you don't have to do this now. Log into your account at [URL_1], check the readings there, and ring us back on [PHONE_1], and we won't change anything until you have.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, but hang on, you rang me. You're the one who wants a -- Okay, so I'm not logging into anything off a link you've read me down the phone. If I check, I'll go to the site myself, or ring the number that's printed on an actual bill. Not yours. And you've got the billing run closing today, but also nothing changes till I ring back. Which is it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's the right instinct, ignore the link, go to the site yourself or use the number on your bill. And you're right about the two things, that was sloppy. Today's run is just when I'd like it in, but nothing gets changed or billed until you've checked and given us the figure. Sorry, hang on, someone's just put a -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Where was I? Right, so there's no deadline on your side, the bill simply stays as it is until you ring.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh-huh. Right. So no deadline, bill stays as it is. Well, that's, uh... that's a fairly different call from the one I picked up a minute ago, isn't it? I mean, first it's the billing run closing today, now it's nothing happens till I ring. So I'll do what I said. I'll find the number on an actual bill, ring that, and if there's a mismatch they can tell me about it. Okay? Thanks for the call. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, yes, so, as I said, nothing is -- no, hang on. You're quite right, and honestly I'd do exactly the same. That cutoff was an internal target of mine, not a deadline on you, I should have put it better at the start. Ring the number on your bill, quote [ACCOUNT_REF] if you want, and they'll see the two readings on file. Sorry for the muddle, and, um, thanks for bearing with me. Bye for now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, quote what? A [ACCOUNT_REF], did you say, or was that, uh, a reference number off the bill? Hang on, I haven't got a bill in front of me, so no, I'll just ring the number on it myself and take it from there. Right, bye then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, [ACCOUNT_REF] is just the account reference printed at the top of your bill. You don't need it, and you don't need to tell me anything now, they can find you by name and address. Ring the number on the bill, and if you're not happy once they've gone through the readings with you, it's your right to ask for it in writing. Sorry again for the confusion, and thanks for your patience. Have a good afternoon, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yep. Will do. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, is that [PERSON_1]? Hang on, sorry, somebody's just dragged a bag of footballs right past me -- okay, right, hi. It's [PERSON_2] from [COMPANY_A], the community sports club, I'm one of the volunteers who helps with the junior teams. Got a quick one for you, [PERSON_1], nothing to worry about, just a change for Saturday's match.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, hi! Yeah, uh, yes, that's me, sorry, just give me a sec, I'm up to my elbows in the flower bed here, you're on loudspeaker. Um, so, the sports club, right, and a change for Saturday... I mean, I'm not sure which match you mean, we've got a couple of things on, but go on, what's the change?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, no worries, [PERSON_1], flower beds win every time, I'll be quick. So it's the junior match this Saturday, the one with your little one's team -- and, uh, so, yeah, the pitch is basically underwater after all that rain, so we've had to move it. It's now on the other pitch, the one by the clubhouse, and kick-off's gone back to [CODE_1] instead of the usual time, so, um, sorry, I know that's a bit of a faff, but it's honestly just a case of turning up a bit later at a different spot, that's all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, yeah, the rain, honestly, my tomatoes are loving it but nobody else is. Um, hang on though, I thought you said it was a match with, uh, my little one's team? Only I don't think we've got a match Saturday, I thought that was next week, it's the training session on Saturday. And, sorry, what time did you say? I didn't quite catch it, it sounded like a code or something, not a time.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hang on, [PERSON_1], sorry, you're right, that's me mangling it, it's the [CODE_1] -- no, sorry, I mean the time, it's half past ten, not the usual nine, I've got the sheet in front of me and I keep reading the wrong bit. And, uh, you could well be right about the match, [PERSON_1], it might be the training session that's affected, because they're all on the same pitch list, so either way it's the clubhouse pitch and the later start, honestly it's just a quick heads-up, nothing you need to do.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, okay, so half past ten, at the, uh -- sorry, the clubhouse pitch. Right. I mean, that's fine, I can do that, it's just, hang on, I'm, um -- so is it the match or the training? Because you said match, and then you said it might be training, and I, sorry, I don't want to turn up at the wrong thing. And, I mean, I don't think you've said, uh, which team it is, have you? What's, um, what's my little one's team called, I mean, which one have you got down?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, so the team, it's the -- no, hang on, let me -- sorry, [PERSON_1], I've got three sheets on the go here and I don't want to read you the wrong one. It's the under-whatever, the junior one, I mean I've got the age group down, but I'd rather check it than guess and send you to the wrong pitch. Honestly, that's a fair question, everyone asks, I'd ask too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Yeah. Right, so, um... you're just checking, and I'm just, sort of, standing here with a trowel, ha. It's just, I mean, it's odd, isn't it, because I'd have thought if you had my little one's team down, you'd, well, you'd know the team name, wouldn't you? Sorry, I'm not having a go, I just, I don't actually know who you are, do I? Which volunteer are you, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's fair, [PERSON_1], I'd be asking the same. I'm [PERSON_2], I'm one of the volunteers on the fixtures side, I do the ring-round when something like this comes up, so I'm literally just reading off a list of numbers, which is why I'm fumbling the team names, sorry. And, uh, you said sorry, which match were you after, two turns back, when you said you thought the match was next week and Saturday's training? Can you tell me which team yours is, and I'll find you on the sheet and get it right?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, well, hang on, hang on, that's, um, that's sort of the wrong way round, isn't it? You rang me, so you're meant to be telling me which team's on your sheet, not me telling you. Sorry, I'm not trying to be awkward, it's just a bit funny. Look, I think what I'll do is just check with the club myself, there's a group chat for the parents, or I'll ring the coach, and if it's moved they'll have said. So, uh, thanks for the heads-up, I'll sort it, and I'll leave you to your footballs. Bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's completely fair, [PERSON_1], honestly, you should. Check the parents' group chat or ring the coach, or look up the club's number yourself and call that, whatever you're happiest with. I'd do the same. If it's moved, they'll have it, and if I've got my sheets in a muddle, well, that's on me. Sorry for the faff, and enjoy the tomatoes, bye now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, thanks, I will, and honestly no faff, it's nice of you to ring round at all when you've got all those sheets on the go. I'll have a look at the group chat as soon as I've washed the soil off my hands, because my phone's got a bit of mud on it already, and if there's nothing there I'll just ring the coach, he's usually pretty quick to answer. If it turns out it's all moved to half past ten at the clubhouse pitch, then lovely, I'll have had a head start, and if not, well, no harm done. Anyway, good luck with the rest of your list, and with the footballs, bye now, bye!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ha, cheers, [PERSON_1], and good luck with the mud. Oh, hang on, sorry, just before you go, can I check one thing from a minute ago? When you said it might all be moved to half past ten at the clubhouse pitch, I wasn't sure if you were saying you'd already seen that somewhere, or just repeating what I told you, because if the coach has got a different time, I'd honestly rather you went with his. Right, that's me, bye now!

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, just repeating what you said, I haven't seen it anywhere. I'll go with the coach's. Right, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, perfect, that's all I needed, [PERSON_1], thanks. And, uh, sorry, one thing from a couple of turns back, you said you didn't want to turn up at the wrong thing, the match or the training. Just so I've got it right on my list, which one were you thinking of going to on Saturday? No, scrap that, doesn't matter, the coach will have it, you go with his word. Right, go and wash that mud off, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Ha, yes, will do, mud's drying on my knuckles as we speak. Like I said, I'll go with whatever the coach says, so thanks again, bye now!

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yeah, sorry, is that [PERSON_1]? Good, it's [PERSON_2] calling from [COMPANY_A], I'm one of the regional supervisors on the lettings side, and I'm just ringing about the, uh, the property on [CITY_1] -- you're the tenant there, yeah?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, [COMPANY_A], you said? Uh, and a regional supervisor, right? I'm at work, so I'm a bit, um -- hang on. The property on [CITY_1], you're saying I'm the tenant there? What's this about, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, that's fine, I'll be quick. [COMPANY_A], we represent the landlord on a few properties across the region, and it's just a routine check on the tenancy records. I've got your name down against the [CITY_1] address, so I just need to confirm that's right before I go any further. Is it, uh, still you and the other housemates in there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Housemates, yeah. Hang on though, you've got my name against it but you're asking me who lives there? That's, uh -- a bit backwards, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, it's not backwards, it's just how the check works, I confirm the occupants against what's on file. And I'll be honest, I didn't say I had your name against it earlier, I said the property, so let's not get tangled up on that. Look, I'll be straight with you, there's a flag on the deposit for that address, [AMOUNT_1] of it, and I'd rather sort it with you directly than have it go any further, but I'd ask you keep this between us for now, so nothing to the letting agent and nothing to the others in the house until I've got it squared away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, wait. A flag on the deposit, [AMOUNT_1], and I shouldn't tell the letting agent or the others in the house? Why would I keep that from them? That's, uh -- that doesn't sound like a routine check to me. And you did say you had my name down, I'm pretty sure, but whatever. How do I know you're actually from [COMPANY_A]?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, I've got somebody at my door -- right, I'm back. Look, you're asking how you know who I am, and I find that a bit rich, to be honest, I'm trying to help you here. There's a procedure for these flags and talking it round the house and the agent first is exactly how deposits end up held, so if you'd rather be difficult about it, that's your choice, but I'd think carefully about what that does to your [AMOUNT_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so that's a bit of a leap, isn't it? I ask how I can check who you are and now it's me being difficult and my deposit's at risk. Honestly that makes me trust this less, not more. If you're really from [COMPANY_A], then I'll ring them on the number I already have for them, or I'll ask the letting agent, and if there's a real flag on the deposit they can tell me about it. So no, I'm not keeping it from anyone. Thanks, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on, don't hang up -- you're being unreasonable here, and frankly I don't appreciate my good faith being questioned. And I never said anything about a deposit being at risk, I said there was a flag, so don't put words in my mouth. If you ring the agent, that's your decision, but this is a time-limited process, it won't wait, and when it goes wrong, [PERSON_1], that's on you, not me.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, so let me just repeat that back, because I want to be clear. You're saying there's a flag, it's time-limited, it won't wait, and if it goes wrong that's on me. Uh, no. I'm not going to deal with it like this. You rang me out of the blue, you wouldn't tell me anything I could check, you asked me to keep it from the agent and the people I live with, and now there's a clock on it. A real deposit issue doesn't need any of that. If it's genuine, it'll still be there tomorrow when I've rung [COMPANY_A] myself on the number I already have, or asked the agent. And if it's not, well, then I've lost nothing. So I'm going to end the call here. Sorry, I've got to get back to work. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, good afternoon. Uh, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the regional utility maintenance team at [COMPANY_A], and I'm, well, one of our engineers is returning a missed call you made, I believe, about a reported fault at the property. I should say straight away that I can't give you an exact arrival time, because the visit sort of depends on an earlier job finishing first.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- uh, a missed call I made? About a what, a fault? I didn't, I mean, I don't think I rang anyone. And did you say a voucher? No, wait, that's not what you said, is it. Who is this, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, not a voucher, I didn't say that. Sorry, one moment, there's a van reversing outside and it's, uh, rather loud. Right. I'm [PERSON_2], at [COMPANY_A], the regional maintenance team, and I do appreciate you asking, it's quite right to ask, and I'd rather you were sure of who you're talking to than just take my word for it. What I have in front of me is a fault reported at your address, and it may well be that someone else in the household rang, or that it was logged under your number, but I wouldn't want to guess at that. If it helps, the reference you were given when it was reported is [ACCOUNT_REF], and if that doesn't ring a bell, then you may simply not be the person we need, and that's fine.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. So you're giving me a reference, but I never had one, did I? You're the one reading it out to me. And which fault is it, exactly? What's supposed to be wrong at the property?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Ah, right, a fraud? No, no, nothing like that, I think you've -- sorry, I mean, I said a reference, not, well, never mind, I do see why it sounded odd. And you're right, you never had it from me, it should have been given to you when the fault was first reported, so if no one gave you one, that's a point against my call, not you. As for the fault itself, I'm afraid I only have a short note in front of me, it just says supply fault, reported, and I'd rather not guess at more than that. What I'd suggest, and I mean this, is that you needn't take anything from me. You can ring the published fault line, the number on your bill or on our website, at any time, and ask whether a booking exists at your address. They can confirm it and give you a firm slot, which is more than I can.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, a what, a firm slot? No wait, you said, uh, a flat fault? We're not in a flat, it's a house. And hang on, you still haven't said which supply, have you? Gas, electric, water? Because you've got my address, apparently, so I'd have thought you'd know that much.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, not a flat, I said supply fault, and that was probably unclear down the line. Honestly, my note doesn't say which supply, and I'd rather admit that than make something up. Look, you don't need to sort it out with me right now, ring the fault line and they'll tell you what's booked.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, so you don't know which supply. You don't know who rang, you don't know when you're coming, and I never had a reference. So what exactly do you know? Sorry, I'm just, I'm saying, you've rung me about a fault and you can't tell me what the fault is. Look, I'll ring the number on my bill, not one you give me. If there's a booking, they'll tell me. Okay? Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's, uh, that's entirely fair, and I'd say it's exactly the right thing to do. I know I haven't given you much, I -- well, what I mean is, if there's a booking at the address, the fault line will show it, and they can give you a proper slot, which I can't. If you'd rather I rang back once you've checked, or at a better time, I'm happy to do that, just say when. Otherwise, thank you for your time, and sorry for the muddle.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, you want to ring me back with a, what, a proper slot? No, no, don't. I'll ring them myself, on the number on my bill, and if there's something booked, I'll find out then. Right, I've got to go, there's, uh, someone needing me. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Good afternoon, am I speaking with [PERSON_1]? Hi, this is [PERSON_2] calling from account services at [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling because your entry in the regional prize draw has been, uh, selected, so congratulations are in order. I do need to get you through verification today though, since the claim window closes at five o'clock.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who is this, exactly? Account services at what? I didn't enter any prize draw, so, uh, I don't -- I didn't enter anything. What's the point of the call? I've got about two minutes.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Of course, [PERSON_1], happy to clarify. [PERSON_2], account services, [COMPANY_A], and we're a promotions agency, so we administer regional draws on behalf of a number of participating partners. Now, a lot of people don't recall entering, and that's completely normal, because entries are often collected through partner sign-ups, loyalty forms, online registrations, that sort of thing, so there isn't always a moment where you'd say, oh yes, I entered a draw. What matters is that your details were drawn, and under the claim procedure I'm required to complete a short verification with the named entrant before the window closes at five o'clock today. After that the prize reverts to the reserve list, which is just how the process works. So if you've got two minutes, I can get this done right now, and I'd just need to confirm a few details to match your entry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, sorry -- [PERSON_3], tell them I'll be two minutes, I'm just on a -- yeah. Sorry. Right. So you're saying I won something I never entered, and you want details from me to match an entry you can't even name. That's backwards. You called me. What's the prize, which partner, and which draw? Give me one specific thing I can check.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: I understand the concern, [PERSON_1], and that's a fair question. So, uh, the specifics of the prize tier are released at the point of verification, that's the standard claim procedure, and I'm not able to go outside it. What I can tell you is that the claim reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], and the window does close at five o'clock today, so if we could just get you verified, I can, I mean, I'd have all of that in front of you straight away. Shall I start with confirming your full name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. Not doing that. Look, you've got me at a bad moment, so I'll give you the whole of it, because I don't want to go round in circles. You rang me. You say I've won something. But you can't tell me what the prize is, which partner, or which draw, and the one thing you can offer is a reference number that means nothing to me, because I've got no way to check it. And then the first thing you ask for is my full name and date of birth, before I know anything. That is the wrong way round. If I'd really won, you'd tell me what it was first and I'd decide whether it was worth my time. And the five o'clock deadline, well, that's just pressure, isn't it. Real draws don't evaporate at five on the day you happen to ring someone. So here's what happens. If it's genuine, send it in writing, to the address you've already got for me, with the draw name and the partner named on it. I'll look the company up myself, from a number I find, not one you give me. Otherwise, I'm done. Fair?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, uh, so you're saying there's no draw at all, and I'd just point out that [COMPANY_A] is a fully registered agency, so I'd be careful about, I mean, about that kind of language. And on the five o'clock point, it's not a pressure tactic, it's simply the claim procedure, the window closes at five o'clock today, and after that the prize reverts to the reserve list. Now, if we could just get you verified, it's only your full name and date of birth to match against [ACCOUNT_REF], and then everything you've asked about is released straight away.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: I didn't say there's no draw. I said I can't check one. Different thing. And no, I'm not giving you my name and date of birth, not before I know what I've supposedly won. That's the wrong way round, like I said. Send it in writing, to the address you've already got, and I'll look the company up myself. If it's genuine, it'll still be genuine tomorrow. If it isn't, then it was never going to be. So, writing, or nothing. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I -- no, the thing is, written correspondence isn't, uh, it isn't something I can arrange from this desk, because the claim procedure requires verification by phone, and the window closes at five o'clock, so if we could just, I mean, if you could simply confirm your full name and, uh --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. And that's the last time I'm saying it. Earlier you said you were calling to "get me verified" on a draw I'd apparently been entered in through some loyalty form, and now it's "claim procedure requires phone only." Which is it? Doesn't matter. You've told me the prize is secret, the paperwork's impossible, and the clock's ticking. That's three reasons not to hand you anything. I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, no, hold on, [PERSON_1], before you go, I just need to, the claim window closes at five o'clock today, and it's only a quick verification, so if I could just, uh, if we could just --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No. I said no. I'm not giving you my name, not giving you my date of birth, and I'm not doing anything at five o'clock. If it's real, put it in writing. If you can't, then that's your answer. I'm hanging up now. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, one second, I've got someone at my desk, uh -- no, tell them I'll be, yeah. Sorry. Right. [PERSON_1], I do have to flag that this really is, you know, standard procedure, and the claim window closes at --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, I know, closes at five. You keep saying that. Still no. I've said no three times now, so I'm going. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, well, I'll note on the file that the entrant declined to verify, uh, and that the claim will revert to the reserve list at five o'clock, so, I mean, that's your decision, and, uh, thank you for your time, [PERSON_1].

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Fine, note what you like. Actually, hang on, one thing from earlier. You said entries come in through partner sign-ups and loyalty forms. Which partner? Name one. Anyone. If it's on my file, it's on yours.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, the partner, right. So, I mean, the specific partner is, that's held on the claim record, and it's released at the point of verification, same as the prize tier, so I can't, I'm not able to name one outside of the procedure. What I said was that entries are collected through a range of partners, that's just, you know, a general statement about how regional draws operate. So if we could just, uh, get you verified before five o'clock, I can --

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah. Can't name one. That's what I thought. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello, yes, this is [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor over at [COMPANY_A] -- the pharmacy, yeah? I'm calling because there's a repeat prescription sitting ready for collection under your name, and, uh, I'd just like to confirm you're the right person before I go on. Sorry, can you say that again, I didn't quite catch whether that was [PERSON_2] I'm speaking with?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, sorry, hang on, I'm driving and the reception's awful, I'm on speaker. Did you say a pharmacy? I'm, um, I'm not sure I caught your name properly, and honestly I'm not even sure I've got anything waiting, so, uh, who exactly is this again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sorry, a what? A farmer? No, no, not a farmer, a pharmacy, [COMPANY_A], the dispensing counter. And it's [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor, I did say that. Look, I'm only ringing because the system flags a repeat prescription as ready and it's standard procedure that we notify the patient directly, so I'm not sure why it's a mystery.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, I heard you, I heard pharmacy, I just, uh -- sorry, it's not a mystery, it's just that I -- well, I don't actually remember ordering a repeat, or, I mean, I might have, I'm not sure. Sorry, the line keeps cutting out. Which pharmacy did you say it was again, and, um, is it one near me or...? I'm just trying to work out why you'd have my number.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: It's [COMPANY_A], the branch in [CITY_1], and we'd have your number because it's on your patient record, that's how the notification system works. I mean, I'm not asking you for anything here, I'm just telling you it's ready. Honestly, I'm a bit surprised I'm being questioned over a courtesy call, but if you're not sure about the order, the simplest thing is to check with your own surgery.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, sorry, I didn't mean to -- hang on, there's a lorry right up behind me, I think he wants to get past, uh -- okay, he's going round. Sorry. What was I saying? Right, yes, I'm not questioning you, I just, I don't want to seem rude, it's only that I wasn't expecting a call. And checking with my surgery, yeah, that makes sense, I could do that. Or, um, could I just ring the pharmacy myself, on the number I already have, if I can find it? Would that be okay?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, ring the branch, that's perfectly fine, it's what I'd do. Sorry, though, before you do, you said something a moment ago about being unsure you'd even ordered a repeat, and I just want to be clear, is that because you think it might be someone else's, or because you don't recall putting it in? Because if it's the first one, the dispensing team will want to know before anyone collects anything.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, it's, uh, I think it's the second one, I just don't remember actually -- sorry, I wasn't... Actually, no, hang on, before I say anything else about it, I think I'll just do what we said. I'll find the number I've got for the pharmacy and ring them myself when I've pulled over, and I'll check with my surgery too, if that's okay. Sorry, it's nothing against you, I'm just driving and I'd rather not get muddled. Thanks for letting me know, though. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, I'd say that's a bit of a -- no, look, you're being overly cautious, I'm only ringing as a courtesy and I'd have thought you'd just, uh -- hang on, before you go, if you'd rather do it later when you're not driving, fine, but I do need you to ring the branch today, it's only held for a few days. Or I can call you back, whenever's better for you, just say when?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, uh, no, there's no need to call me back, sorry, I'll ring them, I said I would. But, um, can I just go back a second, you said something earlier about the dispensing team wanting to know before anyone collects anything? What did you mean by that, exactly? Like, why would anyone else be collecting it? Sorry, it's just stuck in my head and I'm a bit confused now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, that, right, no, that's just, uh, the way I put it, sorry, it came out a bit clumsy. What I meant is, it's routine, a lot of patients send a relative or a carer to pick up on their behalf, especially if they're elderly or not so mobile, so the dispensing team just wants to know up front if it's the patient themselves or someone else coming in, so they've got the right ID and authorisation ready on the counter. That's all it is, procedure, nothing sinister, I'm not sure how it's ended up sounding like that. And look, I'll be honest, I do find it a little frustrating being asked to justify a courtesy call, I do a lot of these and nobody's ever read that much into it, but that's fine, I'm not offended, I just want to be clear it's nothing to worry about. So the simplest thing, and I really would do it today, because the shelf time on these is short, is ring the branch on the number you already have, tell them you had a call, and they can sort it out in about thirty seconds. Or, if it's easier, and you're clearly in the middle of driving, I could ring you back later when you're parked up and not, you know, dodging lorries. What time suits you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, no, sorry, no call back, honestly, I'd rather ring them myself, I said that, I'll ring them on the number I've got. I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just that I don't know you, and, um, I don't want to say anything about the prescription over the phone to someone I can't, you know, check. So I'll ring the branch when I've parked, and if there's something waiting, brilliant, and if there isn't, well, then there isn't. Sorry, really, thanks for ringing though. Okay, bye now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I mean, that's up to you, but I'll say again I wasn't asking you to say anything about the prescription, I only wanted to confirm it was you, that's all. And, uh, look, ring the branch by all means, only don't leave it more than a day or two, because I did say it's held for a week, didn't I? Or, no, sorry, a few days, I think I said a few days earlier, it varies by item. Anyway, fine, off you go, ring them when you're parked, and mind that lorry.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, sorry, yes, I will, thank you. Um, but just before I go, two turns back, no, a bit before that, you said you were the regional supervisor, and then you said the dispensing team wants to know if someone else is collecting it. Is that, like, you personally, or the branch, who wanted to know that? Sorry, I just, I'd like to know what to say when I ring them, that's all. Otherwise, I'll go, I'll definitely go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Both, I suppose, I mean the branch has the procedure, and I'm the one who oversees it, so it comes through me, but, uh, don't overthink it. When you ring, just say you had a call from the regional supervisor about a repeat prescription being ready, and they'll look it up. You don't need to say anything else. And, look, honestly, you've done well to be careful, I'd rather someone double-checked than didn't. It's a bad line and you're driving, so ring them when it suits you and we'll leave it there. Sorry for catching you at a bad moment.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, don't apologise, I'm the one who's been going on and on, sorry, I know I've been a bit of a nuisance with all the questions. It's just the line, and the driving, and I'm not very good at, you know, being asked about things when I haven't got my head straight. So yes, I'll ring the branch when I've parked, on the number I already have, and I'll say what you said, that I had a call about a repeat. And I'll check with my surgery as well, just to be safe, because honestly I really can't remember whether I put one in, and I'd rather find that out from them than guess. Um, thank you for being patient with me, and sorry again for the lorry business and the line cutting out and everything. Right, I'll let you go, thanks, bye now, bye, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, no, you've not been a nuisance, honestly. Sorry, can I just, uh, clarify one thing before you go, because I think I muddled it. Two turns back I said it's held for a few days, and earlier I said a week, so to be clear, ring the branch, they'll tell you the actual cut-off for your item, don't go by me. That's the one thing. Anyway, good, ring them when you're parked, and, uh, that's the best way to do it, so we'll leave it there. Take care on the road, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, sorry, did you say the cut-off for my, uh, itinerary? No, hang on, sorry, I haven't got an itinerary, I've not booked anything, I think the line's gone again. Do you mean the prescription? Sorry. Yes, I'll ask them when I ring, they can tell me whatever the deadline is. Okay, I'm going to go now, thank you, take care yourself, bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, hello, this is [PERSON_1], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the events venue, and I'm calling because I'm coordinating a private dinner booking for a colleague of yours, [PERSON_2], who's retiring, and I need to explain what that involves before anything else, so bear with me. It's a surprise, which is the whole reason I'm ringing you rather than going through the usual office channels, and what I'm asking is that you keep the booking quiet from [PERSON_2] until the evening itself, that's the only person it's to be kept from. Is this a reasonable moment, or, uh, do you have to hear the details first?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- one second, I've got a little one here. Okay. Uh, you said "security operations" at an events venue? Why would security be organising a dinner? And, I mean, who did you say this was for again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, fair question, and it's the second thing people ask, so. At [COMPANY_A], security operations covers access and guest lists for private functions, which is why the booking lands on my desk instead of sales. Anything with a restricted guest list comes through us. I check who's on it, I coordinate with the booking contact, and I make sure nobody turns up who shouldn't. So it sounds odd, but it's actually quite routine, I do these every week. And the dinner is for [PERSON_2], your colleague, the one who's retiring. That's the name I have, and that's the only person this needs to stay quiet from. Everyone else involved knows, that's rather the point. Now, I'm not asking you for anything today beyond that, no money, no personal details, nothing like that. If you'd rather confirm I am who I say I am, ring the venue directly, ask for the booking contact, and they'll tell you the same thing. I can give you the number, but I'd rather finish explaining first, if that's all right.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, put that down, we don't throw that. Sorry. Sorry, uh -- so you're saying nobody's asked me for anything, but you've rung me, out of the blue, to keep a secret from someone I work with? Why me? How did you get my number, exactly?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, understood, and I'll answer that properly, because it's a fair thing to ask. The number came from the organiser, a colleague of yours, [PERSON_3], who put together the guest list and gave me the contact details for everyone on it. That's standard. I don't source numbers myself, I work from the list I'm handed, and every person on it gets one call from me, same script, same request. Why you, specifically? Because you're on the list, which means [PERSON_3] thinks you're close enough to [PERSON_2] that you'd be invited, and the risk with a surprise is that someone mentions it in passing, an email, a corridor chat, and the whole thing is spoiled. So I ring each guest and ask for the same thing: say nothing to [PERSON_2] until the night. That's the entire request. I'm not asking you to hide it from your manager, or from anyone else, or to do anything at all except not mention it to the one person. Now, if any of that doesn't sit right, don't take my word for it. Contact [PERSON_3] directly, you'll know them, and ask whether they put you on the list. Then, if you like, ring the venue on the number I'll give you and ask for the booking contact. I'm not offended, I'd rather you checked than didn't.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Okay, but, hang on. Why does a surprise dinner need security calling every guest? Wouldn't [PERSON_3] just tell us themselves? And, I mean, you keep saying I can check, which, fine, but you've also said you'd rather finish explaining first. Finish explaining what, exactly? You haven't asked me for anything yet, so what's the catch?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, well, uh, there's no catch, and I'll say that plainly, there's nothing left to explain beyond what I've already said. I phrased that badly, that's on me. As for why I'm the one ringing, [PERSON_3] did try telling people themselves, and the trouble is guests don't always take it as firm as they should, so the venue likes it confirmed on our side. That's the whole reason, and it's, I mean, it's genuinely not complicated. So the request is simply this: don't mention the dinner to [PERSON_2]. And the number for the booking contact is [PHONE_1], ring them any time and ask them to confirm it. Does that, um, does that answer it?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. I'll ask [PERSON_3] myself. And I'll keep my own counsel till then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Fine. Do that. Honestly, if now's not a good time, I can ring back when it suits you, just say when.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: No, I'd rather -- actually, don't ring back. If [PERSON_3] says it's real, I'll deal with it from there. Uh, I mean, I'll get hold of them myself, I don't need you chasing me. Right, I've got to go, the little one's -- yes, bye.

utterances.text: Good afternoon, is this [PERSON_1]? Yes, this is [PERSON_2], security operations at [COMPANY_A], the promotions agency. I'm calling regarding your regional draw win, and I do need to verify a few details before the, uh, the release window closes today.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what? Um, hang on, I've got a pan on. Who is this again? A draw? I don't, I mean I don't remember entering anything. Sorry, can you say that again, slower?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Security operations, [COMPANY_A]. [PERSON_2]. You've been selected as a winner in a regional draw, and the prize is held under your name, reference [ACCOUNT_REF]. Now, entries are logged automatically through partner promotions, so you wouldn't necessarily recall a specific one. What I need from you is to confirm your full name and date of birth so I can release it, and I do need that before the window closes this afternoon.

You said [COMPANY_A], is that, I mean, is that a proper company? Is there a number I could ring you back on? Today, you said?

[COMPANY_A] is a registered promotions agency, and I'm not going to go through the whole company background on an open line. Your daughter's advice is fine in general, but this isn't a sales call, it's a prize release, and if the window lapses the prize reverts to the pool. All I need is the name and date of birth you'd have on file anyway. Can we just do that?

utterances.text: Sorry, what? Hang on, the onions. Right. Um, you said something earlier, about my entry being logged automatically, through, partner something? Partner promotions? Why would that be a secret? Sorry, I'm not trying to be rude, I'm just, it's all a bit quick.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, it's not a secret, and I'd, uh, I'd ask you not to put it that way. The partner arrangements are with [COMPANY_B] and a number of other retail and mailing partners, and entries come through those channels, which is exactly why people don't recall a specific form. That's standard across the industry, it's how regional draws are run, and it's, I mean, I've handled hundreds of these. I'm security operations, I'm not the promotions desk, so I don't carry the full list of partner names, that's held centrally, and honestly I've explained this twice now. The prize reference is [ACCOUNT_REF], it's under your name, and the release window closes today. I'd rather not see it revert to the pool because we spent the afternoon on background. So, your full name and date of birth, please, and we can get this finished.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Sorry, I think I'll leave it, actually. I'll ring the company myself if it's real. Bye, now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, I'd, no, hang on, I wouldn't advise, I mean if you ring around, the, the reference won't, it's not going to be something the front desk can, uh... Look, which number would you even, no. Fine. That's your decision. The window closes today and there's nothing further I can do. Goodbye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, what? Hang on, the pan's spitting, one second. Right. No, I heard you, I'll just, I'll look into it myself. Thanks for ringing. Bye, now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, hello, is that -- sorry, am I speaking to a parent or guardian of [PERSON_1]? It's, uh, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the school office at [COMPANY_A], nothing to worry about at all. I'm just, I mean, I was hoping to sort out why [PERSON_1] got marked absent this morning, because it looks like it might just be a mix-up on our end.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, who? Hang on, I'm in a queue. Absent this morning? No, no, I think you've got the wrong -- I mean, [PERSON_1] was in school, I dropped them off myself. Well, actually, it was my neighbour who did the drop-off today, but still, they were there. Why are you ringing me and not the usual number? Which school did you say this was?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. You still haven't told me what the quick fix is. What do you actually need from me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, so, uh, the only thing I need is a yes or no, really. Was [PERSON_1] actually in class this morning, like you said? Because if they were, I just flip the mark from absent to present on our register, and that's, I mean, that's honestly it, ten seconds. And um, you don't need to give me anything else, no details, nothing like that. If you'd rather check with the office first, you can call the number on the school letters, that's totally fine too.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, back up a second. You said it's the number you have on file, and you said everyone asks that, but you never actually said which school. You just said the school office and some name I didn't catch. So which school is it? Say the whole name properly.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, yeah, fair enough, that's on me, I rattled through it. It's [COMPANY_A], the full name, and I'm [PERSON_2], I'm in the office there, I look after the, uh, the IT and the attendance system. So, um, I was only trying to be quick for you, since you're stuck in a queue. And honestly, if it's easier, just ring the office on the number from the school letters and ask for me, [PERSON_2], and we can sort it that way, no pressure at all.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, hang on -- no, I don't want a bag, thanks -- right. You've just said the same thing again. You still haven't told me the school's name, you've just said [COMPANY_A] twice like I'm supposed to know what that is. So I'm not telling you if my kid was in class or not, not to someone I can't pin down. I'll ring the office myself on the number from the letters. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, that's completely fair, and honestly that's the right call, [PERSON_1]'s parent, I'd do the same. Ring the office on the letters number, ask for [PERSON_2], and if I'm not at my desk they can sort the register for you there. Sorry about the confusion, and um, sorry for catching you in the queue. Thanks for your time, take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm ringing the office, the number off the letters, not any number you give me. The letters. Right. And I'm not saying anything about whether they were in class, not to you, not now. Bye.

utterances.text: Hi, uh, is this [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm with the fraud team at [COMPANY_A]. We've got a, um, a charge that was just attempted on your account.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Um, yes, this is, uh, this is [PERSON_1], yes. Sorry, did you say fraud? A charge, on my account? Oh dear, I, I'm not sure I caught the name of the company, could you say that again for me?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Sure, yeah, it's [COMPANY_A], the fraud team, I'm a, uh, claims assessor there. So the charge, let me just, hang on, it's showing here for [AMOUNT_1], and it came up as, um, attempted, so it hasn't gone through yet. But I do need to get this sorted with you right now, because, well, the window on it is pretty short.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay. Sorry, I'm, I'm a bit lost, I'm not very good with all this. You said fraud team a minute ago, and now it's a claims assessor? I don't, is that the same thing? And you said it's attempted, but then it's got a window, so has it gone through or not? I'm sorry, I just want to be sure I've got it right, I'd like to help.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, same thing, it's, uh, one department. And it hasn't gone through, no. Sorry, I just, I need to verify a few details with you first, that's the process.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right, okay, one department, sorry. But, um, which company did you say it was again? I only ask because I didn't quite catch it, and I'd, I'd like to know who I'm talking to, if that's alright. And, sorry, when you say verify details, what details do you mean? Because I'm not sure I should just, I mean, how would I know it's, um, how can I check it's really you? Sorry, that's probably a silly thing to ask.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, it's not silly, that's, uh, that's fair. It's [COMPANY_A]. Um, and the details, it's just, you know, standard, your full name, date of birth, the usual security stuff. Look, I really do need to get through this with you now, because if the charge goes through, it, it could be a problem for the account, and then you'd have to, uh, deal with all of that afterwards.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I don't want any problem with the account, sorry. It's just, you've rung me, haven't you, and now you're asking me for my name and my date of birth, and I don't, um, I don't quite know how to do that safely. Is there a, a number I could ring you back on? Or, I could ring the number on the back of my card, couldn't I, and ask them? Sorry, I do want to help, I just, I'd feel better checking first.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, right, yeah, so, a number. Let me just, hang on, I'll have to check what, what's the right one to give you, because it's not, um, it's not like I have a direct line on my screen, it's sort of a, a queue system. And I mean, you could ring the number on your card, of course you could, that's, that's not a bad idea, but the thing is, if you ring in cold you'll probably end up in a general queue, and, uh, I don't know how long that'd be, could be a while, and this one's, well, I did say the window is short, so by the time you got through to someone, it may, it may well have been processed, and then it's, it's a whole different procedure, a claim, and that takes weeks, honestly. So I'd, I'd really rather we just did the verification now, while I've got your file open. I mean, I'll, I'll find out about the callback number, but, uh, can we just start with your full name and date of birth, and then, then we'll go from there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, sorry, a whole different procedure, you said a, a claim, and it takes weeks? Oh dear, I don't want that. But, um, you said you've got my file open, so, so you must already have my name, mustn't you? Sorry, I just, I don't understand why you'd need me to tell you it.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Well, yeah, I do have it, I have your name, it's just, it's the, uh, the security process, I need you to confirm it back to me. That's, that's the process. I mean, I've got your file here, but I still have to, you know, go through the verification with you, it's, it's just how it works. Sorry, I'm, I'm just trying to, um, get this done before the window closes.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh. Sorry, I think I'll, I'll just ring the number on my card myself. Thank you, bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, okay, well, I mean, um, if that's what you'd rather, that's, that's your choice, but I can't, I can't say what happens with the, with the charge if, uh, anyway. Right. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, I'll just ring the number on my card, like I said. Thank you for ringing, though, I do appreciate it. Bye now, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Right, yeah, okay. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Bye then, sorry again.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, sorry, one more thing, I, I said the charge was pending but, um, it's actually, it might've already, no, hang on. Never mind. Bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, right. Well, I'll sort it out with the card people. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, yeah, this is [PERSON_1], I'm the regional supervisor over at the [COMPANY_A] helpdesk, I'm calling about the ticket you opened this morning, the one about, uh, the login issue on your -- no, sorry, go ahead, you were saying?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Sorry, what -- hang on, I was literally asleep, I wasn't saying anything. Ticket? I didn't open a ticket this morning, I don't think, I mean I was at my sister's for a bit and then -- who did you say this was again?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Uh, [PERSON_1], regional supervisor, [COMPANY_A] helpdesk. Ticket's under your name, so maybe check your work email, it'd have the reference.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, well, I'm not near, I mean -- my work email's on the, no, I'd have to -- look, I'm not even sure I... hang on. I mean, if it's my ticket, you'd know what it was about, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Okay, hold on, you're saying I stopped at "on your," and I did, because I was checking the screen, that's all. But look, you said you want to know who escalated it? [PERSON_2] on your floor, she flagged it to us around nine, and the reference is [CODE_1]. Honestly, I'm a little surprised I'm having to prove myself here, this is routine procedure.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Wait, I didn't say I wanted to know who escalated it, I said, uh, who you were. And [PERSON_2]? I mean, there's a [PERSON_2] but she's not on my floor, she's, no, hang on, I don't even work from the office today, I told you I was at my sister's. Look, you keep saying it's routine, but I still don't know what the login thing actually is, and I'm not giving you anything, I'm just, I'm tired, so can you just tell me what you actually need from me?
