utterances.text: Okay, fair, I did get ahead of myself there, and, uh, so -- right, so what I actually need is just ten minutes where I can connect to your machine and clear the stuck session on the ticket, and, um, I know that sounds like a lot when you're half asleep. But I'd rather you not read anything out to me. If you'd rather verify first, no problem at all, you can log a callback request through the internal portal and I'll ring you back once it's showing on my side. Does that work?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Connect to my machine? No, see, that's -- I mean, I'm not even at it, it's at home on the desk and I'm at my sister's, well, I was, I'm back now, I think, I just woke up on the sofa and honestly I can't tell you what day it is half the time. But no, I wouldn't do that anyway, not with someone who rang me out of the blue, because we had that thing at work, a training thing, where they said never let anyone get on your computer unless you rang them first. So, uh, the callback thing, the portal, I don't know where that is, I don't use it, I'd have to ask somebody, and that's sort of the point, isn't it? If it's a real ticket then it'll still be there tomorrow. So I'm going to ring the helpdesk number on, I don't know, the back of my pass or the intranet, and ask them, and if you're who you say you are, that'll be fine, won't it? Okay? Right. Bye now.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, that's fine, honestly, that's the right call. Ring the number on the intranet, give them the ticket reference and mention [PERSON_1], and we'll sort it from there. Sorry for the early start.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, okay, so the intranet, or the pass, one of the two, I'll ring that one. Not the number you'd give me, I mean, I'm not saying you were going to, I just, yeah, I'll look it up myself. And it's not early, it's the afternoon, I only dozed off. Anyway, I'll ring them, the proper helpdesk, and see if there's a ticket at all. Bye now, then.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yes, yes, look it up yourself, that's what I said, use the intranet number, not one from me. And, uh, sorry, afternoon, right, I did say early, my mistake. If there's no ticket under your name, then it's probably a mix-up on our side, a crossed wire, and I'll sort it out here, no harm done. Okay, so, you ring them, I'll leave it with you, take care.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, I'll ring them. Though, uh, I think you said earlier it was my work email I should check for the reference, and now it's just ring the number and give them the reference, and I haven't got a reference, have I, because I never saw one. Whatever, I'll just ask them if there's anything under my name. Right, bye then, take care.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're right, I -- sorry, I made that more tangled than it needs to be. You don't need a reference at all, just ask them if there's anything open under your name, and if there isn't, that's on us, a crossed wire, and I'll chase it from my end. Honestly, I'd rather you checked than sat there wondering, so, yeah, go and ring them. Take care, and sorry for waking you.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm, yeah. I'll ring them. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hi, hello, is this -- sorry, am I speaking to [PERSON_1]? It's [PERSON_2], I'm calling from the school office at [COMPANY_A]. Uh, nothing to worry about at all, it's just a quick one, I'm trying to sort out why [PERSON_3] got marked absent this morning, and I thought, well, you might be the best person to ask.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, who? Sorry, I'm in the middle of a queue here. Yeah, that's me, but I don't know a [PERSON_3]. Or, well, hang on, I think my kid's at a different school, not that one. Which school did you say?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, right, no, that's fine. It's [COMPANY_A], the school office. Probably just a mix-up on my end, [PERSON_1], sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right. Wrong number then. Fine.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, uh, no, absolutely, wrong number, my apologies. I think what's happened is the number's been entered wrong on the pupil record, or, I mean, an old contact's still sitting on the system, that happens a lot. Anyway, I'll get it sorted from my end, [PERSON_1], so you won't get another call from us. Sorry again for catching you in the middle of the queue, and, um, have a good rest of your day.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hang on, hang on. Two seconds ago you asked if you were speaking to me, by name. So how'd you get my name off a wrong number? And you said something earlier about that [PERSON_3] being marked absent and I'd be the best person to ask. Why would I be the best person to ask about a kid I've never heard of?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, fair question, [PERSON_1], and honestly it's a bit of a muddle on my end. The name came off the contact sheet for [PERSON_3], so whoever filled that in either typed your number by mistake or used to have it as theirs. And, uh, "best person to ask" was just me assuming you were the parent, which clearly you're not. Look, you don't need to do anything at all, I'll flag the number as wrong on the record and nobody'll ring you again. If you'd rather check I'm genuinely from the school, you can look up the [COMPANY_A] office number yourself and ring it, that's no bother either.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Mm. Sorry, hang on -- no, I'm fine, the woman in front's just arguing with the till. Uh, right. So you're saying someone wrote my number on a form by mistake. Well, that's convenient. And you rang a stranger about a kid's attendance, which, I don't know, doesn't feel like something a school office does cold, does it? Anyway. You've not asked me for anything, I'll give you that. So what is it you actually want from me? Because if it's nothing, I'm going to go.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Honestly, [PERSON_1], nothing. That's the whole truth. All I wanted was to know if you were [PERSON_3]'s parent so I could clear up the absence, and you're not, so we're done. I don't need your details, I don't need you to do anything, and I wouldn't ask for any of that over the phone anyway. And you're right, it's not great that I rang a stranger, that's on us for having a wrong number on file. I'll get it taken off today. Sorry for the hassle, and go on, go back to your queue, I'll let you get on.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Right, nothing. You want nothing. Okay. But I'm still going to say it, I don't know that kid, I don't have a kid at that school, so take the number off, yeah? Take it off. And don't ring me again, because next time I'm not going to be this polite. Right, I'm at the front now, I'm going. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yeah, no, completely, [PERSON_1], I'll take it off today and you won't hear from us again. Sorry, and, uh, thanks for putting up with me, I know you were busy. Oh, and just so you know, I did say I was ringing about [PERSON_3] being marked absent last week, which, hang on, no, sorry, it was this morning, I keep mixing the days up. Anyway, that's on my end, not yours. Cheers, [PERSON_1], bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Uh, yeah, well. Look, last week, this morning, I don't care which, that's the second time you've tripped over your own story. Anyway. Um, just take the number off and that's it, okay? That's it. Right, bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, that's it, [PERSON_1], number's coming off, promise. Sorry, one sec, somebody's just put a whole stack of registers down right in front of me, hang on -- right, sorry. Yeah, and fair enough on the days, I've had a bit of a morning here. Cheers for your patience, and take care, bye now.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, okay, but you keep saying bye and then you're still talking. Take the number off. Take it off. That's all I want, and I'm not saying it again, I'm at the till. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Yep, understood, it's coming off, and that's me done, I mean it this time. Sorry, [PERSON_1], I did say earlier I'd got the name off the contact sheet, but now I'm looking at it, it's actually the old emergency contact list, so, uh, that's why it was out of date. Anyway, number's off, no more calls, bye.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Contact sheet, now an emergency contact list. That's the third version of it. I don't care which one it is. I've said what I want, take the number off, and if I get another call I'll be ringing the actual school to ask about you. Right. I'm done. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Hello? Uh, hi, sorry, is this [PERSON_1]? ... Hello, are you still there? Sorry, I think the line went quiet for a second. It's [PERSON_2] calling from the compliance team at [COMPANY_A], your brokerage, and, um, I'm sorry to ring out of the blue like this.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, I'm here. Sorry, who did you say you were with? Compliance at... I didn't catch the company name, it came out kind of garbled.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, that's my fault, I'm on a bit of a rubbish line. It's [COMPANY_A], uh, your brokerage, where you hold the investment account. I'm [PERSON_2], on the compliance team, and I'm just ringing about a routine suitability review we run on accounts, it's really there for your own protection. Is that, um, is that all right to go on with, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Hm. Okay, so, I'll be honest, I'm working right now, half watching a screen, so you've caught me mid-something. And I do have a brokerage account, but I'm not sure that's the same one you're calling from, because you still haven't actually said the name. You've said "your brokerage" twice now, which is sort of like someone saying "your bank" without telling me which one. That's, uh, I mean, it's not nothing. So, small thing, what's the company actually called? And what number are you calling from, because I'd want to see if it matches anything I've got on file. Then we can talk about this review.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, that's a completely fair thing to pick up on, and I'm sorry, I should have said it plainly the first time. The name is [COMPANY_A], and I'm calling from [PHONE_1]. Please do check that against whatever you've got on file, or just look at the number on the back of your statement or on the website and ring us through that instead, I honestly wouldn't mind at all. And, um, while you're doing that, I'm not asking you to buy anything or move anything, this is only a review of what the account already holds. Are you still with me, [PERSON_1]?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, still here, just, uh, give me a second, I'm looking at the, hm. Right. So, okay, you said the name this time, which I'll give you, except what you actually said was a placeholder-sounding string, not a name I'd recognise, but fine, let's park that. Here's a small one. If you're my brokerage, what's the account for? Like, which type, is it the general investing one, or something else? And what should I be seeing at the top of a statement from you? Just humour me.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry, yes, that's a fair thing to ask. Um, so the account I've got flagged is the [ACCOUNT_REF] one, and on the top of your statement you should see the [COMPANY_A] name and that same reference, and below it the holdings, [AMOUNT_1] in total at the last valuation, I think. Actually, hang on, sorry, I said it was a routine review earlier, but looking at the file again, it's tagged as a follow-up, not a first review, so I'm not certain why. As for the account type, I, uh, I'm honestly not sure the file says, and I don't want to guess at it and get it wrong with you. Can I find out and ring you straight back on [PHONE_1], or, if it's easier, we could do the whole review in writing and you can check every line against your own statement? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I'm still here. So, hang on, let me just say that back. You rang me about my account, you can't tell me what type of account it is, and the review went from routine to a follow-up while we were talking? Sorry, I'm not trying to be difficult, I just, I asked what the account's for, and I didn't really get an answer. That's the bit I keep coming back to. If you're my brokerage, that's on the first line of the file, surely. Anyway, you offered writing, and honestly that I'd take. Send it to the address you've got on file for me, not one I read out to you, and I'll check it against my own statement. Or I ring the number on the back of my statement, not yours. Which of those do you want?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, you're not being difficult at all, I'm sorry, you're right to keep coming back to it. And, um, the account type should be right there on the first line of the file, I agree. I can't see why it isn't, and I don't want to bluff you, so I'll find out. Do the writing, please, sent to the address you already have on file, and I won't ask you for anything on this call. Ringing the number on the back of your statement is perfectly fine too, whichever you'd rather. Was there something I said earlier you wanted me to go back over, the follow-up bit, maybe? Sorry, you're still there, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yeah, yeah, I'm here, just, uh... hm. Okay. No, I don't need you to go back over the follow-up bit. Writing to the address you've already got is fine. If it's real, it'll turn up and I'll check it against my own statement, and if I want to chase it I'll ring the number printed on my statement, not the one you gave me. Right, so that's what happens. I'm not giving you anything on this call, and I'll leave it there. Thanks for being straight about not knowing the account type, I suppose. Bye.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, hello, sorry -- is that [PERSON_1]'s parent or guardian? Um, it's [PERSON_2] calling from the office at [COMPANY_A], I'm the case handler for attendance. I'm just ringing because [PERSON_3] was marked absent this morning and we didn't have a message, so I wanted to check everything's all right. Hello? Are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh -- hello, yes, I'm here, sorry, I was just putting the kettle on. Did you say you're ringing about a, um, a tax case? Because I don't think I've got anything like that going on, dear. Who did you say you were again? It's nice to have a call, mind, it's been ever so quiet today.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh no, sorry, I think I've confused things -- not a tax case at all, no. I'm [PERSON_2], from the school office at [COMPANY_A]. It's about [PERSON_3], who was marked absent this morning, and we just wanted to make sure they're safe and well. Is that, um, is that someone you look after? Sorry, hello, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, a school, right, yes, I'm still here, dear, sorry. Now hang on, you said a name a moment ago, [PERSON_3], was it? Could you say that again for me? Only I don't think I caught it properly the first time, what with the kettle going. I did have a nephew once who went missing from school for a whole afternoon, turned out he was at the pictures, can you imagine. But no, I'm not sure that name is anyone I look after, so I might be the wrong number altogether.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, I'm so sorry, yes, it's [PERSON_3] -- that's the pupil's name, [PERSON_3], from [COMPANY_A]. And you may well be right that it's the wrong number, I'd hate to have bothered you for nothing. I did only want to be sure the child was safe, you see, that's all this is. Um, hello, are you still there?

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I'm still here, dear, I'm still here. Well, I think it's the wrong number, you see, because I don't look after any children, not now, they've all grown up and gone, I think it is the wrong number. It's just me here, just me and the kettle. But it's very good of you to ring round and check, I will say that, it's nice that somebody bothers. Was there anything else you needed, or did you just want to make sure about the, um, the little one?

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: No, no, nothing else, that was all I wanted, just to be sure the little one was safe, that's all. I'm so sorry to have troubled you, it's only that the number's on our file for [PERSON_3], so I thought -- well, I thought I'd check. Hello? Are you still there? It's only that if it is the wrong number, I'd best look at our records again, and I'd hate to leave you worrying.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, no, I'm not worrying, dear, don't you fret about me. It's just, well, it's funny that my number would be on your file, isn't it? I've had this number donkey's years. Maybe somebody wrote it down wrong, they do that, don't they, a seven looks like a one. Yes, I'd have another look at your records if I were you, and I hope the little one turns up safe. And thank you for ringing, it was nice to hear a voice, it really was. Right, I'll let you get on. Goodbye now, dear.

utterances.speaker: caller
utterances.text: Oh, yes, thank you, I'll do that, I'll check the number against our records -- sorry, one second, there's someone at my door, I'm just -- no, it's fine, they've gone. Sorry. Um, you've been very kind, and if you'd rather, you can always ring the school office yourself on the number from the school's own website or the phone book, that way you know it's us. I'm quite happy for you to do that. Hello, are you still there? Goodbye then, dear, and sorry again for the bother.

utterances.speaker: receiver
utterances.text: Oh, that's very kind of you, dear, but I don't think I'll need to ring anyone, since it's only the wrong number, isn't it? Though it's good to know, about the phone book. I haven't looked in mine for years, I wonder where it's got to. Anyway, no bother at all, no bother. You look after yourself, and I do hope the little one's turned up. Goodbye now, dear.
